chapters.title: Chapter 1910 - 1%
paragraphs: Max closed his eyes and entered a calm meditative state.

Then something changed inside him. At first, it was only a faint point of light in the depths of Max’s body. Then another appeared. Then another. One by one, countless specks of light began shining across his body like stars appearing in a dark sky.

It was beautiful, too beautiful for a battlefield. His body did not burn with ordinary aura, and it did not release bloodline pressure. It did not erupt with lightning, flame, dragon scales, divine veins, or sword force.

Instead, he began to shine like a night sky filled with distant stars. The light was dark, deep, and vast, and every star within it seemed to contain a separate distance, a separate direction, and a separate space folded beyond imagination.
Revona’s eyes sharpened as the Null Origin Tide touched the starlight. Nothing happened.

The pale-gray nullifying wave flowed over Max’s body, trying to erase the new power, but the starlight did not dim. It did not resist in the normal sense, and it did not clash or push back. It simply existed on a scale that Revona’s nullifying force could not define properly.

Revona’s pupils contracted, and for the first time, horror appeared in her eyes. She could not nullify it. Her Void Origin Eyes could not trace its foundation, and the Null Origin Tide could not erase its structure.

Even Return To Nothing could not immediately identify what it was supposed to return to nothingness. It felt as though the power rising from Max did not belong to the same layer of existence as everything else she had erased.
Max released a small breath. The breath sounded soft, but as it left his lips, the entire Devouring Flames Domain became still.
’Finally, I can tap into this power again even if this percentage of power was only 1% of what I previously tapped into.’
A memory passed through Max’s mind.
Orion. The hidden temporal link. The legacy of the Dimensional Keeper.

Back then, through that strange connection between himself and the last user of the Dimensional Keeper legacy, Max had briefly tapped into the legacy of the Dimensional Keeper that should have been far beyond his current self.
Since then, he had spent what felt like thousands of years in accumulated comprehension, trial, and repeated failure, trying to touch that same state again.

Most attempts had failed, and some had barely succeeded for a breath. But now, under the pressure of Revona’s Null Origin Tide, with all external powers stripped away, the deepest part of the Dimensional Keeper legacy finally answered him again.

The starlight in Max’s body deepened. It no longer looked like ordinary stars. It looked like countless dimensions shining in a dark sky. Each point of light felt like a sealed world, and each faint glow carried the weight of distance, space, time, and existence itself.
This was not the power of his Divine Veins. Not the power of his black flames. Not the power of his lightning. Not the power of his draconic essences.
This was the Dimensional Keeper legacy, a power that did not simply use space but kept dimensions, scaled far beyond the level Revona’s current nullification could fully erase.
Max raised Dragonheart. The Emotion Severing Path around the sword, which had almost gone dull, suddenly brightened with cold and terrifying clarity.

The starlight from the Dimensional Keeper legacy flowed into the blade, not as ordinary energy but as a vast dimensional authority that gave the severing edge a foundation Revona’s eyes could no longer understand.

Revona reacted instantly. The Null Origin Tide surged, and Return To Nothing condensed before her once again. She poured everything into both attacks. The pale-gray wave rushed toward Max from all directions, nullifying the remaining black flames completely, and the weakened but still terrifying Return To Nothing formed at the center of the tide.
Together they became the strongest defense and attack Revona could release in that instant.
Max stepped forward. The starlight around his body made every step look as if he was crossing different layers of space. He raised Dragonheart above his head, then slashed down.
"Emotion Severing Sword."
The sword descended. There was no thunderous roar at first, only a single beautiful line of dark starlight and cold severing force. Then everything in its path split.

The Null Origin Tide was cut open. The massive domain-like wave that had erased Max’s divine veins, dragon essences, black flames, lightning, dragon scales, and time distortion was severed from its own nullifying foundation, and the pale-gray tide split apart like a curtain before Dragonheart.

Return To Nothing followed. Revona’s strongest technique, already gathered again at the center of the wave, tried to drag the sword strike back into origin emptiness. But this time, the severing force was powered by the Dimensional Keeper legacy.

The sword edge did not remain only in the present space where Revona’s eyes could trace it. It seemed to cut from several dimensions at once, passing through direction, distance, timing, and meaning before Revona could fully lock onto one layer.
The Return To Nothing trembled. Then it split, fully. The origin emptiness was cut apart from its core.

Revona’s eyes widened. For the first time, she could not understand what had happened fast enough. The sword light had already passed. The Null Origin Tide collapsed, Return To Nothing shattered, and the Devouring Flames Domain, which had nearly vanished, was blown apart by the aftermath of the strike.
The black flames opened, and the outside world finally saw the stage again. But by the time the spectators could understand what they were seeing, Max was already standing beside Revona.
Dragonheart rested against her neck. The blade did not cut her skin, but it was there. Still. Absolute.
Revona stood frozen in place. Her pale eyes were wide, the Void Origin Realm behind her was gone, and the remaining traces of Return To Nothing scattered into fading ash-like emptiness around her.
Blood slipped from the corner of her mouth, but she did not seem to notice it. Her entire attention remained on Max and on the sword touching her neck.
The whole Divine Realm fell silent. No one had seen the full battle inside the domain, but they had seen the final moment.

They had seen a dark star-like radiance split open the dying black flames, a sword line cut through the last wave of Revona’s nullification, and Max appear beside her before anyone could follow his movement.
Revona slowly turned her eyes toward him.
"What was that power?"
Max’s starlight slowly faded. His body looked exhausted now, truly exhausted, but his hand remained steady around Dragonheart.
"A power I have not fully mastered yet."
Revona stared at him for a long moment. Then she closed her eyes, and her voice came very soft.
"I lose."
Angelina Valerius’s voice descended over the silent arena.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Revona Defeated.]
The screen above the stage updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 22]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 21]
For one breath, no one moved. Then the Divine Realm erupted with a roar that seemed capable of shaking every ancient land beneath the heavens.

chapters.title: Chapter 1911: Damian vs Ervin!
paragraphs: The roar caused by Max Morgan’s victory over Revona did not fade quickly.

Even after the transfer light carried both of them back to their pillars, the Divine Realm remained trapped in the shock of what had just happened. Revona had been the first of the undefeated four to fall, but she had not fallen cheaply.

She had forced Max to reveal more power than anyone else in the entire Cosmic Ascension Conference, including the Devouring Flames Domain, Divine King Punishment, his four Divine Veins, the full release of 5000 Draconic Essences, the Dragon Scales Transformation, the strange time power connected to his clone, and finally that mysterious star-like legacy power that even Revona’s nullification could not fully erase.

No one could treat her defeat as weakness. If anything, the battle had proved that Revona’s strength was terrifying enough to push Max into revealing a depth that had been hidden even after all his previous victories.
But the final stretch did not stop. Angelina Valerius waited until the golden laws of the Eternal Hourglass restored the stage again.

The black flames vanished completely, the cracked ground became smooth, and the residual aura of nullification, lightning, draconic pressure, and dimensional starlight faded from the arena one by one. Only after the battlefield returned to its original state did she raise her hand again.
"The second battle among the remaining undefeated participants will now be selected."
The giant screen above the arena changed once more. Only three undefeated names remained shining at the top.
[Max Morgan]
[Ervin]
[Damian Voss]
Revona’s name had not disappeared, but it had moved slightly below them now.
[Revona]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 21]
The sight alone caused countless spectators to inhale deeply. One monster had fallen, and three remained.
The names spun again. Max Morgan. Ervin. Damian Voss. The light moved faster and faster, and the entire Divine Realm grew quiet once more.
After watching Max and Revona’s battle, no one thought their hearts could withstand another immediate peak collision, but the Eternal Hourglass clearly had no intention of showing mercy.
The first name stopped.
[Damian Voss]
The Sword God Palace disciples immediately straightened. The second name continued rotating. It passed Max Morgan. Then it stopped.
[Ervin]
The screen enlarged.
[Final Undefeated Battle]
[Damian Voss vs Ervin]

The entire Divine Realm erupted again. Sword Sovereign Heaven stood against Abyssal Origin Descent, the strongest genius of the Sword God Palace against the most mysterious spear genius of the conference.

One had cut through divine light, war body power, curses, dawn authority, and even Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth. The other had swallowed star power, heavenly luminance, curse authority, void-space corridors, and nearly everything that had entered the range of his abyss.

This battle carried a different kind of pressure from Max against Revona. Max and Revona’s battle had been a clash between overwhelming layered power and absolute nullification, while Damian and Ervin’s battle felt like a confrontation between two ancient paths that should never have been placed in the same world, a sword that ruled all blades against an abyss that returned all things to depth.
On his pillar, Damian Voss slowly opened his eyes. His expression remained calm, but his sword intent had already begun to rise.

Ervin also stood quietly. His black spear rested in his hand, and his gaze was as deep as a sea with no bottom. He did not speak, but the faint shadow of the broken gate behind him seemed to stir even before he moved.
Rakan Thorne crossed his arms, his grin returning.
"This one will not be clean."
Orion Starfall leaned forward.
"No. Both of them are too dangerous for that."
Kaiden Voidmere looked at Ervin with a serious gaze.
"If Damian’s sword cuts the gate before it opens deep enough, Damian wins."
Morgana Starveil said softly, "And if the abyss swallows the sword rhythm before the final edict descends, Ervin wins. Though I am not sure how Ervin’s path works."
Revona sat quietly on her pillar, still pale from the previous battle, but her eyes had not lost their sharpness.

Max stood silently and watched. He had fought Ervin before and had seen the strange depth of Abyssal Origin Descent, and he had also seen Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven cut through concepts that most people could not even touch.
This battle was not one where either side could hold back and slowly test each other. If either Damian or Ervin tried to begin cautiously, the other would seize the rhythm and crush them immediately.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both participants.
"Damian Voss."
"Ervin."
"Enter the stage."

Two beams of light descended. Damian appeared on one side of the central arena, sword in hand, his robes moving softly around him. Ervin appeared opposite him, black spear lowered, his shadow stretching strangely behind him.
For a few breaths, neither moved. Then Damian spoke first.
"You have not shown everything."
Ervin’s voice was calm. "Neither have you."
Damian’s hand tightened around his sword. "Then we should not waste time."
Ervin raised his spear slightly. "Agreed."
Angelina Valerius lowered her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
The moment the words appeared, both of them released their Pseudo Cosmic Paths. There was no probing strike, no opening exchange, and no cautious movement.

Damian’s sword rose, and the sky behind him split into a vast sword world. Sword-edge mountains appeared, rivers of sword light flowed through the air, an ancient sword altar stood at the center, and high above it a silent palace appeared around an empty throne.
A single sword hung before that throne, radiating a pressure that made every weapon in the audience tremble.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven."

At the same time, Ervin planted his black spear into the ground. The stage beneath him darkened, and a black sea rose from nowhere, silent and endless, spreading beneath his feet until the entire arena seemed to stand above an abyssal ocean.

Ancient waves rolled without sound. In the distance, a broken gate emerged from the depths, half submerged, enormous, ancient, and covered in unreadable symbols. The moment it appeared, the light of Damian’s sword world dimmed slightly near the edges.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."
Boom!

The two Pseudo Cosmic Paths collided before their masters even moved. Sword light pressed downward while abyssal depth rose upward, and the center of the arena became divided between a silver-white sword heaven and a bottomless black sea.
The stage cracked from the pressure, and the Eternal Hourglass barrier brightened instantly as golden laws poured around the battlefield.
Damian moved first.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, First Edict, All Blades Refuse Submission."

Countless sword lights descended from the sword heaven, not as random attacks but as edicts of submission. Every sword line carried authority that forced weapons, techniques, and killing intent to lower themselves before Damian’s blade.

chapters.title: Chapter 1912: An Intense Battle!
paragraphs: Ervin raised his spear.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, First Depth Tide."

The black sea rose in a towering wave of abyssal water that met the falling sword lights. The sword edict cut through the first layer, then the second, then the third, but each time the sword light continued deeper, the abyss swallowed part of its sharpness.
The first wave split apart, though the sword lights that passed through it had already dimmed by half.
Ervin stepped forward.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Thrust."

His spear pierced out, and a black current followed the spear tip, moving not across the surface of the stage but beneath the sword heaven’s pressure, as though it wanted to attack from the depth beneath Damian’s own footing.
Damian’s eyes shifted.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Second Edict, One Sword Divides Heaven."
A single sword light descended and split the incoming current apart, but Ervin had already vanished into the shadow of the black wave. He appeared to Damian’s left and thrust again.
"Abyss Spear Art, Gate Shadow Thrust."
The spear carried the shadow of the broken gate. Damian turned his sword sideways.
"White Horizon Guard."
Clang!
The spear struck the sword, and the impact forced both of them back half a step. Only half a step, but that was enough to make the entire arena erupt.
"They are equal in the first collision!"
"Damian’s sword cut the abyssal tide, but Ervin’s depth weakened the sword edict!"
"This will be close!"
Damian did not give Ervin time to expand the abyss freely. His sword moved again.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Third Edict, Blade Meets The Depth."

A massive sword shadow descended from above, aiming directly at the black sea beneath Ervin. It did not target Ervin’s body. It targeted the connection between Abyssal Origin Descent and the battlefield, as if Damian wanted to cut the sea itself apart before it could deepen.
Ervin’s gaze became colder.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth."

The broken gate opened slightly, and a deep, ancient pressure surged from beyond it. The descending sword shadow struck the sea, but the moment the Gate of the First Depth opened, the black water rose in a circular spiral and wrapped around the sword shadow like a hungry vortex.
The sword continued cutting while the abyss continued pulling, one wanting to divide and the other wanting to sink.
The clash lasted three breaths. Then both powers exploded.

Damian slid back several steps. Ervin also retreated, his spear leaving a long mark across the stage. Blood appeared at the corner of Ervin’s mouth, and a thin cut appeared across Damian’s sleeve. Both had been touched, and both had been forced.
Damian raised his sword again without changing expression.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Fourth Edict, Palace Sword Descends."

The palace above the sword altar brightened, and a palace-sized sword descended from the sky, carrying an oppressive sword authority that made countless swordsmen across the Divine Realm feel their hearts tremble.
This strike was not merely sharp. It felt like the judgment of the sword palace itself, as if all paths beneath it had to be split open.
Ervin looked up. The black sea beneath him became still, too still. Then the broken gate opened wider.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."

A whirlpool appeared beneath the descending palace sword. The enormous sword tried to cut through it, but the abyssal pull wrapped around it from all sides, dragging layers of sword authority downward. Sparks of silver-white sword light erupted across the sea surface while black waves rose and swallowed them again.
Damian stepped forward, strengthening the palace sword. Ervin also stepped forward, strengthening the abyssal whirlpool. For a terrifying moment, neither gave ground.

Then Damian changed the sword’s path. Instead of forcing the palace sword straight down, he tilted his blade, and the palace sword suddenly split into three sword shadows, each attacking from a different angle.
Ervin’s Return To Depth swallowed two, but the third cut through, and blood splashed from Ervin’s shoulder.
The Sword God Palace disciples roared.
But before they could celebrate, Ervin’s spear moved. He had allowed the third sword shadow to cut him in exchange for a path.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Reversal."
The abyssal current that had swallowed the first two sword shadows reversed violently, carrying fragments of Damian’s own sword authority back toward him.

Damian’s eyes narrowed, and his sword flashed three times. He cut apart the reversed current, but one fragment still passed through and struck his chest. His body slid backward, and a small line of blood appeared at his lips.
The arena became even more heated.
"They are both injured!"
"Ervin used Damian’s sword force against him!"
"Damian cut through Return To Depth, but Ervin turned the swallowed sword authority back!"
Max watched silently, his eyes deep.

This battle was exactly as dangerous as he expected. Damian’s sword was terrifying because it could cut the critical line behind any technique, while Ervin’s abyss was terrifying because anything that entered it could be swallowed, delayed, sunk, reversed, or returned through a deeper path.
It was not a simple matter of sword against spear. It was the clash between severance and depth.
Damian stepped forward again, his aura sharpening.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Fifth Edict, Sword Heart Cannot Be Drowned."

The sword before the throne vibrated faintly, and Damian’s entire body became covered in sword light. For the first time, the black sea beneath him failed to drag his sword intent downward. His sword heart stabilized itself above the abyss, refusing to sink, refusing to slow, and refusing to be swallowed.
Ervin’s expression became more serious. Damian vanished, and his sword appeared before Ervin’s throat. Ervin raised his spear and blocked.
Clang!
Damian struck again. Then again. Then again. Each sword attack was clean, deadly, and aimed at the weakest transition points in Ervin’s spear path.

Ervin defended with Hollow Moon Guard, Deep Current Reversal, and Gate Shadow Thrust, but Damian’s sword heart had become too stable, and the abyss could no longer swallow the outer rhythm of the sword as easily as before.

A cut appeared across Ervin’s arm, then another near his ribs, then a third along his thigh. But Ervin did not retreat. His black spear moved more slowly now, and deeper. He stopped trying to match Damian’s speed and began letting every sword strike fall closer before answering.
It looked dangerous, almost suicidal, but each time Damian’s sword approached, Ervin’s spear rose from a deeper angle, forcing Damian to adjust at the last instant.

Damian’s sword cut Ervin’s shoulder. Ervin’s spear grazed Damian’s waist. Damian’s sword pierced through Ervin’s defense. Ervin’s abyssal current struck Damian’s chest. Both of them were now bleeding, and neither gave ground.
Then Ervin opened the broken gate again.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Second Depth Pressure."

The entire black sea sank, not downward but deeper, and the pressure changed at once. The sword lights around Damian became slower, as though each slash now had to pass through layers of unseen depth before reaching Ervin.
Damian’s Sword Heart Cannot Be Drowned resisted the pressure, but even that edict could not completely ignore the Second Depth.
Damian’s gaze sharpened.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Sixth Edict, Bleeding Sword Severance."

He slashed his own palm across the blade, and blood touched the sword. The sword heaven changed again. The blade became crimson white, and the sharpness around Damian rose to a level that made even Ervin’s abyss tremble.
This was a sword edict fueled by Damian’s blood and sword heart together, used only when ordinary sword authority could no longer cut deep enough.

"Abyssal Origin Descent, First Depth Tide."
The black sea rose in a towering wave of abyssal water that met the falling sword lights.
The sword edict cut through the first layer, then the second, then the third, but each time the sword light continued deeper, the abyss swallowed part of its sharpness.
The first wave split apart, though the sword lights that passed through it had already dimmed by half.
Ervin stepped forward.

His spear pierced out, and a black current followed the spear tip, moving not across the surface of the stage but beneath the sword heaven’s pressure, as though it wanted to attack from the depth beneath Damian’s own footing.
Damian’s eyes shifted.

"Abyss Spear Art, Gate Shadow Thrust."

Damian turned his sword sideways.
"White Horizon Guard."

"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Third Edict, Blade Meets The Depth."
A massive sword shadow descended from above, aiming directly at the black sea beneath Ervin.
It did not target Ervin’s body.
It targeted the connection between Abyssal Origin Descent and the battlefield, as if Damian wanted to cut the sea itself apart before it could deepen.
Ervin’s gaze became colder.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth."
The broken gate opened slightly, and a deep, ancient pressure surged from beyond it.
The descending sword shadow struck the sea, but the moment the Gate of the First Depth opened, the black water rose in a circular spiral and wrapped around the sword shadow like a hungry vortex.
The sword continued cutting while the abyss continued pulling, one wanting to divide and the other wanting to sink.
The clash lasted three breaths.
Then both powers exploded.
Damian slid back several steps.
Ervin also retreated, his spear leaving a long mark across the stage.
Blood appeared at the corner of Ervin’s mouth, and a thin cut appeared across Damian’s sleeve.
Both had been touched, and both had been forced.
Damian raised his sword again without changing expression.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Fourth Edict, Palace Sword Descends."

The palace above the sword altar brightened, and a palace-sized sword descended from the sky, carrying an oppressive sword authority that made countless swordsmen across the Divine Realm feel their hearts tremble.
This strike was not merely sharp.
It felt like the judgment of the sword palace itself, as if all paths beneath it had to be split open.
Ervin looked up.
The black sea beneath him became still, too still.
Then the broken gate opened wider.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
A whirlpool appeared beneath the descending palace sword.

Sparks of silver-white sword light erupted across the sea surface while black waves rose and swallowed them again.
Damian stepped forward, strengthening the palace sword.
Ervin also stepped forward, strengthening the abyssal whirlpool.

The abyssal current that had swallowed the first two sword shadows reversed violently, carrying fragments of Damian’s own sword authority back toward him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1913: The Remaining Battles!
paragraphs: Damian attacked with a single sword, and the Second Depth Pressure split apart. A wound opened across Ervin’s chest, and he retreated several steps, blood falling onto the black sea beneath his feet.
The Sword God Palace disciples shouted with wild excitement.
But Ervin looked down at the wound, then raised his eyes. The broken gate behind him opened a little more.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."
His voice was still calm.
"Gate of the Second Depth."
Boom!

The gate opened, and a darkness deeper than the black sea appeared beyond it. The entire arena trembled. Damian’s Bleeding Sword Severance pressed forward, but the moment the Gate of the Second Depth opened, the abyss stopped retreating.
The black sea rose in a terrifying column behind Ervin, and a pressure far heavier than before descended onto Damian’s sword heaven.
The sword palace shook. The sword altar trembled. Even the empty throne above the sword heaven seemed to be pulled downward by the depth beyond the gate.
Ervin raised his spear.
"Second Depth Spear."
The abyssal sea gathered around the spear tip.
"Sunken World."
The spear thrust out, and a whole world seemed to sink behind that thrust.
Damian raised his sword with both hands.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven, Final Edict."
The single sword before the empty throne descended.
"Throne Of The Only Sword."
All sword lights vanished. The mountains of sword edges faded, the rivers of sword light disappeared, and the palace dimmed. Only Damian’s sword remained. One sword, one will, and one throne.
The entire Divine Realm stopped breathing.
Damian slashed. Ervin thrust. Throne Of The Only Sword met Sunken World.
The collision did not explode immediately. For one breath, the whole arena became still. Then the stage shattered.

Golden laws surged madly around the barrier as sword authority and abyssal depth tore through the center of the battlefield. Damian’s sword cut into the sinking world, splitting layer after layer of abyssal pressure.

Ervin’s spear pushed forward, forcing the sword line deeper and deeper into darkness. Every inch of the clash felt like a decision between two possible endings. If Damian’s sword cut one layer further, Ervin would fall, and if Ervin’s abyss sank the sword one breath longer, Damian would lose.

Both of them poured everything into the clash. Damian’s hand bled along the sword hilt, and Ervin’s chest wound tore open further. The broken gate behind Ervin groaned, and the empty throne behind Damian trembled. Neither retreated.
Crack!
The sword line cut through Sunken World, and the abyssal spear shadow split apart.
The Sword God Palace erupted in joy.
But Ervin did not stop. His eyes became deeper than ever before.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."
The broken gate behind him opened to its widest point yet.
"Second Depth Spear."
His voice was quiet, but it carried through the entire arena.
"Abyss Returns All Roads."
The shattered Sunken World did not disappear. It returned, not as the same attack but as countless fragments of abyssal route gathering behind Damian’s sword line.

The paths Damian had already cut became roads leading back toward him, each one carrying a remnant of Ervin’s depth. Damian’s Final Edict had cut through the direct attack, but Ervin had hidden his last move inside the broken routes left behind by the clash itself.
Damian’s eyes changed. He realized it a fraction too late. He turned his sword, and the Throne Of The Only Sword cut backward, severing most of the returning abyssal roads.
But not all. One road remained, a narrow black path no wider than a spear tip that slipped through the edge of the sword’s final arc and appeared before Damian’s chest.

Ervin appeared at the end of that road. His spear stopped against Damian’s heart. At the same time, Damian’s sword stopped at Ervin’s throat. Both weapons reached their targets, but Ervin’s spear was one breath closer. One tiny margin. One impossible fraction.
The entire arena froze. Blood dripped from Damian’s lips, and blood also fell from Ervin’s throat where Damian’s sword edge had barely touched the skin. Neither moved.
For several breaths, the whole Divine Realm remained silent. Then Damian looked down at the spear touching his chest. His expression remained calm. After a long moment, he lowered his sword.
"I lost."
The words were quiet, but they shook the entire Divine Realm.
Angelina Valerius announced the result immediately.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Damian Voss Defeated.]
The screen above the arena updated.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Ervin]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 22]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Damian Voss]
[Total Battles Fought: 22]
[Total Wins: 21]

For a breath, the Sword God Palace was completely silent. Then even there, many disciples slowly clenched their fists, not in shame but in pain and respect. Damian had not been crushed, and he had not been overwhelmed.
He had pushed Ervin to the very brink, forced him to open the Gate of the Second Depth wider than before, and nearly ended the battle with Throne Of The Only Sword.
The difference between victory and defeat had been so small that countless spectators were still unsure whether they had seen it clearly.
At the hidden forces watching Ervin, the silence was even heavier. Ervin had won, but his victory had come by the smallest possible margin.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Damian sheathed his sword slowly. Ervin lowered his spear. For the first time, a faint trace of exhaustion appeared on Ervin’s face.
Damian looked at him and said, "You won."
Ervin replied calmly, "Your final sword attack was also very strong."
Damian nodded once. "I know but it wasn’t strong enough."
Ervin gave a slight nod.
The transfer light descended and returned both of them to their pillars.
The second undefeated record had been broken.
Damian Voss had fallen, and only two participants still stood undefeated, Max Morgan and Ervin.
However, the moment the Divine Realm erupted into discussion about the final champion being decided between those two, Angelina Valerius raised her hand once again.

Her calm gesture immediately pressed down upon the chaotic noise spreading through the Eternal Hourglass, and the great screen above the arena shifted from the battle result to the complete ranking rules of the final competitive stage.
"The winner of the Cosmic Ascension Conference will not be decided by one undefeated pairing alone," Angelina said, her voice clear and steady. "This stage is still based on total victories."
The crowd quieted. The defeated geniuses on the pillars also looked toward her.

Angelina continued, "Max Morgan and Ervin remain undefeated, but several important battles among the top four have not yet taken place. Those battles will still affect the final number of victories, the ranking order beneath the champion, and the possibility of equal records."
The four names appeared once again.
[Max Morgan]
[Ervin]
[Revona]
[Damian Voss]
Then the remaining matchups appeared beneath them.
[Ervin vs Revona]
[Max Morgan vs Damian Voss]
[Damian Voss vs Revona]
[Max Morgan vs Ervin]
The moment those four matchups appeared, the entire Divine Realm became heated again.

Angelina looked over the arena and said, "Ervin must still face Revona. Max Morgan must still face Damian Voss. Damian Voss and Revona must also battle each other. After those battles, Max Morgan and Ervin will have their final confrontation."
The great screen flashed with golden light.
"After all remaining battles are completed, the participant with the highest total number of wins will become the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference."

chapters.title: Chapter 1914: Ervin vs Revona!
paragraphs: The explanation caused the atmosphere to become even heavier. Damian’s loss did not make him irrelevant, and Revona’s loss did not remove her from the stage’s importance.
Ervin still needed to prove whether his abyss could swallow Revona’s nullification, and Max still had to face Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven before reaching Ervin.
This also meant that the final battle between Max and Ervin would become even more terrifying, since every prior result would sharpen the pressure surrounding it.
Rakan Thorne grinned from his pillar.
"Good. They still have to fight everyone properly."
Orion Starfall laughed softly.
"That is fair. A round-robin should not let anyone escape a monster just because another monster fell first."
Kaiden Voidmere looked at the projected matchups.
"Ervin against Revona will be difficult. Damian against Max may be even worse."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly.
"And Damian against Revona will decide which of the fallen undefeated monsters stands higher."

Damian Voss stood silently on his pillar, his expression calm despite his recent defeat. His sword had lost to Ervin by the smallest margin, but his battle intent had not weakened, and when his gaze moved toward Max, the sword intent around him became colder and more refined.

Revona sat with her eyes half-closed, still recovering from her terrifying battle against Max. She had lost, but no one doubted her strength. If anything, everyone now looked at her with even deeper fear, because they had seen how far she had pushed Max before falling.
Ervin stood quietly with his black spear in hand. Max also stood calmly, Dragonheart resting at his waist.

The two undefeated participants had not yet faced each other, but the path toward their final battle was now clear. Before Max and Ervin could decide the crown, the remaining top-four battles had to burn through the stage.
The Cosmic Ascension Conference had not ended. It had entered its most dangerous stretch.
Angelina Valerius allowed the explanation to settle across the Eternal Hourglass.
The four remaining top matchups shone above the arena, each one heavy enough to decide not only records but pride, reputation, and the final shape of the Cosmic Ascension Conference.

Even after Max Morgan defeated Revona and Ervin defeated Damian, nothing had become simple. If anything, the path to the championship had become even more intense, because every remaining battle among the top four now carried the weight of the entire Divine Realm’s attention.
The giant screen shifted again.
[Remaining Top Four Battles]
[Ervin vs Revona]
[Max Morgan vs Damian Voss]
[Damian Voss vs Revona]
[Max Morgan vs Ervin]
The names remained there for several breaths. Then Angelina raised her hand.
"The next battle will now be selected."
The golden light around the screen spun once, then twice, before the first matchup brightened.
[Ervin vs Revona]
The moment those two names shone, the entire arena fell into a deep silence. Then the Divine Realm erupted.

Abyssal Origin Descent stood against Void Origin Realm, the broken gate against the Void Origin Eyes, an abyss that swallowed everything into unfathomable depth against a pair of eyes that erased, nullified, hollowed, and returned power to nothing.
This was not a battle of simple force. This was a battle between two terrifying paths that both denied the enemy in completely different ways. Ervin’s abyss did not merely block attacks.
It sank them, swallowed them, redirected them, and dragged their meaning into the depth behind the broken gate.
Revona’s void did not merely defend. It traced the source of power, erased its structure, nullified its authority, and returned it to nothingness before it could complete its purpose.
Across the Divine Realm, countless spectators began speaking at once.
"Ervin defeated Damian by the smallest margin."
"But Revona pushed Max further than anyone."
"Can the abyss swallow Void Origin Realm?"
"Can the Void Origin Eyes erase the broken gate?"
"Return To Nothing against Gate of the Second Depth. This might be even stranger than Damian and Ervin’s battle."
On the pillars, the defeated geniuses also became serious.
Rakan Thorne crossed his arms and grinned.
"This one will be annoying to watch, but terrifying."
Orion Starfall smiled faintly, though there was rare seriousness in his eyes.
"Revona already fought Max, so she is not in perfect condition. But Ervin just fought Damian to the limit too. Neither one is fresh."
Kaiden Voidmere looked toward Ervin’s black spear, then toward Revona’s pale eyes.
"That makes it more dangerous. When people like them are exhausted, they stop wasting power and go straight for decisive moves."
Morgana Starveil’s purple eyes reflected the names above.
"Depth against nothingness. I wonder which one can deny the other more completely."

Damian Voss stood quietly on his pillar, his gaze fixed on Ervin. He had just lost to that abyss by a margin so thin that even the spectators had almost failed to recognize it, but there was no resentment in his eyes.
Only focus, only respect, and only the cold awareness that the man who had beaten his sword now had to face an opponent whose ability could erase even the foundation of attacks.
Max Morgan also watched silently. He had faced Revona and knew better than anyone here how terrifying her fully awakened Void Origin Eyes were.

He had been forced to reveal layers of power he had kept hidden for the entire conference, and even then, Revona’s Null Origin Tide had almost stripped him bare before the Dimensional Keeper legacy answered him.

But he had also faced Ervin before, and he knew that Abyssal Origin Descent was not an ordinary Pseudo Cosmic Path. It did not behave like darkness, and it did not behave like water. It was depth, return, and an ancient gate to something far more profound.
This battle would not be easy for either side.
On one pillar, Ervin slowly stood. His expression remained calm, but his face was paler than before. The battle against Damian had clearly cost him.
The Gate of the Second Depth had opened wider than ever, and even though the Eternal Hourglass was healing him, the exhaustion of pushing his abyss that far could not disappear instantly.
On another pillar, Revona also opened her eyes. She was still pale from her battle against Max, her aura thinner, and the faint emptiness in her gaze no longer looked as effortless as before.
Yet when her Void Origin Eyes fully opened, the surrounding space still seemed to quiet down, as if even the laws of the Eternal Hourglass had to acknowledge the danger in her sight.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both of them.
"Ervin."
"Revona."
"Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.

Ervin appeared on one side of the central arena with his black spear in hand, his long shadow spreading beneath him like a silent sea. Revona appeared opposite him, calm and pale, her Void Origin Eyes fixed directly on the man who had defeated Damian Voss.
For a brief moment, neither of them spoke. Then Ervin lifted his spear slightly.
"Your eyes are very troublesome. I don’t know how Max was able to bypass them"
Revona replied quietly, "Your abyss gates are also troublesome too and so I think it will be a good battle."
Ervin’s gaze deepened. "Then we should not delay."
Revona’s eyes shone with faint emptiness. "No. We should not."
Above them, the giant screen flashed.
[Top Four Battle]
[Ervin vs Revona]
The Eternal Hourglass barrier brightened. The entire Divine Realm leaned closer.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
The next battle was about to begin.

sentences.text: The explanation caused the atmosphere to become even heavier.
Damian’s loss did not make him irrelevant, and Revona’s loss did not remove her from the stage’s importance.
Ervin still needed to prove whether his abyss could swallow Revona’s nullification, and Max still had to face Damian’s Sword Sovereign Heaven before reaching Ervin.
This also meant that the final battle between Max and Ervin would become even more terrifying, since every prior result would sharpen the pressure surrounding it.
Rakan Thorne grinned from his pillar.
"Good.
They still have to fight everyone properly."
Orion Starfall laughed softly.
"That is fair.
A round-robin should not let anyone escape a monster just because another monster fell first."
Kaiden Voidmere looked at the projected matchups.
"Ervin against Revona will be difficult.
Damian against Max may be even worse."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly.
"And Damian against Revona will decide which of the fallen undefeated monsters stands higher."
Damian Voss stood silently on his pillar, his expression calm despite his recent defeat.
His sword had lost to Ervin by the smallest margin, but his battle intent had not weakened, and when his gaze moved toward Max, the sword intent around him became colder and more refined.
Revona sat with her eyes half-closed, still recovering from her terrifying battle against Max.
She had lost, but no one doubted her strength.
If anything, everyone now looked at her with even deeper fear, because they had seen how far she had pushed Max before falling.
Ervin stood quietly with his black spear in hand.
Max also stood calmly, Dragonheart resting at his waist.
The two undefeated participants had not yet faced each other, but the path toward their final battle was now clear.
Before Max and Ervin could decide the crown, the remaining top-four battles had to burn through the stage.
The Cosmic Ascension Conference had not ended.
It had entered its most dangerous stretch.
Angelina Valerius allowed the explanation to settle across the Eternal Hourglass.
The four remaining top matchups shone above the arena, each one heavy enough to decide not only records but pride, reputation, and the final shape of the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Even after Max Morgan defeated Revona and Ervin defeated Damian, nothing had become simple.
If anything, the path to the championship had become even more intense, because every remaining battle among the top four now carried the weight of the entire Divine Realm’s attention.
The giant screen shifted again.
[Remaining Top Four Battles]
[Ervin vs Revona]
[Max Morgan vs Damian Voss]
[Damian Voss vs Revona]
[Max Morgan vs Ervin]
The names remained there for several breaths.
Then Angelina raised her hand.
"The next battle will now be selected."
The golden light around the screen spun once, then twice, before the first matchup brightened.
[Ervin vs Revona]
The moment those two names shone, the entire arena fell into a deep silence.
Then the Divine Realm erupted.

Abyssal Origin Descent stood against Void Origin Realm, the broken gate against the Void Origin Eyes, an abyss that swallowed everything into unfathomable depth against a pair of eyes that erased, nullified, hollowed, and returned power to nothing.
This was not a battle of simple force.
This was a battle between two terrifying paths that both denied the enemy in completely different ways.
Ervin’s abyss did not merely block attacks.
It sank them, swallowed them, redirected them, and dragged their meaning into the depth behind the broken gate.
Revona’s void did not merely defend.
It traced the source of power, erased its structure, nullified its authority, and returned it to nothingness before it could complete its purpose.
Across the Divine Realm, countless spectators began speaking at once.
"Ervin defeated Damian by the smallest margin."
"But Revona pushed Max further than anyone."
"Can the abyss swallow Void Origin Realm?"
"Can the Void Origin Eyes erase the broken gate?"
"Return To Nothing against Gate of the Second Depth.
This might be even stranger than Damian and Ervin’s battle."
On the pillars, the defeated geniuses also became serious.
Rakan Thorne crossed his arms and grinned.
"This one will be annoying to watch, but terrifying."
Orion Starfall smiled faintly, though there was rare seriousness in his eyes.
"Revona already fought Max, so she is not in perfect condition.
But Ervin just fought Damian to the limit too.
Neither one is fresh."
Kaiden Voidmere looked toward Ervin’s black spear, then toward Revona’s pale eyes.
"That makes it more dangerous.
When people like them are exhausted, they stop wasting power and go straight for decisive moves."
Morgana Starveil’s purple eyes reflected the names above.
"Depth against nothingness.
I wonder which one can deny the other more completely."
Damian Voss stood quietly on his pillar, his gaze fixed on Ervin.
He had just lost to that abyss by a margin so thin that even the spectators had almost failed to recognize it, but there was no resentment in his eyes.
Only focus, only respect, and only the cold awareness that the man who had beaten his sword now had to face an opponent whose ability could erase even the foundation of attacks.
Max Morgan also watched silently.
He had faced Revona and knew better than anyone here how terrifying her fully awakened Void Origin Eyes were.

He had been forced to reveal layers of power he had kept hidden for the entire conference, and even then, Revona’s Null Origin Tide had almost stripped him bare before the Dimensional Keeper legacy answered him.
But he had also faced Ervin before, and he knew that Abyssal Origin Descent was not an ordinary Pseudo Cosmic Path.
It did not behave like darkness, and it did not behave like water.
It was depth, return, and an ancient gate to something far more profound.
This battle would not be easy for either side.
On one pillar, Ervin slowly stood.
His expression remained calm, but his face was paler than before.
The battle against Damian had clearly cost him.
The Gate of the Second Depth had opened wider than ever, and even though the Eternal Hourglass was healing him, the exhaustion of pushing his abyss that far could not disappear instantly.
On another pillar, Revona also opened her eyes.
She was still pale from her battle against Max, her aura thinner, and the faint emptiness in her gaze no longer looked as effortless as before.
Yet when her Void Origin Eyes fully opened, the surrounding space still seemed to quiet down, as if even the laws of the Eternal Hourglass had to acknowledge the danger in her sight.

"Your eyes are very troublesome.

"Then we should not delay."
Revona’s eyes shone with faint emptiness.
"No.
We should not."
Above them, the giant screen flashed.

The entire Divine Realm leaned closer.

chapters.title: Chapter 1915: An Epic Clash!
paragraphs: Angelina Valerius lowered her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
The moment the words appeared, Ervin and Revona moved at the same time. There was no testing and no polite first exchange.
Both of them had already fought enough battles to understand that holding back in this final stretch was meaningless.

Ervin had just defeated Damian Voss by the smallest possible margin, but that victory had come at a terrifying price. His aura was still unstable, and the shadow of the Gate of the Second Depth behind him had not fully settled.

Revona had already been defeated by Max Morgan after forcing him to reveal layers of strength that shook the Divine Realm, but she had also paid a heavy cost. Her Void Origin Eyes were still sharp, yet the faint paleness of her face proved that her battle with Max had not been easy.
Even so, neither of them hesitated.
Ervin planted his black spear into the stage.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."

The black sea rose, and the broken gate emerged from the abyss, ancient, silent, and terrifying, its unreadable symbols flickering with a darkness that seemed older than the arena itself. The moment the gate appeared, the air around Ervin sank.
The stage no longer felt like solid ground. It felt like a surface floating above endless depth, and anything that stepped too close to him risked being dragged below.
Revona’s eyes opened fully.
"Void Origin Realm."
The world behind her became hollow, without color, sound, or warmth. Only origin-level emptiness spread silently behind her like a pale-gray world that denied all things.
The Void Origin Eyes shone within that emptiness, calmly watching the black sea, the broken gate, the spear in Ervin’s hand, and even the faint abyssal currents moving beneath the stage.
The two Pseudo Cosmic Paths collided before their masters physically exchanged a single blow. Abyss rose upward while void pressed downward.

The black sea tried to swallow the hollow realm into its depths, while the Void Origin Realm tried to erase the structure that allowed the abyss to exist on the battlefield. The center of the arena twisted between sinking darkness and pale emptiness, and the Eternal Hourglass barrier brightened instantly as golden laws poured around the stage.
Ervin raised his spear.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, First Depth Tide."
The black sea erupted forward in a great wave.
Revona lifted one hand.
"Void Origin Eyes."

The first layer of the tide vanished. The second layer hollowed. The third layer lost its direction and collapsed into pale-gray emptiness. But the wave was too deep to disappear completely. Beneath the erased surface, a hidden current continued moving, bending around the Void Origin Eyes’ field of sight and rushing toward Revona’s feet from below.
Revona’s eyes shifted.
"Void Origin Realm, Hollowing Wave."
The hidden current was erased the moment it touched the edge of her realm, but Ervin had already moved. His spear emerged from the shadow of the current.
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Thrust."
Revona turned her palm.
"Void Origin Palm."

Spear and palm collided. There was no loud explosion at first. The abyssal spear force tried to sink into her palm, while the hollow palm seal tried to erase the spear force from its root. The two powers trembled against each other, then burst apart in a ring of black water and pale-gray emptiness.
Ervin slid back half a step. Revona also retreated half a step.
The Divine Realm erupted immediately.
"They are equal at the start!"
"Revona erased part of the First Depth Tide, but Ervin hid a second current beneath it!"
"His abyss is not simple to nullify!"
"And her Void Origin Realm is not simple to swallow!"
Ervin did not slow down. He knew that if he allowed Revona’s eyes to calmly study his abyss, the battle would become more difficult with every breath.

He had seen what happened to Kaiden, and he had seen how Revona adapted to the Grand Void Labyrinth. He had also seen how even Max had needed to create multiple layers of power and hidden timing just to bypass her perception.
So Ervin attacked more fiercely than ever.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth."

The broken gate opened slightly, and a deeper pressure descended upon the stage. The black sea beneath Ervin became heavier, darker, and more ancient. He stepped forward, and the abyss moved with him.

His spear thrust out again and again, each strike carrying hidden currents, delayed depths, and sinking force that tried to drag Revona’s Void Origin Realm into a lower layer before her eyes could erase it.
"Abyss Spear Art, Hollow Descent Thrust."
"Abyss Spear Art, Gate Shadow Thrust."
"Abyss Spear Art, Deep Current Reversal."
Revona’s eyes moved calmly. One thrust vanished, and the shadow of the gate was hollowed. The reversed current was erased halfway, but the remaining half curved around her and struck her shoulder.
Blood appeared, and the arena stirred. Ervin had wounded her.
Revona looked at the blood on her shoulder, then back at Ervin. Her expression did not change, but the emptiness in her eyes deepened.
"Trace To Nothing."

The next abyssal current Ervin released did not merely disappear. Revona’s eyes followed it backward, tracing the route through the black sea until they found the deeper current that carried it. That hidden current collapsed, then another, then another. Several of Ervin’s concealed abyssal paths vanished inside the black sea itself.

Ervin’s gaze sharpened, and he immediately changed his rhythm. Instead of sending currents toward her, he let the black sea sink beneath the stage. For a breath, nothing attacked Revona. Then the ground below her disappeared.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."

A whirlpool opened beneath Revona’s feet, dragging her downward with frightening force. This was not a direct attack to be erased from the front. It was a pull from below, a sinking authority that tried to claim her position and return it to the abyss.
Revona’s Void Origin Realm expanded beneath her. The whirlpool hollowed, but it did not vanish fully. The depth continued pulling. Revona’s body sank half a step, then one full step.

Her eyes shone brighter as she erased the first layer of the whirlpool, then the second, then the third. But the Return To Depth technique kept rising from lower layers of the black sea, and for a brief moment, the entire Divine Realm saw Revona being dragged downward.
Ervin stepped forward and thrust his spear.
"Gate Shadow Thrust."
The spear tip arrived before her chest.
Revona’s eyes narrowed.
"Void Origin Realm, Silent Eye Field."

The emptiness around her gaze spread outward in a wide arc. The Gate Shadow Thrust dulled instantly, its killing intent erased before its spear force could fully arrive. At the same time, the Return To Depth whirlpool beneath her feet lost its deepest foundation and collapsed into nothingness.
Revona stepped out and struck forward with her palm.
"Void Origin Palm, Hollow Return."

Ervin raised his spear to block, but the palm seal did not attack the spear. It struck the abyssal support around his body instead. The black sea beneath him thinned, and the Gate of the First Depth trembled. Ervin was pushed back several steps, his expression turning more solemn.
Rakan Thorne watched with a tight grin.
"They are already hurting each other."
Orion Starfall’s eyes were bright.
"Ervin is attacking from depth. Revona is erasing from origin. Every clash is cutting away something fundamental."
Kaiden Voidmere looked grim.
"If this continues, whoever loses control of their Pseudo Cosmic Path first will lose."

Damian Voss watched Ervin quietly. He had just fought that abyss himself, so he knew how terrifying the Gate of the Second Depth was. Yet even he could see that Revona was forcing Ervin to spend more power than he wanted, since every route erased by her eyes made the black sea less stable.
Max stood silently, his gaze fixed on Revona. He knew what she still had not used, and he knew that if Ervin could not get past it, the battle would end exactly as she intended.
On the stage, Ervin took a slow breath. The black sea around him darkened again.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."
The broken gate opened wider.
"Gate of the Second Depth."
Boom!

The entire stage sank under invisible pressure, and Revona’s Void Origin Realm trembled. The second depth was not merely stronger than the first. It changed the nature of the abyss. The black sea no longer only swallowed attacks.
It made everything feel lower than itself, so sword light could sink, star power could sink, and spatial routes could sink. Even void emptiness seemed to gain weight under its pressure.

chapters.title: Chapter 1916: Too Strong!
paragraphs: Ervin raised his spear.
"Second Depth Spear."
The black sea climbed onto the spear like a world sinking into one point.
"Sunken World."
The spear thrust forward.
Revona’s eyes flashed.
"Void Origin Realm, Return To Nothing."
A condensed point of emptiness formed before her palm.

Sunken World crashed into Return To Nothing, and the stage vanished under the collision. The black sea tried to sink the point of nothingness into the Second Depth, while Return To Nothing tried to erase the world carried by the spear.
For several breaths, neither side moved. The entire arena seemed locked between two forms of denial. One returned everything to depth. The other returned everything to nothing.
Ervin’s arms trembled, and Revona’s face turned paler. Both were being pushed. The Gate of the Second Depth groaned behind Ervin, and the Void Origin Realm flickered behind Revona.
The pressure between them became so terrifying that golden laws from the Eternal Hourglass had to descend again and again to stabilize the barrier.
Then Ervin suddenly coughed blood, but his eyes did not waver. He stepped forward into the collision, and the black spear in his hand cracked faintly beneath the pressure.
"Abyssal Origin Descent."
His voice became deeper.
"Forbidden Depth Art."

The moment those words appeared, the expressions of several hidden experts across the Divine Realm changed. Behind Ervin, the broken gate opened beyond the safe limit, and the symbols on it bled black light.

His flesh tore open along his arms, shoulders, and chest, as if his own body could not withstand the depth he was trying to call out. Bones groaned, and blood flowed down his hands and dripped onto the spear. Even his aura became unstable, as though the abyss he controlled was beginning to pull him down as well.
Revona’s eyes sharpened.
"You will break your body."
Ervin replied quietly, "It doesn’t matter."
The broken gate roared.
"Second Depth Forbidden Spear."
The abyss gathered behind him like a collapsed world.
"Gate Beyond Drowning."
Ervin thrust, and this time, even Return To Nothing was pushed back. The point of origin emptiness trembled violently as the forbidden spear pressed into it.

The abyssal force behind Ervin’s strike was no longer merely trying to sink an attack. It was trying to drown the law of nullification itself beneath a depth that should have been beyond his current limit.
Revona’s feet slid backward, one step, then another. Blood spilled from her lips.
The Divine Realm went wild.
"He is pushing Return To Nothing back!"
"Ervin is using a forbidden technique!"
"His body is cracking!"
"He is trying to defeat Revona before she can use that final nullifying wave!"
Inside the stage, Revona’s expression finally became strained. Her Void Origin Eyes shone so brightly that faint cracks of pale light appeared around her pupils.
She poured more power into Return To Nothing, but Ervin continued pushing forward, his body breaking under the force of his own forbidden depth.
His spear pressed closer, and the black sea rose behind him like an apocalypse. Revona’s Return To Nothing began to distort. For a moment, it truly looked as if Ervin might break through.
Max narrowed his eyes. Damian’s gaze sharpened. Orion stopped breathing. Rakan’s fists clenched.
Then Revona raised her other hand. Her voice was quiet.
"Void Origin Realm."
The hollow world behind her opened fully.
"Null Origin Tide."
A pale-gray wave erupted from Revona in every direction.

It was the same move she had used against Max, the same final domain-like nullifying attack that had stripped away the power of his Divine Veins, his 5000 Draconic Essences, his Dragon Scales Transformation, Divine King Punishment, the Devouring Flames Domain, and even the timing advantage created by his clone.
Now it descended upon Ervin.

The black sea was struck first, and the Second Depth trembled. The abyssal waves lost their shape and began vanishing layer by layer. The hidden currents were erased, and the swallowed power inside the sea was nullified.
The path connecting Ervin to the Gate of the Second Depth dimmed violently.
Ervin’s forbidden spear still pressed forward, but the Null Origin Tide spread around it. The abyssal force coating the spear vanished, and the Second Depth pressure disappeared from its tip.
The black light bleeding from the gate was erased, and the forbidden art collapsed around Ervin’s body.

His eyes widened slightly. His body had already been pushed to the brink, and now the Null Origin Tide stripped away the very powers sustaining his final attack. The black sea beneath his feet dried into emptiness.
The Gate of the Second Depth flickered like an illusion about to vanish. The abyssal aura covering his body disappeared, and the spear in his hand lost its terrifying depth.

For one breath, Ervin stood there with almost nothing left, just like Max had before him. His power was gone. His abyss was silent. His gate had dimmed, and his forbidden technique had been nullified.
His body, already cracked from forcing the Gate Beyond Drowning, trembled violently as blood poured from dozens of wounds.

Revona stood opposite him, also pale, wounded, and breathing unsteadily. Null Origin Tide had clearly cost her greatly, especially after using Return To Nothing against the forbidden spear. Her Void Origin Eyes were strained, and blood stained her lips, but the pale-gray tide still surrounded her.

Ervin tried to raise his spear. His arm shook, and the spear rose only halfway. The Gate of the Second Depth flickered behind him, but it could not open again. The Null Origin Tide had stripped too much away.

Unlike Max, Ervin did not have the Dimensional Keeper legacy. He did not have a higher-scale power that Revona’s nullification could not define. He had only his abyss, and his abyss had been nullified.
Revona looked at him quietly.
"You gave everything."
Ervin did not answer. He forced one foot forward, and his body almost collapsed from that step alone.
The crowd fell silent. Even Revona’s eyes flickered slightly. Ervin was still trying to move.

He gathered the last trace of abyssal force inside his body. It was not enough to open the gate, not enough to summon the sea, and not enough to form a true technique. It was only a faint black current around the spear tip, a remnant of a remnant, but he still pointed it toward Revona.
"Abyss Spear Art."
His voice was hoarse.
"Hollow Descent."
He thrust. The spear moved slowly compared to before, but it carried all that he had left.
Revona raised her hand. The pale-gray tide moved, and the last black current vanished. Her palm stopped before his chest.
"Void Origin Palm."

The hollow force struck, and Ervin’s body was thrown backward. He crashed into the shattered stage, rolled once, and came to a stop near the edge of the arena. His spear fell beside him, and the broken gate behind him finally disappeared completely.
For a few breaths, no one spoke. Ervin tried to move, and his fingers twitched toward the spear, but his body did not rise.
Angelina Valerius looked down at him and spoke calmly.
"Ervin is unable to continue."
The result appeared above the arena.
[Winner: Revona.]
[Ervin Defeated.]
The Divine Realm remained silent for one long breath. Then it erupted.
Revona had won. She had lost to Max, but she had defeated Ervin.

Ervin had given everything. He had opened Abyssal Origin Descent from the beginning, forced the Gate of the Second Depth, and used Return To Depth and Sunken World before finally turning to a forbidden depth technique that almost shattered his own body.
He had pushed Revona so hard that she had been forced to use Return To Nothing and then the same Null Origin Tide she had used against Max.
But he could not get past it. Once Null Origin Tide stripped his abyss away, he had nothing left that could reverse the battle.

"That woman is terrifying."
Orion Starfall smiled bitterly.
"Yes. Max was the only one who could still pull out something after that tide erased everything."
Kaiden Voidmere nodded slowly.
"Ervin had the strength to nearly break Return To Nothing. But Null Origin Tide ended him."
Morgana Starveil looked at Revona with a deep gaze.
"She was pushed to the edge again."

She had won, but just like against Max, she had been forced to use everything.

The transfer light descended and carried Ervin back to his pillar, where the Eternal Hourglass immediately began repairing his broken body. Revona also returned to her pillar and sat down without a word.
The battle had ended, and Ervin had fallen. The final stretch of the Cosmic Ascension Conference had become even more unpredictable.

The other returned everything to nothing.

The abyssal waves lost their shape and began vanishing layer by layer.

The abyssal force coating the spear vanished, and the Second Depth pressure disappeared from its tip.
The black light bleeding from the gate was erased, and the forbidden art collapsed around Ervin’s body.
His eyes widened slightly.
His body had already been pushed to the brink, and now the Null Origin Tide stripped away the very powers sustaining his final attack.
The black sea beneath his feet dried into emptiness.
The Gate of the Second Depth flickered like an illusion about to vanish.
The abyssal aura covering his body disappeared, and the spear in his hand lost its terrifying depth.

His power was gone.
His abyss was silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 1917: Damian vs Max!
paragraphs: The shock of Revona’s victory over Ervin had not even fully settled when the giant screen above the Eternal Hourglass shifted once again.
The new records shone clearly for all to see.
[Max Morgan] [Total Battles Fought: 22] [Total Wins: 22]
[Ervin] [Total Battles Fought: 23] [Total Wins: 22]
[Revona] [Total Battles Fought: 23] [Total Wins: 22]
[Damian Voss] [Total Battles Fought: 22] [Total Wins: 21]
The moment the updated records appeared, countless people across the Divine Realm immediately understood how heavy the next battle would be.
Max, Ervin, and Revona now stood tied at twenty-two victories, while Damian had fallen one step behind with twenty-one. That meant the next result would affect everything.

If Max won, he would rise to twenty-three victories and place one foot ahead of all the others before his final battle with Ervin. If Damian won, he would rise to twenty-two victories again and drag the entire top ranking back into chaos.
Angelina Valerius stood calmly above the stage and waited for the murmurs to settle. Then she raised her hand.
"The next battle will now begin."
The light above the arena spun once more, and under the focused gazes of everyone present, two names slowly brightened until they stood alone above all others.
[Max Morgan vs Damian Voss]
For a moment, the entire arena seemed to forget how to breathe. Then the Divine Realm erupted once more.

The Black Dragon Clan disciples all stood up at once before the huge live screen floating above the clan grounds. Some of them clenched their fists, some widened their eyes, and some simply stared without blinking, because everyone understood what this meant.
Max was finally going to face the strongest swordsman of the Sword God Palace in a true official battle of the final stage.
Lady Virelia looked at the screen with a solemn gaze, but beneath that solemnity there was a clear trace of expectation.
"Max," she murmured softly, "do your best."
The seven family heads standing nearby also watched with serious expressions.

Even Mathew Grimes, who had long since stopped underestimating Max, narrowed his eyes and said, "This battle will be dangerous. Damian Voss is not a man who loses twice in spirit, even if he already lost once in record."

On the other side of the Divine Realm, the Sword God Palace disciples had already become extremely excited. Their strongest genius had lost to Ervin by the smallest margin possible, and many of them had been left with frustration burning in their chests.
But now that Damian had been matched against Max, the same Max who held Dragonheart and had embarrassed the Sword God Palace more than once, their emotions surged again.
"It is finally happening!"
"Senior Brother Damian must win this!"
"Max Morgan may be strong, but in a pure sword battle, how can he compare to Senior Brother Damian?"
"He carries the Sword of the Sovereign, but that does not make him the strongest swordsman!"
Even among the hidden forces, many old monsters silently straightened in their seats. This battle was not merely about victory count. It was also about the dignity of the sword path itself.

Damian Voss represented the refined and tyrannical edge of the Sword God Palace, while Max Morgan carried Dragonheart, the Emotion Severing Path, and a sword talent that had already shocked the entire conference time and again.
On the pillars inside the Eternal Hourglass, the remaining geniuses all turned their eyes toward Max and Damian.
Orion Starfall smiled widely. "Good. I have been waiting for this one."
Rakan Thorne laughed. "If these two really go all out with swords, the stage might split."
Kaiden Voidmere watched quietly. "It depends on what kind of battle they choose to fight."

Revona, still pale from her fight against Ervin, slowly lifted her eyes and looked toward Max. There was no doubt in her gaze, since she knew better than most here that Max’s sword was not ordinary anymore.

Ervin also raised his head and looked toward the arena. Even though he had just lost, his eyes were still deep and focused, and he too wanted to see what kind of sword path Max would reveal against Damian.
Angelina’s voice rang out clearly.
"Max Morgan."
"Damian Voss."
"Enter the stage."

Two beams of light descended. Max appeared on one side of the arena, calm as ever, Dragonheart resting at his hand. Damian appeared on the other side, his posture straight, his sword already in hand, and the sword intent around him calm but terrifyingly condensed.
He no longer looked like a man bothered by his previous defeat. If anything, he looked even sharper now, as if the loss to Ervin had only refined his edge further.

The two of them faced each other across the stage. For a few breaths, neither spoke. Then Damian looked at Max and said calmly, "We have already crossed swords before, but that was not an official battle."
Max smiled faintly. "That is true."

Damian’s gaze shifted briefly to Dragonheart, then returned to Max’s face. "You and I are both swordsmen. If we fight normally, the battle may drag on longer than it should, and both of us still have more battles ahead."
Max looked at him with mild curiosity. "So what do you propose?"
Damian lifted his sword slightly, and the sword intent around him sharpened.
"One sword attack each," he said. "No repeated exchanges. No prolonged battle. We each use one true sword attack, and with that single clash, we decide the victor."
The moment those words were spoken, the arena fell silent again. One sword attack. Just one.

The Sword God Palace disciples were stunned for a moment, but then many of them became even more excited. To them, this was the most fitting way for a swordsman of Damian’s level to fight another swordsman he acknowledged. It would not be a contest of exhaustion, attrition, or secondary abilities. It would be a direct collision of sword paths.
At the Black Dragon Clan, many disciples also stared with widened eyes.
"Only one attack?"
"Is Damian that confident?"
"No. This means he truly acknowledges Max."

Lady Virelia’s eyes sharpened as she looked at Max on the screen. She understood Damian’s intention very well. This was not arrogance alone. It was also pride, a swordsman’s pride. If he could not defeat Max through the sharpest essence of his sword in one strike, then he would have no need to drag the battle any further.

chapters.title: Chapter 1918: One Sword Attack!
paragraphs: On the stage, Max looked at Damian for a few silent breaths. Then he smiled.
"Good."
He slowly drew Dragonheart from its sheath, and a cold, clear hum spread across the arena.
"If a single sword attack is enough for you," Max said calmly, "then a single sword attack is enough for me as well."
Damian’s eyes became even sharper. "So you agree?"
Max nodded once. "I agree."
That simple answer immediately made the entire Divine Realm hold its breath again.
Angelina Valerius looked at both of them for a moment before speaking. "The terms are accepted. This battle will be decided by a single sword clash."

Her words caused the stage beneath them to begin glowing brighter. The laws of the Eternal Hourglass strengthened the barrier around the central arena, as if even it understood that one attack from Damian Voss and one attack from Max Morgan would not be ordinary sword moves.
Damian took a step back and raised his sword before him. Max also stepped back and held Dragonheart in both hands. The air between them changed at once. No one spoke, and no one moved carelessly.

Every spectator, every genius, every elder, and every clan across the Divine Realm fixed their gaze on the stage, because everyone understood one thing. The next moment would decide everything between these two swordsmen.
The entire Eternal Hourglass became silent after Max and Damian agreed to decide the battle with one sword attack. This was not a silence born from confusion. It was the silence of anticipation.

Everyone understood that a normal battle between these two would have been earth-shaking. Damian Voss had Sword Sovereign Heaven, a terrifying Pseudo Cosmic Path that had already cut through Aurelian’s divine luminance, Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth, Rakan’s War God Body, and many other supreme techniques.

Max Morgan had Dragonheart, the Emotion Severing Path, and a depth of sword comprehension that had only grown more frightening with each battle. If they fought normally, the clash could have lasted a long time, with both sides revealing layer after layer of strength.
But they had chosen one attack. One sword. One collision. One result.

On the stage, Damian Voss slowly closed his eyes. The sword in his hand lowered slightly, and the air around him became completely still. For a few breaths, there was no movement from him at all, yet the entire arena began to feel a sharp pressure spreading outward.

It was not wild, loud, or explosive like lightning or the abyss. It was the kind of pressure that made every sword in the Divine Realm tremble inside its sheath, because Damian’s entire being seemed to be gathering into one pure edge.
Above and behind him, Sword Sovereign Heaven began to appear. Sword-edge mountains rose into existence, and rivers of sword light flowed across the sky.
An ancient sword altar stood at the center of that world, while far above it the sword palace appeared with its empty throne.
The single sword hanging before the throne descended slowly, and as it did, all the countless sword lights throughout the Sword Sovereign Heaven bowed toward it.

This was not the First Edict, nor the Second, nor the Third, Fourth, Fifth, or Sixth. Damian did not intend to hold anything back. Against Max Morgan, anything less than the strongest attack would be meaningless.

His sword heaven began to collapse inward. The mountains of swords broke apart and turned into streams of sharp light, and the rivers of sword energy rose into the sky and flowed into the descending sword before the throne.

The sword altar cracked, and the palace trembled. The empty throne shone with a cold and noble brilliance. All of Damian’s sword authority, sword heart, sword intent, sword laws, blood, will, and battle experience gathered into the weapon in his hand.
"Sword Sovereign Heaven."
Damian opened his eyes.
"Final Edict."
The single sword before the throne fused into his blade.
"Throne Of The Only Sword."

The moment those words fell, the entire sword world behind him disappeared. No sword mountains, no sword rivers, no sword palace, and no altar or throne remained. Only Damian remained, and only his sword remained.
Because only one sword remained, everything else in the arena seemed to lose the right to be called sharp.
Across the Divine Realm, every swordsman felt their heart tremble, and the Sword God Palace fell into complete silence. This was Damian Voss pushing his strongest sword attack to the absolute limit.

The attack he had used against Ervin had already been terrifying, but now, after experiencing defeat and refining his sword heart through that loss, and after facing Max Morgan directly, Damian’s final edict had become even purer than before.
His sword was no longer merely cutting force, law, rhythm, space, or authority. It was declaring that beneath this one sword, all other paths would be judged.

Max stood opposite him, and Dragonheart hummed softly in his hand. The moment Damian’s strongest attack reached its peak, Max’s eyes became serious as well. He had already seen how terrifying Throne Of The Only Sword was.

If Damian had used this attack against most other geniuses, the battle would have ended instantly. Even Revona’s Void Origin Eyes would need to treat this sword with caution, because Damian had compressed his entire Pseudo Cosmic Path into one clean and absolute strike.

Max exhaled slowly. He did not activate Divine King Punishment. He did not release the Devouring Flames Domain. He did not use the four Divine Veins, and he did not summon the power of the Dimensional Keeper legacy again. This was a sword battle, so he would answer with the sword.
Dragonheart rose before him, and a cold, silent aura spread from the blade.
"Emotion Severing Path."
The moment those words left Max’s mouth, the warmth of the arena vanished. Damian’s sword was pure, proud, sovereign, and absolute. Max’s sword was quiet, cold, forbidden, and terrifying.
The Emotion Severing Path did not merely carry sharpness. It carried severance. It severed feeling, intent, connection, rhythm, authority, and the invisible things that allowed power to remain whole.
The air around Dragonheart became deathly calm, as if every emotion in the battlefield had been cut away before the sword was even swung.
But this time, Max did not stop there. He closed his eyes for a brief moment, and then the sword technique inherited from the Sword Saint flowed through his body.
"Saint Origin Sword Art."

The moment the name appeared, Dragonheart’s aura changed again, and the cold severing power of the Emotion Severing Path gained structure. Before this, Max’s Emotion Severing Path had been frightening because of how forbidden and unpredictable it was.
It could sever things that should not be severed, and even top geniuses struggled to understand where the true danger lay.
But now, when Max fused it with the Saint Origin Sword Art, that forbidden severing path gained a sacred sword framework that seemed to arrange every strand of severance into perfect order.
Emotion Severing Path was the edge, and Saint Origin Sword Art was the form. One was forbidden severance, and the other was the Sword Saint’s order.
When the two merged, the power gathered around Dragonheart became so sharp, so calm, and so complete that even Damian’s eyes changed.
For the first time, a trace of deep admiration appeared in his gaze.
