chapters.title: Chapter 1928: Winner of Cosmic Ascension Conference!
paragraphs: For one breath, the final result screen above the Eternal Hourglass shone like the brightest star in the starry sky.
The whole Divine Realm seemed frozen under that golden light, as if everyone needed a moment to take in what had just happened.
Ervin’s strongest forbidden spear, the Body-Burying Abyss Spear, had come out with enough force to shake the Eternal Hourglass itself. Still, Max Morgan had faced it without fear.

He had unleashed the full power of his 5000 Dragon Essences, entered the Dragon Scales Transformation, strengthened his body with the four Divine Veins, gathered Divine King Punishment into his blade, guided the Emotion Severing Path through the Saint Origin Sword Art, and cut down the strongest attack Ervin had ever thrown.
The black sea was gone. The broken gate had faded. Ervin’s spear had snapped. And Max Morgan was still standing.

Angelina Valerius looked down at the arena, her pale golden eyes taking in the state of the battlefield. Golden light from the Eternal Hourglass wrapped around Ervin, healing the damage from his forbidden technique and keeping his body from breaking down further.
Across from him, Max stood with Dragonheart lowered at his side. His dragon scales were fading, and small sparks of seven-colored lightning drifted around him like the last pieces of a storm.
Then the result screen changed.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 24]
[Total Wins: 24]
[Total Defeats: 0]
Beneath it, new words appeared.
[Perfect Victory Record Achieved.]
Then a second record showed up.
[Ervin]
[Total Battles Fought: 24]
[Total Wins: 22]
[Total Defeats: 2]
The whole Eternal Hourglass went quiet. No one spoke. No one cheered. It felt like no one was even breathing.

Then Angelina Valerius raised her hand. The golden light around the Eternal Hourglass grew brighter, and the huge screen above the arena stretched out until it filled almost the entire sky over the stage.
Ancient symbols circled around it slowly, like divine seals marking down an event people would remember for years to come.
Angelina’s voice rang out.
"The final battle has ended."
Her tone was calm, but there was a weight behind it that made every word land harder.
"With twenty-four wins, zero losses, and a perfect record in the final stage, Max Morgan is the winner of the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
The golden screen lit up.
[Cosmic Ascension Conference Champion]
[Max Morgan]
For one moment, those words hung over the arena like something out of the heavens. Then the whole Divine Realm exploded. The noise was bigger than anything that had come before it.

Every viewing formation linked to the Eternal Hourglass shook under the flood of voices. Countless cities, forces, clans, palaces, floating islands, ancient halls, trading hubs, academies, and hidden corners of the world shook with millions of people shouting Max’s name at once.
Max Morgan. The name spread like wildfire.
In the Black Dragon Clan, the entire place lost it. Disciples shouted until their voices went hoarse. Elders who had kept their composure for centuries stood up with shaking hands.

Some laughed out loud. Some slammed their fists on tables hard enough to break them. Some just stared at the screen with wet eyes, still not quite believing that someone from their own clan had reached the top of the Cosmic Ascension Conference with a perfect record.
"Champion!"
"Max Morgan is the champion!"
"Twenty-four wins and not a single loss!"
"The Black Dragon Clan has raised the strongest genius of this whole conference!"

Lady Virelia stood in front of the huge projection with her hands clasped behind her back. Her face stayed calm, but the small curve at the corner of her mouth said everything she didn’t put into words.

She was the one who had chosen Max. She had brought him into the Black Dragon Clan and watched him grow from an unknown talent into someone who could now stand above Damian Voss, Revona, Ervin, Orion, Kaiden, Rakan, Aurelian, and every other top genius of this generation.
Mathew Grimes stared at the screen for a long moment before letting out a deep breath.
"From now on, no one in the Divine Realm will dare call him just a lucky junior."
Another family head nodded slowly. "That’s right. From now on, every force out there will have to put his name at the very top of their watch list for the younger generation."
In the Sword God Palace, the mood was mixed. Damian Voss had now lost twice in the final stretch, but none of the swordsmen there could deny what they’d just seen.
Max hadn’t won because Damian was weak. He’d won because his sword was sharp enough to cut through the final edict of Sword Sovereign Heaven itself.
Many disciples stared at the champion screen without saying a word, their pride stung, but quietly shaken by the sheer beauty of the sword clash they’d just watched.
In the Nine Star Court, Orion Starfall’s supporters cheered and sighed all at once. Orion had lost to Max, but that fight had forced Max to bring out the Emotion Severing Path in full.
The Nine Star Court’s elders knew well enough that Orion’s loss hadn’t dulled his shine. It had just placed him in the same era as someone even more terrifying.

In the Grand Void Sanctum, Kaiden Voidmere’s elders watched the screen with heavy, unreadable faces. Max had beaten Kaiden with a clear edge in the Void Genesis Art and the Dimensional Sovereign Body.
Now that Max was champion, their thoughts grew even more complicated, since they understood the link between Max and their own supreme inheritance path was not a simple one.
In the War God Palace, Rakan Thorne’s supporters laughed loudly despite his loss. To them, losing to the champion wasn’t shameful. It just proved Rakan had fought someone truly worth fighting.
In the elven lands, the reaction hit harder. Aurelian Lareth sat in silence in front of the projection, his face pale, his fists clenched so tight his nails dug into his palms.

Every time Max’s name flashed on the screen, it felt like another slap to his pride. The stolen Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline inside him pulsed faintly, and Max’s calm voice echoed in his memory again.
"Take care of my bloodline until then. It won’t be long before I come for it."
Aurelian’s face twisted, but he said nothing. There was nothing he could say.
Far from him, among the scattered survivors of the old third elven faction, Nancy, Caroline, Jessica, and others watched the same projection with pounding hearts.

Some covered their mouths. Some cried quietly. Some just stared at the white-haired young man under the champion screen, struggling to connect him to the child whose life had once been torn apart by betrayal.
Caroline’s eyes filled with tears. "He really did it."
Nancy nodded, her voice shaking. "Her Majesty’s son is the champion."
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the other top fighters were watching Max too.

Revona sat quietly, pale and worn out, but there was no bitterness in her eyes. She had lost only after pushing Max hard enough to reveal a power that even her Null Origin Tide couldn’t erase. To her, that loss made sense.
Damian Voss stood with his sword sheathed, calm, a trace of respect still lingering in his eyes.
Ervin, still wrapped in healing golden light, looked at Max and smiled faintly despite his battered state.
"You really became champion."
Max looked back at him. "You made that final fight hard."
Ervin laughed softly. "Not hard enough."
Max didn’t answer right away. Then he smiled.
"You kept standing until your spear broke."
Ervin’s smile stayed faint. "It was the least I could do."

chapters.title: Chapter 1929: End of the Conference!
paragraphs: Angelina Valerius lowered herself slightly, and the golden light around the arena gathered above Max.

A glowing mark slowly took shape in the sky, marking him as champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. It didn’t sink into him right away. It just hovered there, shining like a crown waiting for the formal ceremony.
The whole Divine Realm watched that scene. Countless people understood this moment meant more than just the end of a conference. It marked the rise of a name.

Max Morgan had entered the Cosmic Ascension Conference as a surprising talent from the Black Dragon Clan. He was leaving it as the strongest genius of his era. At least, that’s what most of the Divine Realm believed.
But far away from the great clans and palaces buzzing over the new champion, there was a quiet, out-of-the-way planet with dim skies, broken mountains, and a small city protected by old formations.

Inside a simple, well-guarded hall on that planet, a few people were watching the same broadcast. The picture wasn’t as clear as the ones the big forces had. It flickered now and then from the distance and interference, but the words above the arena still came through.
[Cosmic Ascension Conference Champion]
[Max Morgan]
Among the people in that hall stood a beautiful woman with a calm smile.

Freya, Max’s older sister. Her eyes stayed fixed on the screen, and when she saw Max standing under the golden champion banner, her expression softened in a way few people around her had ever seen. There was pride in her eyes, but no surprise.
There was warmth in her smile, but no disbelief.

Beside her stood Lucien. He stared at the projection for a long while without saying anything. His usual easy manner had given way to something more serious, and his eyes stayed locked on Max’s figure, as if he were trying to measure something the screen couldn’t fully show.
After a long pause, Lucien let out a slow breath.
"He’s really become the strongest genius in the Divine Realm."
The others in the room turned toward him. Lucien didn’t look away from the screen.

"I always knew Max was special, but this is different. Beating Revona, Damian, Ervin, and everyone else with a perfect record isn’t something you can put down to talent alone." His eyes grew more serious. "If I fought him right now, at the same level, I’m not sure I could beat him."
Those words made the whole room go quiet. Everyone there knew how much pride and strength Lucien carried, so hearing him say something like that meant a lot.
Freya just smiled. Her eyes stayed on Max. She wasn’t shocked, and she wasn’t doubtful. She simply watched the white-haired figure under the champion screen and thought to herself.
’Of course you did it, Max.’
Her smile grew a little warmer.
’I wouldn’t expect anything less from my little brother.’
The final result screen kept shining above the Eternal Hourglass for a long time.
[Cosmic Ascension Conference Champion]
[Max Morgan]
[Final Record: 24 Wins, 0 Defeats]
[Perfect Victory]
Max Morgan had won. The white-haired genius of the Black Dragon Clan had gone through the entire final stage without losing a single match.
He’d beaten the strongest young fighters of this generation one after another.

He’d beaten Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, Rakan’s War God Body, Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth, Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion, Orion’s Nine Star Sovereign Body, Revona’s Void Origin Realm, Damian Voss’s Sword Sovereign Heaven, and Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent.

Every name he’d faced was strong enough to shake an ancient force on its own, yet all of them had eventually fallen to his sword, his body, his bloodline, his Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and the deep well of strength hidden behind his calm face.

Angelina Valerius stood above the restored arena and looked down at Max. Golden light from the Eternal Hourglass gathered around her like streams of ancient power, and for the first time since the final stage began, the giant hourglass above the arena stopped turning.
The sand inside it went still, and the whole world inside the venue seemed to bow toward the end of the conference.
Angelina raised both hands slightly.
"The Cosmic Ascension Conference has come to its end."
Her voice was calm, but it carried further than ever before.

"The final stage is complete. Every battle has been recorded. Every ranking has been confirmed. By the authority of the Eternal Hourglass, watched over by the Primordials, and witnessed by the whole Divine Realm, I officially declare the Cosmic Ascension Conference over."
The golden screen lit up again.
[Cosmic Ascension Conference Officially Concluded.]
[Champion: Max Morgan.]

The moment those words appeared, the whole Eternal Hourglass roared one last time. This wasn’t just a roar of shock anymore. It was a roar of closure, the sound of an era recognizing its newest monster.
The defeated fighters on the pillars looked at Max, each with a different look on their face.

Orion Starfall smiled brightly, his eyes still full of excitement from a fight worth remembering. Rakan Thorne laughed loudly and punched his own palm, clearly already hungry for another shot someday.
Kaiden Voidmere stayed quiet, but the respect in his eyes was plain to see.
Damian Voss stood tall with his sword at his waist, calm and dignified even in defeat.
Revona’s pale eyes stayed fixed on Max, as if she were still trying to work out the star-like power that had gotten past her Null Origin Tide.
Ervin, mostly healed now by the Eternal Hourglass, looked at Max with a small smile, the broken pieces of his spear already restored beside him by the venue’s power.
Angelina’s gaze passed over all of them before settling back on Max.

"The award ceremony and everything else after the conference will be handled according to the rules of the Eternal Hourglass and the agreements between the participating forces. For now, everyone will be sent back to their own forces."
Golden light lit up beneath every fighter. One by one, beams of light came down, and the pillars began to empty. Some fighters vanished quietly.
Some looked at Max one last time before disappearing. Some clenched their fists, already thinking ahead to the day they’d get to fight him again.
Max stood in the middle of the arena as the light gathered under his feet. Dragonheart rested quietly at his side, and the last traces of seven-colored lightning faded from the air around him.
His dragon scales were gone, his divine veins had closed, and the terrifying power from the final battle had settled back into his body.
Even without any visible power around him now, he seemed heavier somehow, as if the title of champion had added an invisible weight to his presence.
Angelina Valerius looked at him one last time.
"Congratulations, Max Morgan."
Max gave a small nod. "Thank you."
Then the golden light swallowed him whole.

chapters.title: Chapter 1930: Celebrations!
paragraphs: The Eternal Hourglass disappeared from his vision. For an instant, there was only silence and flowing golden light. Then the world changed.
Max appeared back in the Black Dragon Clan. The moment his feet touched the ground, a thunderous roar hit him from every direction.
"Max!"
"Champion!"
"Max Morgan!"
"The champion has returned!"

It felt like the entire Black Dragon Clan had gathered to welcome him. The main square was packed with disciples, elders, branch members, family guards, servants, retainers, and powerful figures from every faction in the clan.

Huge banners had already gone up across the sky, black and gold dragon flags flapped in the wind, and countless celebration formations sent streams of light into the heavens. Dragon-shaped fireworks burst above the clan grounds, spelling out Max’s name again and again in blazing golden letters.
[Max Morgan]
[Cosmic Ascension Conference Champion]

The cheering grew even louder the moment everyone saw him standing there. Many young disciples shouted until their voices cracked. Some looked at him like they were seeing the future of the Black Dragon Clan itself.

Even elders who normally kept a strict, dignified air were smiling openly, their eyes full of pride and disbelief. The Black Dragon Clan had sent Max to the Cosmic Ascension Conference as a top-tier genius, but he had come back as the undisputed champion with a perfect record.
That changed everything. This win didn’t belong to Max alone anymore. In the eyes of the clan, it belonged to the whole Black Dragon Clan too.
Lady Virelia stood at the front of the crowd. Her expression stayed calm, but the pride in her eyes was impossible to hide. She looked at Max for a few breaths before a faint smile crossed her face.
"You did well."
Those three words were simple, but to the people who knew her, they carried a lot of weight.
Max smiled faintly. "I only did what I had to do."

Mathew Grimes laughed loudly from the side. "Only did what you had to do? Brat, you beat every monster in that conference and came back with twenty-four wins and zero losses. Do you know how many old clans probably can’t sleep right now because of you?"
Several family heads laughed along, while some elders nodded with serious looks.
One elder said, "From today on, the name Max Morgan won’t just be treated as a rising genius. It’ll be treated as the name of a future overlord."
Another elder added, "No force out there will dare look down on the Black Dragon Clan’s younger generation again."
The disciples roared once more.
"Future overlord!"
"Champion Max!"
"Black Dragon Clan’s pride!"

Max looked out at the sea of excited faces and felt something strange in his chest. He’d faced storms of lightning, abyssal gates, void nullification, sword thrones, war bodies, and divine light, and countless deadly techniques, without his expression really changing much.
But now, standing in front of the clan that had watched him rise through the conference, hearing them celebrate him so sincerely, he felt something quieter settle inside him.

For a moment, his thoughts drifted to his mother, his father, his sister, Caroline, Nancy, Jessica, and everyone else tied to the truth behind his bloodline and his past. Winning the Cosmic Ascension Conference wasn’t the end. It was just a step. An important one, but still just a step.
Aurelian still had the stolen source. His parents were still locked away. The people behind the old betrayal were still out there. There were still enemies waiting beyond this celebration.
But today, at least for this moment, Max let himself smile.
The crowd saw that smile and exploded again.
Lady Virelia’s smile deepened a little. Mathew Grimes stepped forward and clapped Max hard on the shoulder, though the impact meant nothing to Max after everything he’d been through.
"Come," Mathew said with a grin. "The whole clan has been waiting to celebrate. Don’t think you can come back as champion and just quietly disappear like nothing happened."
Max looked at the overflowing crowd, the banners in the sky, the cheering disciples, and the elders watching with shining eyes. Then he sighed lightly, though the smile stayed on his face.
"Looks like I don’t have a choice."
Lady Virelia said calmly, "You don’t."
The disciples nearby laughed. The celebration got even louder.
As Max walked forward into the heart of the Black Dragon Clan, voices rose all around him, chanting his name over and over.
Above the clan grounds, dragon-shaped lights circled the sky, and the golden words announcing his championship kept shining like a message to every nearby territory.
The Cosmic Ascension Conference had ended. Max Morgan had come home. And the Black Dragon Clan celebrated the birth of its champion.
The celebration in the Black Dragon Clan didn’t wind down quickly. For a full day and night, the clan grounds stayed brighter than most cities look in broad daylight.

Dragon-shaped fireworks crossed the sky in waves, celebration formations poured golden light over the main square, and disciples kept talking about the Cosmic Ascension Conference again and again, like they were retelling a legend that had just been born in front of them.
Every battle got discussed. Every opponent got brought up. Every moment where Max revealed a new power got repeated with even more excitement than the last telling.

Max himself got dragged from one hall to another, from one group of elders to the next, and from one crowd of disciples to another, until even he started to think that fighting Ervin’s forbidden final spear had been easier than escaping his own clan’s enthusiasm.
Mathew Grimes laughed every time Max tried to slip away quietly, while Lady Virelia watched from the side with a faint smile that made it clear she had no plans to rescue him.

Lady Virelia was summoned to the central ancestral hall.

sentences.text: The Eternal Hourglass disappeared from his vision.
For an instant, there was only silence and flowing golden light.
Then the world changed.
Max appeared back in the Black Dragon Clan.
The moment his feet touched the ground, a thunderous roar hit him from every direction.
"Max!"
"Champion!"
"Max Morgan!"
"The champion has returned!"
It felt like the entire Black Dragon Clan had gathered to welcome him.
The main square was packed with disciples, elders, branch members, family guards, servants, retainers, and powerful figures from every faction in the clan.
Huge banners had already gone up across the sky, black and gold dragon flags flapped in the wind, and countless celebration formations sent streams of light into the heavens.
Dragon-shaped fireworks burst above the clan grounds, spelling out Max’s name again and again in blazing golden letters.
[Max Morgan]
[Cosmic Ascension Conference Champion]
The cheering grew even louder the moment everyone saw him standing there.
Many young disciples shouted until their voices cracked.
Some looked at him like they were seeing the future of the Black Dragon Clan itself.
Even elders who normally kept a strict, dignified air were smiling openly, their eyes full of pride and disbelief.
The Black Dragon Clan had sent Max to the Cosmic Ascension Conference as a top-tier genius, but he had come back as the undisputed champion with a perfect record.
That changed everything.
This win didn’t belong to Max alone anymore.
In the eyes of the clan, it belonged to the whole Black Dragon Clan too.
Lady Virelia stood at the front of the crowd.
Her expression stayed calm, but the pride in her eyes was impossible to hide.
She looked at Max for a few breaths before a faint smile crossed her face.
"You did well."
Those three words were simple, but to the people who knew her, they carried a lot of weight.
Max smiled faintly.
"I only did what I had to do."
Mathew Grimes laughed loudly from the side.
"Only did what you had to do?
Brat, you beat every monster in that conference and came back with twenty-four wins and zero losses.
Do you know how many old clans probably can’t sleep right now because of you?"
Several family heads laughed along, while some elders nodded with serious looks.
One elder said, "From today on, the name Max Morgan won’t just be treated as a rising genius.
It’ll be treated as the name of a future overlord."
Another elder added, "No force out there will dare look down on the Black Dragon Clan’s younger generation again."
The disciples roared once more.
"Future overlord!"
"Champion Max!"
"Black Dragon Clan’s pride!"
Max looked out at the sea of excited faces and felt something strange in his chest.
He’d faced storms of lightning, abyssal gates, void nullification, sword thrones, war bodies, and divine light, and countless deadly techniques, without his expression really changing much.
But now, standing in front of the clan that had watched him rise through the conference, hearing them celebrate him so sincerely, he felt something quieter settle inside him.
For a moment, his thoughts drifted to his mother, his father, his sister, Caroline, Nancy, Jessica, and everyone else tied to the truth behind his bloodline and his past.
Winning the Cosmic Ascension Conference wasn’t the end.
It was just a step.
An important one, but still just a step.
Aurelian still had the stolen source.
His parents were still locked away.
The people behind the old betrayal were still out there.
There were still enemies waiting beyond this celebration.
But today, at least for this moment, Max let himself smile.
The crowd saw that smile and exploded again.
Lady Virelia’s smile deepened a little.

"The whole clan has been waiting to celebrate.

The celebration got even louder.

chapters.title: Chapter 1931: Master of the 33rd Hall!
paragraphs: The meeting wasn’t open to ordinary disciples, but word got around fast anyway.

The thirty-six halls of the Black Dragon Clan sat among the highest seats of power, just below the true ruling elders and the patriarch’s own authority. Each hall controlled its own resources, disciples, territories, experts, and duties.
A hall master wasn’t just an elder with a fancy title. A hall master was someone whose voice could shape the direction of the whole clan.
And now, Lady Virelia had been named one of the hall masters of the thirty-six halls.
When the news got out, nobody stayed surprised for long. Some elders had once questioned her choice to bring Max in from the mortal realm.

Some had wondered why a woman of her standing would personally get involved with a junior who, back then, had no deep foundation in the Divine Realm and no ancient divine background to match the native geniuses of the top forces. But all those doubts didn’t matter anymore.
Lady Virelia had chosen a mortal. That mortal had entered the Divine Realm. That mortal had represented the Black Dragon Clan.
And that mortal had become the strongest genius of the entire Cosmic Ascension Conference. No political argument could stand up against that. No internal faction could deny that kind of achievement.

Inside the ancestral hall, Virelia stood calmly in front of several supreme elders, her silver eyes steady and unreadable. The old experts around her carried deep auras and ancient authority, but none of them looked at her with the faint dismissiveness some might have shown in the past.
The champion’s spotlight hadn’t landed only on Max. It had also landed on the person who found him, chose him, protected him, and brought him into the Black Dragon Clan.
One old supreme elder looked at her and spoke slowly.

"Virelia, your judgment has brought great fortune to the clan. Max Morgan’s victory has changed how the Divine Realm sees us, and it’s also given the younger generation of the Black Dragon Clan someone to look up to. Because of this achievement, and because of your past merits, the council has agreed to name you the new Hall Master of the 33rd hall."
The hall went quiet.
The 33rd hall wasn’t a weak one. It controlled several important cultivation grounds, a lot of elite disciples, and a big share of resources tied to combat training and bloodline tempering.
For Virelia to be named its hall master right after Max’s victory showed just how much weight the clan had put on her contribution.
Lady Virelia bowed slightly. "I accept."

Her voice was calm, but the elders could tell her standing in the clan had shifted completely. From that day on, no one would think of her as just Max’s master or the woman who picked him up from the mortal realm.
She was now Lady Virelia, Hall Master of the Ninth Dragon Hall, one of the thirty-six hall masters of the Black Dragon Clan.
By the time the news spread through the clan, plenty of disciples got worked up all over again.
"Lady Virelia became a hall master!"
"Of course she did. She’s the one who picked Senior Brother Max out of the mortal realm."
"Can you imagine? A mortal genius she raised up ended up becoming champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
"That alone is enough to shake the whole clan."
"That means Senior Brother Max has even stronger backing inside the clan now too."
The talk kept going for hours.
Max heard the news later that same day. He wasn’t surprised. If anything, he felt she deserved it.

Lady Virelia had backed him back when his name carried no real weight in the Divine Realm, and even though Max had never needed anyone to carry him, he understood well enough that her decision had given him a place inside the Black Dragon Clan and a platform to rise faster.
The next day, the excitement in the clan had cooled down a bit, though things were still lively.

Max sat in a quiet spot inside one of the buildings in the Dimension of Genesis. The pavilion looked out over a lake covered in dark-gold lotus flowers, with thin streaks of spiritual mist drifting above the water.
Alice sat across from him, her eyes bright with curiosity, while Lenavira leaned against the side railing with a calm, faintly amused look.
Alice had been peppering him with questions for almost half an hour.

"So when Revona used that Null Origin Tide and stripped away all your power, what did it actually feel like?" she asked, leaning forward with both hands on the stone table. "Everyone outside could only see the black flames die down and then that star-like light show up around you. I still don’t get how you got out of that."

Lenavira looked at him too. "I’m curious about that as well. That woman beat both Ervin and Damian with the same attack. Even after watching it a few times, I still can’t tell how you broke through it."
Max lifted the tea cup in front of him and took a slow sip.
"It felt awful," he said honestly.
Alice blinked. "That’s it?"
Max smiled faintly. "What else do you want me to say?"

"I want details," Alice said right away. "You became champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, beat Revona, Damian, and Ervin, and now you’re sitting here drinking tea like nothing happened. At least describe it properly."
Lenavira smiled lightly. "She’s got a point. You’re way too calm for someone who just shook the whole Divine Realm."
Max set the cup down.
"I’m calm because the conference is over. If I keep getting worked up after every win, I’ll wear myself out before the real problems show up."
Alice’s expression shifted slightly. "Real problems?"
Max didn’t answer right away. His gaze drifted across the lake.

The Cosmic Ascension Conference had ended, but his enemies hadn’t gone anywhere. Aurelian still held the stolen source of his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. His parents were still locked away in the Celestial Thorn Abyss.
The forces behind his family’s betrayal were still standing. And now that he was champion, even more eyes would be on him than before.
Lenavira noticed the shift in his expression and let it go.
Alice also went quiet for a moment before switching the subject.
"Still, you really did beat everyone. Orion, Kaiden, Revona, Damian, Ervin. Even the people who doubted you before can’t say a thing now."
Max smiled faintly. "They can still say plenty of things."
Alice shook her head. "They can, but nobody’s going to believe them."
Just as she said that, the air above the courtyard shifted.

A deep bell sound rang out across the inner district of the Black Dragon Clan. Once. Then twice. Then a third time. It even reached the Dimension of Genesis, since Max had made sure that anything happening outside could be heard or seen from inside his dimensions.
The bell wasn’t a war alarm, but it carried a solemn weight that made Alice’s and Lenavira’s expressions change at the same time. Max turned his gaze toward the sky as well.

chapters.title: Chapter 1932: Envoy of the Primordial Race!
paragraphs: A black-gold pathway opened above the clan’s outer boundary formation.

Several powerful auras rose from the Black Dragon Clan at once, not out of hostility but as a formal welcome. The sky above the main entrance filled with dragon-shaped formations, and a group of elders appeared beneath the opened pathway.
Among them stood Mathew Grimes, several hall masters, and Lady Virelia, who now wore the formal insignia of the Black Dragon Palace.
Alice stood up. "Someone important arrived."
Lenavira narrowed her eyes. "Very important. The clan wouldn’t use that kind of reception for an ordinary envoy."
Max’s eyes deepened.
A moment later, an elder’s voice echoed through the courtyard.
"Max Morgan, the clan requests your presence at the main reception hall."
Max slowly stood.
Alice looked at him. "Do you know who it is?"
"No," Max said calmly, "but I’d guess it’s connected to the conference."
Lenavira’s gaze sharpened. "The rewards?"
Max didn’t answer, but he was thinking the same thing.

A few moments later, Max arrived at the main reception hall. The mood inside was solemn. Mathew Grimes stood at the front with several high-ranking elders, and Lady Virelia stood slightly to one side, her new hall master token hanging at her waist.
The moment Max walked in, several eyes turned toward him, but the strongest presence in the room didn’t come from the Black Dragon Clan.
It came from the stranger standing near the center.

The man looked tall and ancient, though his face didn’t seem old or young. His hair was silver-black, his eyes carried faint violet-gold rings, and his robe was woven from something that seemed to shift between starlight and darkness depending on the angle.
He didn’t give off overwhelming pressure, yet just being near him made the surrounding air feel denser than usual.
He wasn’t from any ordinary divine race. He was an envoy of the Primordial Race.

The moment Max entered, the envoy turned toward him. His gaze lingered on Max’s face for a second, then seemed to look deeper, as if he were reading through Max’s flesh, blood, aura, soul, and hidden foundation all at once.
But he didn’t act arrogant about it. Instead, he gave a slight nod.
"Max Morgan."
Max looked at him calmly. "I am."
The envoy’s voice was steady. "I am Sarvion, envoy of the Primordial Race. I’ve come under the order of the Primordial Council to escort you to the Primordial Ancestral Domain."
The hall grew even quieter. Even though many had already guessed why he’d come, hearing it said out loud still landed with weight.
Sarvion went on. "As the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, you’ve earned the highest reward the Primordial Race grants to this generation."
Alice and Lenavira had only followed as far as the side entrance of the reception area, but even from there, they couldn’t hide their shock at hearing that.
The envoy looked straight at Max.
"You are to receive the Primordial Award."
Several elders drew in a soft breath at those words.

It was no secret in the Divine Realm that the top ten of the Cosmic Ascension Conference weren’t just rewarded with treasures, cultivation resources, or ancient techniques. Those things had value, but the real meaning of the conference tied back to the Primordials themselves.

The top ten were said to be chosen by the Primordial Race. They’d be granted that race’s bloodline and given a chance to walk the path toward becoming Primordials themselves. For most geniuses, this was the single greatest opportunity of a lifetime.
The Primordial Race stood above countless divine bloodlines. Their foundation went older and deeper, closer to the original laws of existence, than most races could imagine.
Even a trace of their bloodline could reshape a genius’s body, talent, perception, and future. And an official shot at becoming a true Primordial was something even ancient clans would go mad over.
Max wasn’t just one of the top ten. He was the champion. That meant his reward would be the greatest of them all.

Sarvion continued. "The rest of the top ten will be summoned in turn, but the champion has first right. You’ll be brought to the Primordial Ancestral Domain, where the inheritance ceremony will take place. If it succeeds, you’ll officially step onto the path of the Primordial Race and be recognized as a Primordial candidate."
The words "Primordial candidate" made the whole hall tighten up.
Mathew Grimes’s eyes lit up. Several elders couldn’t hide their excitement. Even Lady Virelia’s expression grew more serious.
Max, though, stayed calm.
He looked at Sarvion and asked, "And if the ceremony fails?"
The envoy’s eyes shifted slightly, as if he appreciated the question.

"Then you’ll still receive a partial Primordial bloodline along with other rewards fitting for the champion. But if the ceremony fully succeeds, you won’t just get a bloodline. You’ll become one of us, in name, in foundation, and in future potential."
The hall went silent again.
Alice looked at Max with wide eyes. Lenavira’s expression turned complicated too.
Officially becoming a Primordial wasn’t a small thing. It wasn’t like joining a clan, taking a title, or accepting an ordinary inheritance.

It meant Max’s identity in the Divine Realm would shift again. He was already the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, the strongest genius of the younger generation, and the pride of the Black Dragon Clan. If he also became tied to the Primordial Race, his standing would rise to a level that countless forces would find frightening.
Max looked at the envoy for a moment. Then he smiled faintly.
"So the champion’s reward is to become a Primordial."
Sarvion nodded. "That is the highest reward, among other things."
Max’s gaze stayed calm, but a thought passed through his mind.
’Another bloodline. Another inheritance. Another path.’
He already carried a lot. The Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline. The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. The Dimensional Sovereign Body.

The Emotion Severing Path. Divine King Punishment. The Devouring Flames Domain. The Seven Divine Veins. Dragonheart. The Dimensional Keeper legacy. And now the Primordials were offering him a shot at becoming one of them.
Max didn’t yet know whether this opportunity would turn out simple, dangerous, or tangled up in deeper secrets of the Divine Realm.

But he knew one thing for sure. He hadn’t fought through the Cosmic Ascension Conference just for applause. If there was a reward out there that could make him stronger, he’d take it, because sooner or later, he’d need every bit of strength he could get.

"Then you’ll still receive a partial Primordial bloodline along with other rewards fitting for the champion.
But if the ceremony fully succeeds, you won’t just get a bloodline.
You’ll become one of us, in name, in foundation, and in future potential."
The hall went silent again.
Alice looked at Max with wide eyes.
Lenavira’s expression turned complicated too.
Officially becoming a Primordial wasn’t a small thing.
It wasn’t like joining a clan, taking a title, or accepting an ordinary inheritance.
It meant Max’s identity in the Divine Realm would shift again.
He was already the champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, the strongest genius of the younger generation, and the pride of the Black Dragon Clan.
If he also became tied to the Primordial Race, his standing would rise to a level that countless forces would find frightening.
Max looked at the envoy for a moment.
Then he smiled faintly.
"So the champion’s reward is to become a Primordial."
Sarvion nodded.
"That is the highest reward, among other things."
Max’s gaze stayed calm, but a thought passed through his mind.
’Another bloodline.
Another inheritance.
Another path.’
He already carried a lot.
The Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline.
The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.
The Dimensional Sovereign Body.
The Emotion Severing Path.
Divine King Punishment.
The Devouring Flames Domain.
The Seven Divine Veins.
Dragonheart.
The Dimensional Keeper legacy.
And now the Primordials were offering him a shot at becoming one of them.
Max didn’t yet know whether this opportunity would turn out simple, dangerous, or tangled up in deeper secrets of the Divine Realm.
But he knew one thing for sure.
He hadn’t fought through the Cosmic Ascension Conference just for applause.
If there was a reward out there that could make him stronger, he’d take it, because sooner or later, he’d need every bit of strength he could get.

chapters.title: Chapter 1933: Idle Time With Alice and Lenavira!
paragraphs: Sarvion looked at him and spoke again.
"The Primordial Ancestral Domain is ready. Once your clan has finished its arrangements, you may leave with me."
Lady Virelia stepped forward. "How much time does he have?"
Sarvion answered calmly. "The champion has priority, but the ceremony can’t be pushed back for long. Three days at most."
Mathew Grimes looked at Max. "Then you’ll prepare during those three days."
Max nodded.
Sarvion’s gaze stayed on him. "Max Morgan, champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, the Primordial Race awaits you."
The reception hall fell into a heavy silence.
Outside the hall, the Black Dragon Clan was still soaking in the glow of Max’s victory. But inside, everyone understood that the next Chapter of his journey had already opened.
The Cosmic Ascension Conference had ended. The road to the Primordials had begun.
The three days before Max had to leave for the Primordial Ancestral Domain passed faster than he expected.

The Black Dragon Clan wanted him to rest, prepare, and settle after the conference, but Max had no plans to spend those days buried under endless visits, formal congratulations, and elders quietly trying to probe the powers he’d revealed.
The conference had already put too many eyes on him.

Every force in the Divine Realm was studying his abilities, his fighting style, his bloodline, his sword path, his lightning, his black flames, his physical strength, and the mysterious star-like power he’d used against Revona.
If he stayed openly in the clan, he wouldn’t get a single hour of peace.
So Max went to the Dimension of Genesis.

For him, it was an escape. For Alice and Lenavira, it was simply home. They already lived there. Lily tagged along too, buzzing around excitedly like a small spirit who could never sit still for long.
The moment Max arrived, the noise of the Black Dragon Clan faded behind him.

The Dimension of Genesis stretched out in its vast, peaceful glory, full of pure energy, ancient light, floating islands, spiritual lakes, and distant stars that looked close enough to touch yet far enough to remind anyone that this place wasn’t ordinary.
The air here carried a feeling of beginnings, as if every breath held a trace of creation itself.

Alice was already there, sitting on the edge of a floating platform like she’d never left. Lenavira stood nearby under a drifting veil of light, calm as always, as if she’d been standing there since the world began.
Neither of them looked surprised. This was their home. They just watched Max as he arrived.
"You’re back," Alice said casually, like he’d only stepped out for a short walk.
Max paused for a moment, then smiled faintly. "I suppose I am."
Lenavira gave a soft nod. "Was it the Primordials?"
"Yes. I leave in three days."
Lily zipped around Max’s head in a circle, giggling. "You always leave us!"
She hovered in front of him, puffing her cheeks slightly like a kid complaining about being left behind.
Max glanced at her. "You were with Alice and Lenavira the whole time."
Lily crossed her arms. "Still boring!"
Alice chuckled. "She says that even when nothing’s wrong."
Lenavira’s lips curved slightly. "She says it when everything’s wrong too."
Lily pointed at them both. "Hey!"
Max watched them for a moment and let out a light breath. For once, his mind didn’t jump straight to cultivation, battles, or enemies.
The Dimension of Genesis wasn’t a place he had to "enter" anymore. It was just where he came when he needed quiet. And Alice and Lenavira were already part of that quiet.

The days that followed were calm. Max didn’t spend every moment cultivating. Sometimes he walked with Alice beside the spiritual lake while she asked him about the conference, about Orion’s excitement, Rakan’s stubbornness, Damian’s sword, Revona’s terrifying Null Origin Tide, and Ervin’s final forbidden spear.

Sometimes Lenavira sat with him under an ancient tree on one of the floating islands, talking about the deeper meaning behind the Primordial Race’s arrival and what kind of test he might face in the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
Lily followed everywhere. Not quietly. She hovered, spun, complained, laughed, and occasionally tried to "help" by dramatically explaining things she barely understood.

At one point, she even tried to copy Max’s serious expression while floating upside down. Alice laughed so hard she nearly fell off the platform. Lenavira just shook her head, though her eyes stayed warm.

Max didn’t mind. For these few days, the outside world faded. There was no Cosmic Ascension Conference. No Aurelian. No stolen bloodline source. No imprisoned parents. No Primordial envoy waiting outside. Just the people close to him and the quiet passing of time inside the Dimension of Genesis.

During those three days, Max also did a fair bit of business. He first met up with Lucia and Isabella, then had a deep talk with Lucia about Crown and about how he was building his own force and would need people he could trust.
In the end, Max invited Lucia into Crown, and she accepted.
After that, Max told Isabella, Lucia, Jonathan, and Julie to keep working the plan of recruiting other geniuses using his name.

Now that Max had become the strongest genius in the Divine Realm, almost everyone would have heard of him. That was exactly the plan he’d had from the start: use his fame to pull people into his own force.
While all this was happening, Max’s cultivation didn’t sit still either.
In truth, his foundation had already reached its limit long before the final battle. Throughout the entire Cosmic Ascension Conference, Max had stood at the very peak of the Law Awakening Realm.
His accumulation was far beyond what ordinary geniuses could match.

Every battle had tempered him, and every clash with a Pseudo Cosmic Path had sharpened his understanding. Every life-and-death exchange against opponents like Revona, Damian, and Ervin had forced his laws, body, soul, and sword path to refine themselves again and again.

He hadn’t broken through during the conference simply because the timing hadn’t been right. He’d suppressed it. He’d controlled it. But now, in the calm of the Dimension of Genesis, the barrier finally loosened on its own.

chapters.title: Chapter 1934: Law Refinement Realm level 1
paragraphs: On the third day, Max sat cross-legged on a floating island above a sea of silver mist. Alice and Lenavira were nearby as always, not watching from a distance like outsiders but simply there as part of the space itself.
Lily hovered above Max’s shoulder, swinging her legs in the air like a kid waiting for something interesting to happen.

Around Max, the laws of the Dimension of Genesis began to gather. At first the movement was gentle. Then it grew vast. Strands of law energy rose from every direction, circling him like countless rivers returning to their source.

The Law Awakening Realm was the stage where cultivators first sensed the deeper laws of the world, and Max had already reached its limit. Now his body, soul, and inner world weren’t just awakening to laws anymore. They were refining them.
The barrier shattered silently.
Boom!
A vast aura burst out of Max’s body. The Dimension of Genesis trembled softly, not from danger, but in response.
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 1st Level.]

Max opened his eyes. For a moment, his pupils seemed to hold countless flowing laws. His aura was no longer wild. It had grown deeper, more condensed, more refined. The power inside him no longer felt newly awakened.
It felt like something being sharpened, purified, and folded into his foundation.
Alice smiled immediately. "You broke through."
Lenavira nodded calmly. "Law Refinement Realm, first level."
Lily clapped her hands excitedly. "Finally! That took forever!"
Max slowly stood, and the moment he did, his Pseudo Cosmic Paths responded.

First came the Emotion Severing Path. A cold, silent sword aura spread from him, but it was no longer rough or unstable. It had become cleaner, more precise, more complete. Every edge felt like it knew exactly what it was meant to cut.
Lily leaned forward curiously. "Ooooh, it feels sharper."

Then Divine King Punishment stirred. Seven-colored lightning flickered above Max’s palm. The thunder no longer felt like raw wrath alone. It carried structure now, as if a divine tribunal was slowly taking shape inside it, and the authority behind it had deepened.
Lily’s eyes widened. "That one looks scary now."

Then the Devouring Flames Domain woke up. Black flames appeared around Max’s fingers, silent and controlled. They no longer burned wildly. They devoured with precision, like something that had learned patience.
Lily immediately hid behind Alice. "I don’t like that one."
Alice laughed softly. "You’re the one who always gets too close."

The three Pseudo Cosmic Paths rose around Max at once. The Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, and the Devouring Flames Domain, along with other auras that also kept rising around his body.
Lenavira watched quietly. "They’re nearing completion."
Max could feel it too. They were close. But not complete.
Lily peeked out again, serious for once. "You’re still far from finishing them. Even if they look close, they’re not real Cosmic Paths yet."
Alice tilted her head. "What’s missing?"
Lily puffed her cheeks. "Everything important!"
Max closed his hand, and the paths sank back into his body.
"So they’re nearing completion," he said quietly.

Lily nodded. "Yes. But only on the edge. My inheritance memories told me a lot about the cosmic paths. You can refine them, strengthen them, make them scarier, but completing them before the Divine Lord Realm is impossible."
Alice looked at him. "Even for you?"
Lily shook her head firmly. "Especially for him. The stronger the path, the harder it gets. And his are weirdly strong."
Lenavira’s gaze softened. "So Law Refinement Realm only made them more stable."
Max nodded. "That’s enough for now."
He could feel the difference clearly. A stronger body. Sharper laws. More refined control. And Pseudo Cosmic Paths that had stepped closer to something far greater.
Alice smiled. "You just became champion, broke through, and now you’re already getting stronger again. People outside would lose their minds."
Max gave a faint smile. "Then they don’t need to know."
Lily immediately pointed at him. "Yes! That’s right! We hide it!"
Alice looked at her. "You’re very enthusiastic about hiding things."
Lily nodded proudly. "It’s fun!"
Lenavira sighed softly. "That’s not a good reason."
Lily stuck her tongue out.
"It’s about time. I should leave with the envoy of the Primordial Race," Max said suddenly. "Three days have passed."
The mention of the Primordial Race settled the mood right away. The envoy would be waiting. The road to the Primordial Ancestral Domain was about to open.
Max looked toward the distant sky of the Dimension of Genesis, where countless stars shimmered over the sea of mist. The quiet days were ending. He turned back toward them.
"I’ll visit you all later."

Alice and Lenavira both nodded solemnly. They understood that Max’s trip to the Primordial Race would matter a great deal. This wasn’t a simple reward trip, and it wasn’t just about accepting a title.

The Primordial Race stood above countless ancient bloodlines in the Divine Realm, and the chance to officially receive their bloodline and step onto the path of becoming a Primordial was something even supreme clans would dream of for their strongest descendants.
Alice looked at him for a few breaths, then smiled softly. "Be careful."

Lenavira’s gaze was calmer, but the worry in her eyes wasn’t hidden. "Don’t trust everything too easily. The Primordial Race may be handing you a reward, but a reward from a race like that is never simple."
Max nodded. "I know."
Lily floated in front of him and put both hands on her waist, trying to look serious despite her small size. "Come back soon."
"I will," Max said with a smile.
Lily’s serious look melted away immediately. "You better."

Max looked at Alice, Lenavira, and Lily one last time. The Dimension of Genesis stayed quiet around them, and for a moment, he felt the strange contrast between this peaceful world and the storm waiting outside.

Here, Alice and Lenavira had already become part of his life in a way that needed no explaining. Lily still acted noisy and childish, but she was also one of the few beings who understood the depth of his secrets.
Leaving them for this trip wasn’t hard because he feared for himself. It was hard because he knew every step forward would bring him closer to greater danger.
Still, he had to go.

chapters.title: Chapter 1935: Leaving!
paragraphs: A moment later, Max vanished from the Dimension of Genesis.

When he returned to the Black Dragon Clan, the mood outside had already turned solemn. Sarvion, the envoy of the Primordial Race, was waiting near the main transfer square, standing calmly under the protection of several ancient formations.

His silver-black hair moved slightly in the wind, and his violet-gold ringed eyes held a depth ordinary cultivators couldn’t stare into for long. He didn’t look impatient. He simply stood there, as if three days were nothing more than a blink to him.
He wasn’t alone, though. Many members of the Black Dragon Clan had gathered to see Max off.
Lady Virelia stood at the front, wearing the formal insignia of the 33rd hall at her waist. After becoming one of the thirty-six hall masters, her authority in the clan had clearly grown.
The elders near her treated her with far more respect than before, but her attention wasn’t on them. Her eyes were on Max the moment he appeared.
Mathew Grimes stood nearby too, along with several family heads and high-ranking elders. Behind them stood rows of elite disciples, inner clan members, and guards, all quiet.

The earlier celebration had already ended, but the pride in their eyes hadn’t faded. If anything, watching Max prepare to leave for the Primordial Race made them even more aware of how far he’d risen.

A mortal genius chosen by Lady Virelia had entered the Divine Realm. That same genius had become champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. Now he was being personally escorted by an envoy of the Primordial Race to receive the conference’s greatest reward.
For the Black Dragon Clan, this was glory. For Max, it was just another step.
Lady Virelia walked toward him first. "You’re leaving alone?"
Max nodded. "The envoy came for me. No need for anyone else to come along."
Virelia looked at him quietly for a moment. "The Primordial Ancestral Domain isn’t a place the Black Dragon Clan can easily step into. Once you’re on their territory, most of this will be up to you."
"I understand."

"Then remember one thing," Virelia said, her voice calm but serious. "A reward strong enough to change your race and your foundation is never without risk. Don’t let the name of the Primordials blind you."
Max smiled faintly. "I won’t."

Mathew Grimes laughed, though there was concern under it. "You brat, you just became champion and now you’re already off somewhere even more troublesome. Can’t you let the clan enjoy your win a little longer?"
Max looked at him. "The Primordials only gave me three days."
Mathew clicked his tongue. "Exactly. Arrogant old beings."
A few elders nearby coughed lightly at that, but Sarvion didn’t react. It was as if he hadn’t heard a word.
Max looked toward the gathered disciples. The moment his eyes swept over them, many straightened up at once.
"Senior Brother Max, come back safe!"
"Become a Primordial and shock the Divine Realm again!"
"Don’t forget the Black Dragon Clan!"
"Senior Brother Max, we’ll wait for your return!"

Their voices rose one after another until the whole transfer square filled with sound again. It wasn’t as wild as the celebration after his return from the conference, but it carried something deeper. There was excitement, pride, respect, and a faint reluctance to see him leave so soon after his biggest win.
Max gave them a slight nod. "I’ll return."
Those three words were simple, but the disciples cheered again anyway.
Lady Virelia stepped back slightly.
Sarvion finally moved. "Max Morgan, it’s time."
Max turned toward him. "Let’s go."

Sarvion raised one hand, and the space above the transfer square changed instantly. It didn’t tear open violently like an ordinary spatial passage. Instead, countless violet-gold lines spread across the sky in an elegant pattern, forming a gate that looked carved from ancient starlight.

The gate’s aura felt strange. It wasn’t just connecting two places. It felt like it was opening a road through a higher layer of space, one guarded by laws that ordinary divine powers couldn’t easily touch.
The moment the gate appeared, many elders of the Black Dragon Clan grew solemn. Even Lady Virelia’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Sarvion looked at Max. "This path leads to the outer reception boundary of the Primordial Ancestral Domain. Once we pass through, you’ll be under the Primordial Race’s watch."
Max nodded, then stepped forward.
Before entering the gate, he looked back once. Lady Virelia, Mathew Grimes, the elders, the disciples, and countless members of the Black Dragon Clan were all watching him.
The black and gold dragon banners above the square moved in the wind, and the huge formations around the clan glowed softly, as if sending him off.
Max turned back and entered the violet-gold gate with Sarvion.

The world changed. For a short while, there was no ground under his feet and no sky above his head. Max walked through a passage filled with streams of starlight, ancient symbols, and faint echoes of laws that seemed older than most inheritances he’d ever seen.
Sarvion walked ahead of him, his robe shifting between darkness and light with every step. The passage was silent, but Max could feel countless hidden restrictions around them.
Anyone who tried to force their way into this route would likely be erased before they even understood what they’d touched.
After a while, the starlight passage opened, and Max stepped out.
The moment he emerged, his eyes changed slightly.

Before him stood the land of the Primordial Race. It didn’t look like an ordinary territory. There was no single city, no normal mountain range, no simple palace complex. The whole region seemed to sit somewhere between ancient creation and divine order.
Vast continents floated in the sky, connected by bridges of light stretching across impossible distances. Rivers of liquid starlight flowed through the void between them.
Mountains taller than entire worlds rose from the edges of floating landmasses, and above it all, enormous rings of ancient runes rotated slowly, like wheels of law guarding the whole domain.

sentences.text: A moment later, Max vanished from the Dimension of Genesis.
When he returned to the Black Dragon Clan, the mood outside had already turned solemn.
Sarvion, the envoy of the Primordial Race, was waiting near the main transfer square, standing calmly under the protection of several ancient formations.
His silver-black hair moved slightly in the wind, and his violet-gold ringed eyes held a depth ordinary cultivators couldn’t stare into for long.
He didn’t look impatient.
He simply stood there, as if three days were nothing more than a blink to him.
He wasn’t alone, though.
Many members of the Black Dragon Clan had gathered to see Max off.
Lady Virelia stood at the front, wearing the formal insignia of the 33rd hall at her waist.
After becoming one of the thirty-six hall masters, her authority in the clan had clearly grown.
The elders near her treated her with far more respect than before, but her attention wasn’t on them.
Her eyes were on Max the moment he appeared.
Mathew Grimes stood nearby too, along with several family heads and high-ranking elders.
Behind them stood rows of elite disciples, inner clan members, and guards, all quiet.
The earlier celebration had already ended, but the pride in their eyes hadn’t faded.
If anything, watching Max prepare to leave for the Primordial Race made them even more aware of how far he’d risen.
A mortal genius chosen by Lady Virelia had entered the Divine Realm.
That same genius had become champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Now he was being personally escorted by an envoy of the Primordial Race to receive the conference’s greatest reward.
For the Black Dragon Clan, this was glory.
For Max, it was just another step.
Lady Virelia walked toward him first.
"You’re leaving alone?"
Max nodded.
"The envoy came for me.
No need for anyone else to come along."
Virelia looked at him quietly for a moment.
"The Primordial Ancestral Domain isn’t a place the Black Dragon Clan can easily step into.
Once you’re on their territory, most of this will be up to you."
"I understand."
"Then remember one thing," Virelia said, her voice calm but serious.
"A reward strong enough to change your race and your foundation is never without risk.
Don’t let the name of the Primordials blind you."
Max smiled faintly.
"I won’t."
Mathew Grimes laughed, though there was concern under it.
"You brat, you just became champion and now you’re already off somewhere even more troublesome.
Can’t you let the clan enjoy your win a little longer?"
Max looked at him.
"The Primordials only gave me three days."
Mathew clicked his tongue.
"Exactly.

A few elders nearby coughed lightly at that, but Sarvion didn’t react.
It was as if he hadn’t heard a word.
Max looked toward the gathered disciples.
The moment his eyes swept over them, many straightened up at once.

"Become a Primordial and shock the Divine Realm again!"
"Don’t forget the Black Dragon Clan!"
"Senior Brother Max, we’ll wait for your return!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1936: Primordial Ancestral Domain
paragraphs: The energy here was incredibly dense. It wasn’t just divine energy. It was older, heavier, more primal. Every breath carried a strange pressure, as if the air itself held fragments of a beginning from before most races had ever been born.

Far in the distance, Max saw a colossal palace big enough to hold a world inside it. Its pillars were carved with images of ancient beings standing above stars, suns, moons, dragons, phoenixes, titans, and countless other races. The palace didn’t give off any overbearing pressure, yet Max could feel it was watching everything.
Sarvion stopped beside him. "Welcome to the Primordial Ancestral Domain."
Max looked out across the floating continents. "So this is where the Primordial Race lives."
"One of our ancestral domains," Sarvion corrected calmly. "Not the only one."
Max’s eyes flickered slightly. One of them. That alone said something about how deep the Primordial Race’s foundation went.

Sarvion kept walking, and Max followed him across a bridge of violet-gold light. As they got closer to the central reception platform, Max sensed several powerful auras gathering ahead. They weren’t old experts. Their vitality was young, but each aura carried a familiarity Max recognized from the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
When he reached the reception platform, he saw them.

Nine young geniuses were already waiting there. Revona stood quietly near the edge of the platform, her pale eyes half-open and unreadable. Damian Voss stood with his sword at his waist, calm and refined as always.

Ervin leaned slightly on his restored black spear, his expression faintly amused when he saw Max arrive. Orion Starfall crossed his arms with a bright smile, while Rakan Thorne grinned like he was already hoping something exciting would happen. Kaiden Voidmere stood silently, his silver-gray gaze fixed on the space around him.

Aurelian Lareth stood farther off, his expression controlled but stiff the moment Max showed up. Rosaline Lunara and Morgana Starveil were there too, rounding out the top ten geniuses the Primordials had chosen.
The moment Max stepped onto the platform, all nine of them turned toward him. For a brief moment, the air went still.
These were the top ten geniuses of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. Each of them had fought through countless battles.

Each had revealed a Pseudo Cosmic Path or a terrifying foundation. Each was strong enough to represent the very top of the younger generation in the Divine Realm. And now, all of them had been gathered by the Primordial Race.
Orion spoke first. "Champion, you finally arrived."
Rakan laughed loudly. "He had to arrive last. Otherwise how would everyone remember he’s the champion?"
Morgana smiled faintly. "That does sound like something fate would arrange."
Damian gave Max a slight nod. "Max."
Ervin smiled lightly. "You look stronger than before."
Revona’s eyes moved across Max once, and for a brief instant her gaze sharpened. She didn’t say anything, but Max could tell she’d sensed something different.
His breakthrough into the Law Refinement Realm wasn’t easy to hide from someone with the Void Origin Eyes, even if she couldn’t see everything clearly.
Aurelian said nothing. His eyes stayed on Max one breath too long before he looked away.
Max noticed but didn’t bother responding.
’All of them are at the very peak of the Law Manifestation Realm. Just one step from the Divine Lord Realm.’

He thought quietly to himself. He’d beaten every one of them, sure, but that had happened inside the Eternal Hourglass, where all their cultivation had been suppressed down to the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
Now that their cultivation wasn’t held back, Max knew he’d stand no chance against any single one of them.
Sarvion stepped forward and addressed all ten of them.
"The top ten of the Cosmic Ascension Conference have now gathered."
The platform fell silent. Sarvion’s voice carried across the ancient reception ground.

"You’ve all been chosen by the Primordial Race. Each of you will get a chance to receive the Primordial bloodline and step onto the path of becoming a Primordial. Your ranking in the conference will decide the level of opportunity, the depth of ceremony access, and how much reward you’re permitted to attempt."
His gaze moved to Max.
"As the champion, Max Morgan will receive the highest opportunity."
The other nine stayed quiet, though their expressions shifted in different ways. Some looked calm. Some looked curious. Some looked competitive. Aurelian’s eyes darkened faintly.
Max only looked toward the colossal palace in the distance. The Primordial Ancestral Domain stretched out before him, ancient and unfathomable.
The reception platform stayed silent after Sarvion finished speaking.

The ten geniuses stood under the sky of the Primordial Ancestral Domain, surrounded by floating continents, ancient rune rings, rivers of starlight, and a pressure so old that even their powerful foundations felt smaller than usual here. None of them were ordinary.

Everyone standing on this platform had made the top ten of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, and each had fought through countless battles to reach this place. Yet inside the Primordial Race’s territory, even their pride instinctively quieted down.

Max looked toward the colossal palace in the distance. It seemed to exist beyond its own size. From one angle it looked like a divine structure spread across a continent. From another, it looked like a throne hall standing above the beginning of time.

The pillars were carved with images of ancient races bowing, stars collapsing, worlds being born, and four towering figures standing at the center of it all, like rulers of an age no one else had witnessed.

Before Max could study it any further, the air above the reception platform changed. It didn’t tear. It didn’t distort. It simply went still. The rivers of starlight stopped flowing for a breath. The rotating rune rings above slowed down.
Even the ancient pressure of the domain seemed to lower itself, as if welcoming someone who stood above ordinary authority.
Sarvion bowed immediately. "Primarch."
The moment that word left his mouth, the expressions of all ten young geniuses changed.
Primarch. The leaders of the Primordial Race. There were only four of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 1937: Secrets of Void Origin Eyes!
paragraphs: Before Sarvion could say anything else, a figure appeared before the platform. He didn’t arrive through a gate. He didn’t descend from the sky. He was like he was already standing there for a long time.
The man wore a long robe woven from pale gold and deep violet light, and each thread of that robe seemed to hold an ancient rune moving on its own.

His hair was long and white-gold, falling behind him like a river of dawn, while his eyes carried four rotating rings of different colors, each one giving off the feeling of an ancient law refined down to its absolute limit. His face looked young, but the depth in his gaze made him seem older than the Divine Realm itself.

The moment Max saw him, his eyes narrowed slightly. He recognized this person. Not from the Cosmic Ascension Conference. Not from the Black Dragon Clan. But from the temporal domain on Orion’s planet.
Back then, through the strange temporal connection inside that domain, Max had seen the last user of the Dimensional Keeper legacy and had also caught the shadow of the Primordials.
Among them had been four terrifying figures standing above the Primordial Race like pillars holding up an ancient sky.
This man was one of them. One of the four Primarchs.
The Primarch’s gaze swept across the ten geniuses. No pressure came off him, but everyone on the platform felt seen clearly. Not judged. Not suppressed. Just seen.
Their cultivation, bloodline, soul, Pseudo Cosmic Paths, wounds, secrets, and hidden potential all seemed to pass under his gaze in a single instant.
Even Revona’s eyes widened slightly. Damian Voss lowered his gaze out of respect. Ervin’s relaxed expression disappeared.
Orion Starfall’s easy smile vanished.
Rakan Thorne went unusually quiet.
Kaiden Voidmere’s pupils contracted faintly.
Aurelian Lareth straightened at once, clearly aware that no amount of elven pride meant anything in front of a Primarch of the Primordial Race.
The Primarch finally spoke. "I am Arvantos, one of the four Primarchs of the Primordial Race."
His voice wasn’t loud, but it carried across the whole reception platform and seemed to echo inside the ancient rune rings above them.

"You’ve all fought well in the Cosmic Ascension Conference. Each of you has shown talent, foundation, will, and a path worth my race’s attention. Reaching the top ten wasn’t just about winning fights. It also proved that your power has already stepped beyond the ordinary limits of the younger generation."
His eyes moved across them one by one. Then Arvantos’s gaze landed on Revona.
"And Revona."
The platform quieted further. Revona looked at him calmly.
Finally, the Primarch’s eyes shifted to Max.
"And Max Morgan." A faint smile crossed Arvantos’s face. "The champion."
That word tightened the atmosphere again. Max met his gaze without lowering his head.
Arvantos looked at him for several breaths, then said something that made every genius on the platform freeze.
"I’ll be honest. Before the final stage ended, I believed this conference would be won by Revona."
Silence fell. Not ordinary silence. Complete silence. Even Sarvion stood motionless.

The Primarch continued calmly, as if he hadn’t just said something shocking. "In fact, I didn’t just think she had a good chance of winning. I never seriously considered that anyone in this conference could beat her."
The nine other geniuses immediately turned toward Revona. Even Max looked at her with a flicker of interest.

Revona stayed calm. Her pale eyes didn’t ripple, and her expression didn’t change at all. She stood there as if Arvantos were talking about someone else entirely. It wasn’t arrogance. It wasn’t indifference either. It was the kind of calm that made her seem disconnected from ordinary surprise.
Orion Starfall frowned slightly. "You never thought anyone could beat her?"
Rakan Thorne couldn’t hold back. "Even with Damian, Ervin, Max, Kaiden, and the rest of us there?"
Arvantos looked at him calmly. "Yes."
The blunt answer made Rakan’s expression stiffen.
Damian Voss’s eyes narrowed. "Because of her Void Origin Eyes?"
"Because of the true secret of the Void Origin Eyes," Arvantos corrected.
The moment he said that, Revona’s gaze finally shifted slightly. Not in panic. Not in shock. Just acknowledgment.

Arvantos looked at the group and went on. "The Void Origin Eyes aren’t just a powerful pair of eyes that can nullify, hollow, trace, and return power to nothing. Those are only the abilities you saw in battle. Their deeper mystery runs far more terrifying than that."
The ancient rune rings above the platform rotated slowly.
"It’s said the holder of the Void Origin Eyes never truly dies."
The geniuses’ expressions changed again.

Arvantos continued. "In old history, that saying was always treated as a half-myth. Some believed it meant the Void Origin Eyes could preserve the soul. Some believed the eye bloodline would just reappear in later generations. Some believed it was pure exaggeration born from fear. But Revona is a living example that it’s true."
He paused, then revealed the secret.
"Revona is a reincarnated person."
The whole platform went heavy.
Aurelian’s expression changed drastically. "Reincarnated?"
Arvantos nodded. "Not once. Not twice. Over and over. Generation after generation. Body after body. Era after era."
The shock spreading across the top ten was impossible to hide. Even those with the deepest composure felt their hearts skip. A person who reincarnated once was already shocking enough to most forces.

A person who reincarnated repeatedly, keeping memories and experience intact, was something far beyond ordinary understanding. That wasn’t just talent anymore. That was accumulation across generations.

Arvantos looked at Revona again. "The Revona standing here isn’t just a young genius who awakened the Void Origin Eyes in this generation. She’s the same existence as the people who awakened those eyes before her. Different bodies. Different eras. Different identities. But the same person."
Every gaze turned back to Revona. She just stood there quietly, her expression as calm as ever, as if this revelation had nothing to do with her.

Arvantos went on. "Nobody knows the full mystery behind this reincarnation. Not even the Primordial Race has fully uncovered its source. What we do know is that it’s tied to the Void Origin Eyes. Whenever the eyes awaken in a new body, memories of past lives start waking up too. At first they come back as fragments. Then as dreams. Then as instincts. Then as full experience."
He looked at Max. "That’s why I believed she would win."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
