She just stood there quietly, her expression as calm as ever, as if this revelation had nothing to do with her.
Arvantos went on.
"Nobody knows the full mystery behind this reincarnation.
Not even the Primordial Race has fully uncovered its source.
What we do know is that it’s tied to the Void Origin Eyes.
Whenever the eyes awaken in a new body, memories of past lives start waking up too.
At first they come back as fragments.
Then as dreams.
Then as instincts.
Then as full experience."
He looked at Max.
"That’s why I believed she would win."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1938: Perfect Beings!
paragraphs: Arvantos’s voice stayed steady. "During the Cosmic Ascension Conference, most geniuses were drawing on the accumulation of a single life. Revona wasn’t. Her Void Origin Eyes kept awakening further with every battle, and with each awakening, more memories and experience from her past lives came back to her. Her battle instincts, her grasp of power, her sense of danger, her use of nullification, all of it was backed by far more than her current age."
The top ten fell into stunned silence.
Now Revona’s frightening calm made a lot more sense.

The way she’d adapted to Orion’s star power. The way she’d traced Kaiden’s Grand Void Labyrinth. The way she’d forced Max to reveal power after power. The way she’d beaten Ervin and Damian with Null Origin Tide after being pushed to the brink. All of it suddenly felt even more terrifying.
She hadn’t just been talented. She’d been remembering.
Morgana Starveil looked at Revona with deep curiosity. "So the woman standing beside us is the same person who’s lived through countless past lives?"
"Yes," Arvantos answered.
Rakan Thorne stared at Revona, then scratched his head with a complicated look. "That feels like cheating."
Orion Starfall let out a faint laugh, though his eyes stayed serious. "If it’s cheating, it’s the most elegant kind I’ve ever seen."
Kaiden Voidmere looked at Revona and asked, "Do you remember everything?"
Revona finally spoke. "Not everything." Her voice was calm. "But enough."
That single word made the platform even quieter.
Enough.

Enough to become the person the Primarch had expected to win the entire Cosmic Ascension Conference. Enough to make the Primordial Race believe no one should be able to beat her. Enough to make every genius present realize her loss to Max was even more shocking than they’d first thought.
Ervin slowly let out a breath. "No wonder you defeated almost all of us."
Revona didn’t reply to him. She only looked at Max. Max looked back at her. Their gazes met quietly.
Arvantos smiled faintly when he saw that. "That’s why Max Morgan surprised me."
His voice pulled everyone’s attention back to him.

"Revona was the person I expected to become champion. Her Void Origin Eyes, combined with the awakening of her past-life memories, should have put her beyond anyone else in this conference. Yet Max beat her. Then he beat Damian. Then he beat Ervin. And he finished with a perfect record."
The Primarch’s eyes settled on Max.
"So, Max Morgan, your win wasn’t impressive just because you became champion. It was impressive because you beat the one person even I believed shouldn’t lose."

The weight of those words was enormous. The other geniuses looked at Max differently now. They’d already known he was strong. They’d already accepted he was champion. But hearing one of the four Primarchs say he’d expected Revona to be unbeatable made Max’s win feel even more abnormal.
Max stayed calm. After a moment he smiled faintly. "So she was even more trouble than I thought."
Revona looked at him quietly. "You still won."
Max replied, "Barely."
Revona didn’t respond, but for the first time, a faint trace of something almost like amusement crossed her pale eyes.
Arvantos watched the exchange, then turned back to the whole group.

"You should all remember this. The Primordial Race didn’t gather you here just because you won battles. We gathered you because each of you carries something worth testing, refining, and possibly transforming. Some of you have ancient bloodlines. Some have rare Pseudo Cosmic Paths. Some have inheritances. Some have special bodies. Some have secrets even your own forces don’t fully understand."
His gaze swept over them again. "And now, you’ll each be given a chance to step beyond what you were born as."
The mood on the platform turned solemn again. The secret of Revona’s reincarnation still hung in everyone’s mind, but the bigger reason they’d come here was pressing down on them once more.
The Primordial bloodline. The path to becoming a Primordial. The reward promised to the top ten.
Arvantos raised one hand, and the colossal palace in the distance began to shine.
"Come," he said. "The Primordial Selection Ceremony will begin soon."

Arvantos turned and walked toward the distant palace. The ten geniuses followed. Sarvion stayed behind them, silent and respectful, while the reception platform slowly moved forward on its own. It wasn’t flying in any normal sense.

The whole platform seemed to slide along a hidden law path, crossing bridges of violet-gold light, passing over rivers of liquid starlight, and pushing deeper into the Primordial Ancestral Domain with every breath.

As they traveled, the true scale of the Primordial Race’s territory unfolded before them. What they’d seen from the outer reception boundary had only been the surface. The deeper they went, the more impossible the domain became.
Some floating continents held ancient forests where every tree stood taller than mountains. Some held silent lakes that reflected not the sky above but scenes from different eras.

Some were covered in ruins large enough to make divine cities look like toys, and on the broken walls of those ruins were carvings of beings whose faces resembled humans, yet whose presence felt far more ancient and complete.

Max looked at those carvings quietly. The beings shown there were tall, flawless, and powerful. Their bodies were shaped like human bodies, but their eyes held strange rings, their bloodline marks ran far deeper, and their very posture carried a natural supremacy no ordinary divine race could imitate.
Arvantos noticed their stares and spoke without turning back. "You’re looking at the earliest Primordials."
The ten geniuses immediately paid closer attention. Even Revona, who’d stayed calm through the reveal of her reincarnation, looked at the carvings with a flicker of interest.
Arvantos went on. "Before humans existed, before most races of the current universe had built stable civilizations, the Primordial Race already existed."

His voice was calm, but the words carried enough weight to quiet the whole platform. "Back then, we were the first complete race born from the ancient source of existence. Our bodies were powerful. Our souls were stable. Our grasp of law came naturally from birth. Compared to many races that came later, the Primordials could be called perfect beings, in a certain sense."
Rakan Thorne frowned slightly. "Perfect beings?"
Arvantos smiled faintly. "In strength, foundation, and closeness to the laws of existence, yes. But perfection in one direction often creates a flaw in another."

chapters.title: Chapter 1939: Origin of Human Race!
paragraphs: The platform passed through a great ring of ancient runes. Beyond it, the landscape changed again. They saw a vast mural stretched across the side of a floating mountain, showing countless Primordials standing together beneath a sky full of stars.
They looked magnificent, but there were no children among them. No families. No lines of descent. Just adults standing under the ancient heavens with solemn expressions.
Arvantos stopped before that mural. "This was the flaw of the Primordial Race."
The ten geniuses waited. Then Arvantos said it plainly.
"We could not reproduce."
The words changed almost everyone’s expression.
Orion Starfall blinked. "The Primordial Race couldn’t reproduce?"
Damian Voss’s gaze sharpened slightly.
Kaiden Voidmere looked at the mural again, as if trying to figure out whether the missing children had been intentional.
Morgana Starveil’s purple eyes glimmered with curiosity. "A race that can’t reproduce shouldn’t have survived through the ages."
Arvantos nodded. "That’s correct."
He turned toward them slightly, and for the first time a wry smile crossed his face.

"We had long lives, supreme strength, and bodies that naturally held laws other races had to spend countless years learning. Yet we couldn’t create descendants. It was as if some limit had been placed on us the moment we were born."
Rosaline Lunara frowned. "A natural law limitation?"

"Maybe," Arvantos said. "Or maybe something imposed by entities beyond the understanding of even the earliest Primordials. Some of our oldest records call it a restriction. Some call it a punishment. Some call it the decision of gods. The truth’s never been fully confirmed."
Aurelian Lareth couldn’t help but ask, "Did the Primordials try to reproduce with other races?"
Arvantos looked at him calmly. "Of course."
The blunt answer quieted the platform again.

"The Primordials tried everything. We tried with our own race first. Nothing came of it. Later, when other races started appearing, we tried with them too. Humans didn’t exist yet in that era, but there were plenty of early races born from worlds, stars, beasts, spirits, laws, and other sources. The result was always the same." He paused. "No child was born."
The shock in the ten geniuses’ eyes deepened. To them, the Primordial Race had always stood as a supreme race above nearly everything.
They’d assumed the Primordials were ancient simply because they’d existed a long time, not because the race itself had once been trapped in a fatal inability to continue.

Arvantos turned back to the mural. "At first, we thought time would solve it. Then we thought power would. Then law. After that, we tried secret arts, soul division, bloodline imitation, body creation, artificial wombs, divine law fusion, reincarnation attempts, and countless other methods that later races couldn’t even imagine."
His wry smile faded. "All of it failed."
The silence grew heavier. Even Rakan, who usually reacted loudly to everything, said nothing.

Arvantos continued. "A race that can’t reproduce might look invincible for a while, especially if its members are strong enough. But even immortality isn’t absolute. Primordials could die in battle. Primordials could fall to disasters. Primordials could vanish inside forbidden zones. Primordials could be sealed, corrupted, or lost in ancient wars. We were powerful, but our numbers only shrank."

The platform started moving again, this time toward another region where a different set of murals appeared. These carvings showed Primordials seated in a great circle, their bodies glowing with bloodline light.
At the center of the circle stood a vast basin filled with golden-red liquid, and from that basin, countless streams flowed out toward smaller figures. The smaller figures looked human.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Arvantos stopped before the second mural. "Eventually, the Primordials chose the most extreme method." His voice dropped slightly. "We gave up our bloodline."
The ten geniuses froze. Even Max’s expression shifted a little.

Arvantos looked at the human-like figures carved beneath the Primordials. "The first humans were born when some Primordials gave up their complete bloodline, sealed away their Primordial foundation, and let themselves fall into mortality. They lost the natural supremacy of the Primordial Race. Their bodies grew weaker. Their lifespans shortened. Their connection to the ancient source faded. Their law affinity declined. In exchange, they gained something the Primordials had never had."
He paused. "The ability to reproduce."
A heavy silence settled over the platform. The ten geniuses stared at the mural.

The birth of the human race had plenty of legends across the Divine Realm. Some believed humans were created by ancient gods. Some believed they evolved from mortal life forms. Some believed they were fragments of a fallen supreme race. Some believed they were just one of countless ordinary races that rose through struggle. But none of them had expected this.

Humans had come from Primordials. Not as descendants in the ordinary sense. Not as a branch race born naturally. But as Primordials who had abandoned their bloodline entirely and turned themselves into mortals.
Rosaline covered her mouth slightly, unable to hide her shock. "Humans were once Primordials?"
"The earliest humans were," Arvantos answered.
Kaiden Voidmere stared at the mural with a deep gaze. "That explains the resemblance."
"Yes," Arvantos said. "Humans resemble Primordials because humans were shaped from Primordials. The outer form didn’t change much, but the foundation did."
Damian Voss said quietly, "So humanity isn’t a lesser copy of the Primordial Race. It’s a fallen branch."
"A transformed branch," Arvantos corrected. "Fallen is a harsh word, though some ancient Primordials used it at the time."
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly, though her eyes stayed serious. "And humans became capable of having children."

"Yes." Arvantos looked back at the mural. "Once the Primordials who’d given up their bloodline became human, they found out they could bear children. Those children didn’t carry the true Primordial bloodline. They were human. Mortal. Weaker than their origin. But they could grow, multiply, spread, adapt, and survive in ways the Primordial Race never could."
Orion Starfall let out a slow breath. "So that was the start of the human race."

"The start of the true human race," Arvantos replied. "From those first mortals, humanity spread across worlds, star regions, and later the Divine Realm. They were weaker than a lot of ancient races at birth, but they had terrifying adaptability. They could cultivate many paths. They could awaken many bloodlines. They could intermarry with other races. They could rise from nothing again and again."
Rakan Thorne scratched his head, genuinely shaken. "So humans exist because the strongest race in existence couldn’t have kids?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1940: Compatability Test!
paragraphs: Arvantos smiled wryly again. "That’s one simple way to put it."
The words came out almost casual, but the meaning behind them shook the top ten deeply. Aurelian Lareth’s expression turned complicated.

The elven races had always taken pride in their bloodline purity, but standing in the Primordial Ancestral Domain and hearing that humans came from Primordials themselves, even he couldn’t hold onto the same sense of superiority.
Revona stayed calm, but her gaze lingered on the mural longer than before.

Ervin looked thoughtful. "Then the current Primordial Race should have kept declining. If the original Primordials couldn’t reproduce, and a lot of them turned into humans, how did your race survive until now?"
Arvantos’s smile faded into something deeper. "That’s where the second half of our history begins."

The platform moved again. This time they approached a vast ceremonial ground surrounded by thirteen ancient pillars. Each pillar showed a carving of a human standing beneath a Primordial, with streams of bloodline light pouring into their body.
Some of those humans transformed partially. Some fully. Some broke apart. Some stood tall with new Primordial marks carved into their skin.
Arvantos pointed at the pillars. "After humanity began, the Primordials found another path."
The ten geniuses looked at the carvings in silence.

Arvantos continued. "If Primordials couldn’t reproduce naturally, then we’d create Primordials through transformation instead. Rather than birthing descendants, we’d choose humans with supreme potential, awaken the hidden compatibility left over from the origin of humanity, and give them a chance to receive the Primordial bloodline."
His gaze moved across all ten of them. "That’s the reason you’re here."
The mood shifted immediately.

"Since this system began, the Primordial Race has picked the most outstanding human geniuses from different eras, different worlds, and different forces. Some were chosen through wars. Some through trials. Some through bloodline resonance. In the current era, the Cosmic Ascension Conference is one of the most important ways we select candidates."
Max looked at the pillars. "So the top ten get this opportunity because you’re looking for humans who can carry the Primordial bloodline."

"Correct," Arvantos said. "Not every human can carry it. Honestly, almost none can. The Primordial bloodline is too heavy for ordinary bodies and too ancient for ordinary souls. Even supreme geniuses can fail. Some get only a trace. Some get a partial bloodline. Some become candidates. A few, after many more trials, truly step into the ranks of the Primordials."

Alice and Lenavira weren’t here, but Max could almost guess what Lily would say if she heard all this. She’d probably say the Primordials were taking a ridiculously roundabout path just because they couldn’t have kids the normal way.
Orion Starfall looked at Arvantos. "So the Primordial Race has survived by turning humans back into Primordials."

"Yes," Arvantos said. "Humanity came from Primordials who gave up their bloodline, and the Primordial Race keeps going by choosing extraordinary humans capable of receiving that bloodline again. It’s a cycle, though not a perfect one."
Damian Voss’s gaze sharpened. "So humans are both the descendants of the Primordials and the source new Primordials get chosen from."
"Exactly."

The shock on the platform deepened. The history was too big, too strange, too heavy. For countless years, humans had struggled, cultivated, fought, risen, fallen, founded clans, built forces, and established kingdoms, empires, dynasties, and divine powers.
Plenty of human forces believed their origins were ordinary compared to the ancient divine races. Now Arvantos had just told them the truth was far more astonishing.
Humans were born from Primordials. And Primordials kept existing through humans.
Max stayed quiet for a while. This secret changed a lot of things. It explained why the Primordial Race cared so much about the Cosmic Ascension Conference. It explained why the top ten got chosen.
It explained why becoming a Primordial wasn’t just receiving an outside reward, but returning to a source humans had once lost.

Arvantos looked at the ten geniuses and spoke slowly. "Now you understand why the Primordial Race values potential over background. A divine clan bloodline might help you. A supreme inheritance might strengthen you. A rare Pseudo Cosmic Path might set you above others in battle. But none of that alone decides whether you can become a Primordial."
His gaze moved to Max. "What matters most is whether your foundation can bear the return."
The word "return" quieted the platform again.
Arvantos raised his hand, and the thirteen pillars around the ceremonial ground began to glow.

"This is where your first compatibility trial begins. Before any bloodline is granted, before any ceremony is performed, before any of you can be called Primordial candidates, we need to see how much of the ancient source your bodies and souls can handle."

The ten geniuses stood beneath the glowing pillars. The shock from the secret still hadn’t faded, but their eyes had already started to sharpen. Whatever their surprise, whatever they now thought about the origin of humanity, they hadn’t come here just to listen to history.
They’d come to seize an opportunity. They’d come to climb higher. And now the path back to the Primordial source was opening in front of them.
The thirteen ancient pillars around the ceremonial ground shone brighter and brighter until the whole area was drowned in pale gold light.

The moment the light hit its peak, the ground beneath the ten geniuses began to hum softly. Countless ancient runes rose up from the floor one after another, forming circles within circles beneath each of them. The air grew heavy, not with hostility, but with a deep, ancient pressure that seemed to come from the very origin of life itself.
Arvantos stood at the center of the group with his hands behind his back.

"This is the Primordial Compatibility Test," he said calmly. "It doesn’t just test combat strength, and it doesn’t care about fame, background, or a single victory. It measures your body, your soul, your bloodline adaptability, your law foundation, your life force, your capacity to withstand ancient pressure, and the depth of your future potential."
His gaze moved across all ten of them.

"The stronger your compatibility, the higher the bloodline you may be able to receive. If your compatibility is too low, even if I personally wanted to give you a higher Primordial bloodline, your body would explode, your soul would collapse, or your foundation would shatter."
The geniuses’ expressions turned solemn.

sentences.text: Arvantos smiled wryly again.
"That’s one simple way to put it."
The words came out almost casual, but the meaning behind them shook the top ten deeply.
Aurelian Lareth’s expression turned complicated.

The elven races had always taken pride in their bloodline purity, but standing in the Primordial Ancestral Domain and hearing that humans came from Primordials themselves, even he couldn’t hold onto the same sense of superiority.
Revona stayed calm, but her gaze lingered on the mural longer than before.
Ervin looked thoughtful.
"Then the current Primordial Race should have kept declining.
If the original Primordials couldn’t reproduce, and a lot of them turned into humans, how did your race survive until now?"
Arvantos’s smile faded into something deeper.
"That’s where the second half of our history begins."
The platform moved again.
This time they approached a vast ceremonial ground surrounded by thirteen ancient pillars.
Each pillar showed a carving of a human standing beneath a Primordial, with streams of bloodline light pouring into their body.
Some of those humans transformed partially.
Some fully.
Some broke apart.
Some stood tall with new Primordial marks carved into their skin.
Arvantos pointed at the pillars.
"After humanity began, the Primordials found another path."
The ten geniuses looked at the carvings in silence.
Arvantos continued.
"If Primordials couldn’t reproduce naturally, then we’d create Primordials through transformation instead.

Rather than birthing descendants, we’d choose humans with supreme potential, awaken the hidden compatibility left over from the origin of humanity, and give them a chance to receive the Primordial bloodline."
His gaze moved across all ten of them.
"That’s the reason you’re here."
The mood shifted immediately.
"Since this system began, the Primordial Race has picked the most outstanding human geniuses from different eras, different worlds, and different forces.
Some were chosen through wars.
Some through trials.
Some through bloodline resonance.
In the current era, the Cosmic Ascension Conference is one of the most important ways we select candidates."
Max looked at the pillars.
"So the top ten get this opportunity because you’re looking for humans who can carry the Primordial bloodline."
"Correct," Arvantos said.
"Not every human can carry it.
Honestly, almost none can.
The Primordial bloodline is too heavy for ordinary bodies and too ancient for ordinary souls.
Even supreme geniuses can fail.
Some get only a trace.
Some get a partial bloodline.
Some become candidates.
A few, after many more trials, truly step into the ranks of the Primordials."
Alice and Lenavira weren’t here, but Max could almost guess what Lily would say if she heard all this.
She’d probably say the Primordials were taking a ridiculously roundabout path just because they couldn’t have kids the normal way.
Orion Starfall looked at Arvantos.
"So the Primordial Race has survived by turning humans back into Primordials."
"Yes," Arvantos said.
"Humanity came from Primordials who gave up their bloodline, and the Primordial Race keeps going by choosing extraordinary humans capable of receiving that bloodline again.
It’s a cycle, though not a perfect one."
Damian Voss’s gaze sharpened.
"So humans are both the descendants of the Primordials and the source new Primordials get chosen from."
"Exactly."
The shock on the platform deepened.
The history was too big, too strange, too heavy.
For countless years, humans had struggled, cultivated, fought, risen, fallen, founded clans, built forces, and established kingdoms, empires, dynasties, and divine powers.
Plenty of human forces believed their origins were ordinary compared to the ancient divine races.
Now Arvantos had just told them the truth was far more astonishing.
Humans were born from Primordials.
And Primordials kept existing through humans.
Max stayed quiet for a while.
This secret changed a lot of things.
It explained why the Primordial Race cared so much about the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
It explained why the top ten got chosen.
It explained why becoming a Primordial wasn’t just receiving an outside reward, but returning to a source humans had once lost.
Arvantos looked at the ten geniuses and spoke slowly.
"Now you understand why the Primordial Race values potential over background.
A divine clan bloodline might help you.
A supreme inheritance might strengthen you.
A rare Pseudo Cosmic Path might set you above others in battle.
But none of that alone decides whether you can become a Primordial."
His gaze moved to Max.
"What matters most is whether your foundation can bear the return."
The word "return" quieted the platform again.
Arvantos raised his hand, and the thirteen pillars around the ceremonial ground began to glow.
"This is where your first compatibility trial begins.

Before any bloodline is granted, before any ceremony is performed, before any of you can be called Primordial candidates, we need to see how much of the ancient source your bodies and souls can handle."

chapters.title: Chapter 1941: Four Tiers of Primordial Bloodline!
paragraphs: Arvantos raised one hand. "Stand still. Don’t resist."
The next instant, beams of ancient light dropped from each of the thirteen pillars and connected with the central formation. The ceremonial ground came alive immediately.
Streams of golden liquid light started moving beneath the transparent floor like rivers flowing toward each of the ten participants.
At the same time, a huge illusory Primordial symbol appeared high above them, rotating slowly and sending out wave after wave of ancient aura.
The first thing Max felt was pressure. Not ordinary pressure. It felt like the entire history of an ancient race had come down onto his body and was trying to read every part of him.

The pressure didn’t attack him, but it pushed into him with unstoppable force, moving through his meridians, bones, flesh, bloodline, soul sea, and even the hidden corners of his foundation that ordinary people could never sense.
Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body reacted first. The space around his body twisted faintly, as if it were instinctively analyzing the invading ancient force.

Then his Seven Divine Veins gave off a low resonance, followed by the sleeping power of his draconic essences, his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, his multiple refined Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and the countless hidden inheritances resting inside him.
For a moment, Max felt like his whole existence had turned transparent under the ancient light.
Around him, the others went through their own tests.
Revona stood with her eyes half-open, and the moment the ancient force touched her, the Void Origin Eyes in her pupils spun faintly.

The air around her body turned hollow and deep, and for a short moment, faint shadows of other selves seemed to flicker behind her like reflections from countless past eras. It was as if the compatibility test wasn’t just measuring one life, but many.

Ervin’s body gave off a dark abyssal pressure. A black sea seemed to rise invisibly behind him, while the aura of the broken gate inside him showed itself faintly under the ancient light. His body, soul, and abyssal path all looked extremely stable.

Damian Voss’s sword intent rose on its own. He stayed motionless, yet his whole body felt like a perfectly forged divine sword. The test light passed through him, and every part of his foundation answered with a sharp, disciplined hum.

Orion Starfall was wrapped in starlight. It looked like an entire field of stars had woken up inside him, each one supporting his body and making his compatibility grow stronger with every passing breath.
Kaiden Voidmere seemed to merge with a faint void distortion. His space affinity was so high that even the Primordial light around him bent slightly as it passed through him.
Rosaline, Morgana, Rakan, Aurelian, and the rest also showed striking responses, each one different, each one showing exactly why they’d made the top ten.

The compatibility test dragged on for a long time. The thirteen pillars shifted color several times. First pale gold, then deeper gold, then white, then a rich ancient crimson. Each shift meant a deeper layer of examination.
By the time it hit the crimson stage, even the strongest among them wore serious expressions.
Rakan’s muscles were trembling. Orion’s smile was gone. Damian’s sword aura had turned much sharper. Rosaline’s brows had started to knit. Even Revona had fully opened her eyes by now.
Only Max still stood with a relatively steady look, though inside him the pressure had also climbed to an astonishing level. His foundation was simply too vast.

His body alone was already monstrous enough to suppress most geniuses, and then there was his Dimensional Sovereign Body, his Seven Divine Veins, his draconic essences, his Dragon Scales Transformation, his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, multiple strong inheritances, and his Pseudo Cosmic Paths.
All of it combined into a foundation so abnormal that even the Primordial Compatibility Test seemed to grow more active around him.
At last, the light slowly pulled back. The thirteen pillars dimmed one after another, and the huge Primordial symbol above the sky faded into countless streams of ancient runes.
The ceremony ground fell silent. Then, in front of all of them, a compatibility ranking appeared in the air.
Every genius looked up at once. At the very top sat one name.
[1. Max Morgan]
Below him came the rest.
[2. Revona]
[3. Ervin]
[4. Damian Voss]
[5. Orion Starfall]
[6. Kaiden Voidmere]
[7. Rosaline Lunara]
[8. Morgana Starveil]
[9. Rakan Thorne]
[10. Aurelian Lareth]
The moment the ranking appeared, several of the geniuses went quiet. Most weren’t shocked that Max ranked near the top. They were shocked he ranked first so clearly.
Even Arvantos had expected a lot from Max, but seeing the result laid out so plainly still put a faint smile on his face.
"As expected," he said.
Orion let out a breath and laughed helplessly. "So even here, he’s first."
Rakan crossed his arms and grinned. "I knew his body was monstrous, but this is still annoying to look at."
Damian’s expression stayed calm, though his eyes sharpened slightly as he looked at Max. "Your foundation really is absurd."
Ervin smiled faintly. "After fighting him, I can’t say I’m surprised."
Rosaline looked at the ranking, then at Max, with a complicated smile. "You really don’t leave any room for the rest of us."
Morgana’s purple eyes glimmered with interest. "First in the conference and first in compatibility. How greedy."

Aurelian’s face had already gone cold. Landing last among the top ten wasn’t a light hit to his pride, especially given how highly he thought of himself as a chosen genius of the second elven faction.
Revona looked at the ranking calmly, then at Max. "You really were the right person to beat me."
Max only smiled faintly. "I’ll take that as a compliment."
Arvantos stepped forward again, drawing everyone’s attention back to him.
"The compatibility ranking is done," he said. "Next, I’ll explain the four tiers of Primordial Bloodline."
The mood turned solemn again. Arvantos raised one hand, and four streams of ancient bloodline light appeared before them, each one different in color and pressure.

"The first tier is the General Primordial Bloodline. This is the bloodline most Primordials carry. It brings a major transformation to your body, soul, vitality, and law affinity. Even receiving this bloodline alone is enough to lift an ordinary genius far above his original race."
The first stream glowed steadily.

"The second tier is the Special Primordial Bloodline. Only some Primordials have this one. Besides the natural boost the General Bloodline gives, this tier also produces one or more unique bloodline abilities. Those abilities depend on the source bloodline and the inheritor’s compatibility."
The second stream pulsed with a deeper aura.

"The third tier is the Leader Primordial Bloodline. This belongs to the upper rulers and high authorities of the Primordial Race. It doesn’t just strengthen you. It transforms your fundamental level far more deeply and carries stronger source abilities, greater control over ancient laws, and a much higher ceiling for future growth."
The pressure from the third stream made even the top ten narrow their eyes.
Then Arvantos looked at the final stream. It was only a small amount of bloodline light, but its aura was enough to make the previous three streams look dim by comparison.
"And the fourth tier," Arvantos said slowly, "is the Primarch Bloodline."
The whole ceremonial ground went quiet.
"This bloodline is extremely rare. Only the four Primarchs, myself included, carry it."
Even Max’s eyes sharpened at that.

chapters.title: Chapter 1942: A Painful Process!
paragraphs: Arvantos continued. "Don’t think this bloodline gets handed out just because someone plays favorites. It doesn’t. Even if I wanted to give it, the receiver would first have to survive it. This bloodline has the deepest connection to the origin of the Primordial Race, and the conditions needed to carry it are terrifyingly high."

His gaze moved over all ten of them. "As for who gets which bloodline, the answer is simple. It comes down entirely to your body, your foundation, your compatibility, your soul, your potential, and a lot of other hidden factors."
He turned around. "Come. The next stage is waiting."
With that, Arvantos led the ten geniuses away from the ceremonial ground and deeper into the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

Before long, they arrived at a huge structure hidden behind seven layers of ancient formations. It was a circular hall built from pale gold stone, yet the stone itself seemed alive, almost like condensed bloodline essence.

Ancient Primordial runes covered every wall, and at the center of the hall sat a vast circular chamber split into ten positions. Above each position floated a bloodline crystal the size of a human body, and inside each crystal swirled an ancient liquid light that looked like primordial blood.
The moment they walked in, everyone felt their own blood react.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. This was no ordinary place. This was the Bloodline Chamber.

Arvantos turned to them. "This chamber’s been prepared specifically for the ten of you. Sit cross-legged in your assigned positions. The formations will measure your compatibility again in finer detail and guide the bloodline transfer according to your limits."
No one hesitated. One by one, the top ten geniuses walked forward and sat cross-legged beneath their crystals.
Max sat in the foremost position. Revona sat not far from him. Damian, Ervin, Orion, Kaiden, Rosaline, Morgana, Rakan, and Aurelian all settled into their own spots.

Once all ten had sat down, the circular hall began to hum. Ancient runes across the walls lit up. Rings of golden light spread across the floor beneath each genius. The bloodline crystals above them brightened one after another, and the liquid primordial essence inside started spinning faster and faster.
Arvantos stood at the center of the chamber and raised both hands.
"The process of transferring Primordial Bloodlines," he said solemnly, "begins now."
The instant Arvantos’s words fell, the Bloodline Chamber changed completely.

The ten bloodline crystals hanging above the seated geniuses erupted with light at the same time. Ancient runes lit up across the walls, then spread toward the floor like living veins of gold, and in just a few breaths the whole circular chamber turned into a massive bloodline formation.

The rings beneath each genius started spinning in opposite directions, one inward and one outward, creating layered pressure that sank into their bodies from below while the ancient bloodline essence above pressed down from above.
Then the transfer began.
A stream of Primordial bloodline essence came down from each crystal. It didn’t flow gently. It fell like molten light.
The moment the first strand of that essence touched Max’s forehead, his whole body shook violently. Not from weakness. From overwhelming resonance. Everything inside him reacted at once.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body stirred like it had woken up from a deep sleep.

The Seven Divine Veins in his body pulsed rapidly one after another, each one responding to the invading authority. His draconic essence roared like a volcano cracking open after being held down too long.
The Dragon Scales Transformation source ignited on instinct. His Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline trembled as if it recognized something above it.
Even deeper, his other inheritances, refined foundations, Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and the faint trace of the Dimensional Keeper legacy all surged together.
For a brief moment, Max’s body became the meeting point of countless powers. And the Primordial Bloodline crashed straight into all of them.
The pain hit like a collapsing world.

Max’s fingers dug into his knees hard enough to make his joints creak. His back stiffened, and a low sound he couldn’t hold back escaped his throat as the bloodline essence forced its way into his flesh, bones, meridians, and blood. It wasn’t just entering him. It was rewriting him.
It felt like his marrow was being burned and reforged at the same time. It felt like every bone in his body was being crushed to dust and then rebuilt from an ancient blueprint.

It felt like his blood had turned to molten metal running through channels being forced wider by the second. It felt like his soul had been dragged into a primordial furnace, where existence itself was being carved into him.

His breathing turned heavy, each breath sharp and forced through clenched teeth. Even his heartbeat changed. Every beat echoed like a hammer striking ancient steel, deep, heavy, and almost unbearable.
The Primordial Bloodline didn’t ask permission. It simply imposed itself. And Max understood right away that this wasn’t an upgrade. It was transformation at the level of origin.
The pressure went deeper. The bloodline essence didn’t stop at his physical body. It pushed further, sinking into his soul sea. The moment it touched that layer, his whole consciousness trembled.

But instead of falling apart, something inside him steadied. His Dimensional Sovereign Body adjusted first, instinctively spreading the pressure across his whole existence. The Seven Divine Veins fell into a controlled rhythm instead of fighting back chaotically.

His draconic essence, instead of exploding outward, compressed and held on. Even the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline quieted down a little, as if it understood that resisting would only end in destruction.
Max’s face stayed tense, but his body was starting to adapt.
Still, the pain didn’t ease up. If anything, it went deeper. It wasn’t just physical anymore. It was existential. The Primordial Bloodline was reaching into the very idea of what he was.
His vision blurred for a second as waves of burning pain rolled through him. His body shook once, then steadied again through pure will. Sweat gathered at his temples, but he didn’t move.
He could feel it clearly now. If his foundation had been even a little weaker, he would have shattered instantly.

The transfer kept going without mercy. The bloodline essence thickened, pushing deeper into his origin. It felt like countless ancient hands were tearing open the structure of his existence and rebuilding it from a forgotten blueprint.

For a brief moment, Max’s body became the meeting point of countless powers.
And the Primordial Bloodline crashed straight into all of them.
The pain hit like a collapsing world.
Max’s fingers dug into his knees hard enough to make his joints creak.
His back stiffened, and a low sound he couldn’t hold back escaped his throat as the bloodline essence forced its way into his flesh, bones, meridians, and blood.
It wasn’t just entering him.
It was rewriting him.
It felt like his marrow was being burned and reforged at the same time.
It felt like every bone in his body was being crushed to dust and then rebuilt from an ancient blueprint.
It felt like his blood had turned to molten metal running through channels being forced wider by the second.
It felt like his soul had been dragged into a primordial furnace, where existence itself was being carved into him.
His breathing turned heavy, each breath sharp and forced through clenched teeth.
Even his heartbeat changed.
Every beat echoed like a hammer striking ancient steel, deep, heavy, and almost unbearable.
The Primordial Bloodline didn’t ask permission.
It simply imposed itself.
And Max understood right away that this wasn’t an upgrade.
It was transformation at the level of origin.
The pressure went deeper.
The bloodline essence didn’t stop at his physical body.
It pushed further, sinking into his soul sea.
The moment it touched that layer, his whole consciousness trembled.
But instead of falling apart, something inside him steadied.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body adjusted first, instinctively spreading the pressure across his whole existence.
The Seven Divine Veins fell into a controlled rhythm instead of fighting back chaotically.
His draconic essence, instead of exploding outward, compressed and held on.
Even the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline quieted down a little, as if it understood that resisting would only end in destruction.
Max’s face stayed tense, but his body was starting to adapt.
Still, the pain didn’t ease up.
If anything, it went deeper.
It wasn’t just physical anymore.
It was existential.
The Primordial Bloodline was reaching into the very idea of what he was.
His vision blurred for a second as waves of burning pain rolled through him.
His body shook once, then steadied again through pure will.
Sweat gathered at his temples, but he didn’t move.
He could feel it clearly now.
If his foundation had been even a little weaker, he would have shattered instantly.
The transfer kept going without mercy.
The bloodline essence thickened, pushing deeper into his origin.
It felt like countless ancient hands were tearing open the structure of his existence and rebuilding it from a forgotten blueprint.

chapters.title: Chapter 1943: A Slow Process!
paragraphs: Max lowered his head slightly, his white hair falling over his eyes, but his grip on himself never slipped.
He endured. Because there was no other choice.

The chamber around him hummed louder as the formation moved into its next stage. The pressure multiplied, and the Primordial Bloodline stopped flowing in strands. It started coming down in solid pillars of light.

The impact hit Max instantly. His body jolted again, and for a moment his aura flared out of control, bright enough to outshine everything else in the chamber. Then it got forced back down as the bloodline essence pressed even deeper into him.
The pain surged again, sharper, heavier, more absolute. Max’s teeth clenched so hard a faint crack echoed out.
But he didn’t lose consciousness. He couldn’t. Because the moment he did, the transformation wouldn’t stop. It would just break him.
So he held on. Inside him, every power he had was being forced into alignment. Not destroyed. Not erased. Just reshaped to fit the Primordial standard.
Slowly, against all that pain, his body started to adapt. Not comfortably. Not safely. But it happened anyway.

The runes in the chamber glowed brighter, as if acknowledging his resistance and his acceptance at the same time. The formation responded, sharpening the precision of the transfer instead of ramping up the brutality.
Max let out a slow breath through clenched teeth. The pain was still unbearable. But now, underneath it, he could feel something else.
Change. Deep, irreversible change.

The bloodline transfer didn’t end quickly. One hour passed. Then two. Then three. Inside the Bloodline Chamber, time seemed to stop meaning much. The ten geniuses stayed seated beneath their crystals, each one caught in a storm of ancient pain and transformation.

The formation beneath them kept rotating without pause, and the liquid primordial essence above them kept pouring down in controlled streams, sinking into their bodies, merging with their blood, and forcing their old foundations to either adapt or break.
No one spoke. No one had the energy to waste on words.

Even the weakest of these ten was a supreme genius who’d reached the top of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, but right now, every one of them looked like they were being crushed under an invisible mountain.

Their bodies shook from time to time. Their auras flared and dimmed. Their bloodlines resisted, gave in, pushed back, and adapted again. This wasn’t a simple transfer of power. It was a remaking of their existence into something closer to the ancient Primordial source.

Rakan Thorne’s huge body shook violently as golden bloodline light hammered into his bones and muscles again and again. The War God Body he was so proud of held up with terrifying toughness, but even that wasn’t enough to stop blood from leaking out of the corner of his mouth.

Orion Starfall’s star marks lit up one after another, each one going deeper under the pressure of the bloodline, while Kaiden Voidmere’s surrounding space warped so badly that the formation beneath him had to release extra stabilizing runes.

Damian Voss sat straight like a sword planted in the earth, but his face had gone pale, and the sharp aura around him had pulled in tight as he forced every scrap of his will into enduring the change.

Revona’s case was even stranger. Faint shadows of past lives kept appearing and disappearing behind her. Sometimes she looked like a pale young woman with quiet eyes. Sometimes, for the briefest instant, she looked like an ancient cultivator sitting under a ruined sky.

Other times she looked like a cold monarch, a wandering scholar, a battlefield survivor, or a faceless figure standing alone in an empty world. The Void Origin Eyes spun slowly, but they didn’t try to nullify the Primordial Bloodline. Instead, they watched it, endured it, and let it carve itself into her current body.
Ervin’s abyssal aura sank deeper and deeper. Every time the Primordial Bloodline entered him, it seemed to fall into an endless sea before rising back up, more ancient and more condensed than before.
Morgana’s curse aura wrapped around her body like black-violet threads, but the Primordial essence refined those threads without mercy.

Rosaline’s dawn light turned softer but purer, while Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance aura flickered with unstable pride as the Primordial Bloodline forced itself into a foundation already carrying too many complications.
And at the center of it all, Max’s transformation kept going at the highest intensity.

The bloodline crystal above him had become almost blinding. The primordial essence pouring into his body was thicker than anyone else’s. It fell like a pillar of molten starlight, hitting his forehead, chest, and bloodline source all at once. His body had already adapted past the first stage, but the deeper stage was far worse.
Every time he thought the pain had hit its limit, the formation opened another layer, and the Primordial Bloodline sank even deeper, into places even his own senses rarely reached.

His bones weren’t just being strengthened anymore. They were being rewritten. His blood wasn’t just being refined anymore. It was starting to carry an ancient rhythm that had never existed in him before. His soul wasn’t just enduring pressure anymore. It was being forced to accept a new origin mark.

The Dimensional Sovereign Body, the Seven Divine Veins, the draconic essences, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline the Dimensional Keeper legacy, and his refined Pseudo Cosmic Paths all kept resonating under the pressure. None of them got erased.

None of them got replaced. Instead, the Primordial Bloodline seemed to be finding a way to settle above all of them, not as an outside force, but as a higher foundation that could hold everything together.
Max’s head stayed lowered. His breathing stayed slow and heavy. Sweat slid down his face, but his body never bent.
The hours kept passing. At some point, the chamber entered its final stage.
The ten bloodline crystals above the geniuses cracked at the same time. The sound was clear. Not broken from failure. Broken because the essence inside them had been fully released.
Ancient runes surged out of the cracks and turned into ten separate beams of light, each one descending into the body of its chosen recipient.

chapters.title: Chapter 1944: Success!
paragraphs: The pressure inside the chamber climbed to its highest point, and even Arvantos, who’d been calmly watching from the center, finally looked more serious.
"This is the final imprint," he said.
The ten geniuses heard him, but none of them could answer.
The final imprint came down.
Boom!

Every genius trembled. Their bloodlines surged violently. Their souls shook. Their bodies gave off different colors of light as the Primordial essence finally stopped acting like a foreign force and started settling in as part of who they were.
The pain hit its peak, so intense that even Max’s consciousness blurred for a fraction of a breath.
Then something inside him opened.
Not a vein. Not a meridian. Not an ordinary bloodline source. It was like an ancient seal, hidden in the deepest part of his new Primordial foundation, had finally acknowledged him.
The system flashed before his vision.
[Primordial Bloodline Transfer Completed.]
[Bloodline Tier Acquired: Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.]
[Primarch-Level Bloodline Detected.]
[Bloodline Integration Status: Stable.]
Max’s eyes opened slightly.
Tier 4. The highest tier Arvantos had mentioned. The same tier only the Four Primarchs carried.

Even Max, who’d stayed calm through most of the process, felt something shift in his chest at that moment. He’d expected a strong result given his foundation, but seeing the system confirm it still hit different. This wasn’t just a powerful bloodline.
This was a Primarch-level bloodline, rare enough that only four known beings in the whole Primordial Race carried it.
Before he could think it through, the final imprint finished settling into his body. The pain didn’t vanish right away. It slowly pulled back, leaving behind a deep, ancient heat in his blood.

The Bloodline Chamber went quiet. One by one, the beams of light faded. The ten geniuses stayed seated, their bodies still trembling faintly from the aftermath. The bloodline crystals above them had lost their glow and now hung empty, like shells after all their essence had drained out. The runes beneath them kept glowing faintly for a few more breaths before slowly dimming.
Arvantos raised one hand. A wave of gentle Primordial energy passed through the chamber, steadying all ten of them.
"Open your eyes," he said.
They slowly did.
Some looked exhausted. Some looked pale. Some breathed like they’d just survived a disaster. But every single one of them had changed.

Rakan’s body now carried a faint ancient pressure under his War God aura. Orion’s star marks looked deeper and more refined. Damian’s sword presence felt heavier, like his body itself had picked up a more ancient sharpness.

Ervin’s abyssal aura had turned darker and more stable. Kaiden’s space fluctuations felt smoother and more natural. Morgana’s curse aura had picked up a strange golden-violet undertone. Rosaline’s dawn light had turned purer.

Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance had grown brighter, though his face stayed tense. Revona’s Void Origin Eyes were quieter than before, but the emptiness inside them now carried a faint ancient ring of Primordial light.

Arvantos looked at them all in silence. Then his eyes shone. The four-colored rings in his pupils rotated once, and an invisible pressure swept through the chamber. It didn’t hurt anyone. It just examined the new bloodlines that had formed inside them.
A moment later, he nodded. "The transfer has succeeded."
The ten geniuses looked toward him.
Arvantos continued, "All of you have received Primordial Bloodlines."
The mood tightened. Even though they’d already made it through the process, hearing him say it out loud still brought a few quiet sighs of relief.
Then his gaze moved across them one by one.
"Revona. Ervin. Damian Voss. Orion Starfall. Kaiden Voidmere. Rosaline Lunara. Morgana Starveil. Rakan Thorne. Aurelian Lareth."
He paused briefly. "All nine of you have received Tier 3 Primordial Bloodlines."
The chamber fell silent.
Tier 3. Leader Primordial Bloodline. The bloodline carried by the upper rulers and high authorities of the Primordial Race. Even among Primordials, this level stood far above the ordinary.

Any single one of them getting a bloodline like this would have been enough to shake their home forces. For all nine of them to get Tier 3 bloodlines showed just how terrifying this generation’s top ten really was.
Rakan’s eyes went wide. "Tier 3?"
Orion let out a low laugh. "That’s higher than I expected."
Damian Voss stayed calm, but even his gaze had sharpened.
Ervin looked down at his own hand, thoughtful, feeling the new ancient pressure flowing quietly through his blood.
Morgana smiled faintly. "So all of us turned out fairly valuable."
Kaiden Voidmere said nothing, but his eyes clearly showed he was already working through the changes in his body.
Aurelian’s stiff expression finally eased up a bit. Tier 3 wasn’t the highest, but it was still a Leader Primordial Bloodline. Even his pride couldn’t brush that off.
Revona looked at Arvantos quietly. She’d already noticed he hadn’t mentioned Max. Everyone else noticed it a moment later too.
The chamber went even quieter.
Arvantos’s eyes moved to Max. A faint smile crossed his face.
"As for Max Morgan."
Every gaze turned toward Max.
Arvantos spoke slowly, his voice carrying a weight heavy enough to make the whole Bloodline Chamber feel smaller.
"He alone received a Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline."
The words hit the chamber like thunder.

For several breaths, no one said anything. Even the geniuses who’d just gotten Tier 3 bloodlines couldn’t keep their expressions steady. Tier 3 was already incredible, but Tier 4 was on a completely different level.
Arvantos had said it himself before the transfer started. The fourth tier was the Primarch Bloodline, an extremely rare bloodline only the Four Primarchs, him included, carried.
Now Max had it.
Revona’s pale eyes sharpened slightly.
Ervin stared at Max for a long breath before smiling helplessly.
Damian Voss lowered his gaze for a second, then looked back at Max with even deeper respect.
Orion laughed softly, though there was clear disbelief in his voice. "Of course he did."
Rakan shook his head. "This man doesn’t know how to be normal."
Morgana’s smile turned more amused and more serious at the same time. "First in the conference, first in compatibility, and now the only Tier 4 bloodline. That’s excessive."
Kaiden Voidmere looked thoughtful. "A Primarch-level bloodline."
Aurelian’s face darkened again. Whatever joy he’d felt from getting a Tier 3 bloodline got crushed the second he heard Max had gotten the one thing no one else had.
His fists tightened, but he still didn’t say anything. In this place, in front of Arvantos, any foolish show of resentment would only embarrass him further.

Max stayed seated quietly. His expression didn’t change much, but he could feel the bloodline inside him now. It wasn’t roaring. It was calm. Too calm. Like a sleeping ancient monarch resting in his blood, waiting for the day his body could fully wake up its authority.
Arvantos looked at Max with deep eyes. "Your foundation was strong enough to bear it."
Max stood slowly. The moment he rose, a faint pressure moved through the chamber. It was subtle. Not overpowering. Not released on purpose. But all nine other geniuses felt it.

The aura of the new Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline was still asleep inside Max, yet even in that dormant state, it carried something that made their own Tier 3 bloodlines react faintly. It wasn’t suppression in any crude sense. It was hierarchy. A natural gap in origin.
Just then Max’s cultivation of 1st level Law Awakening Realm began to react violently.
"It looks like you are leveling up." Arvantos smiled seeing the intense energy fluctuations around Max.

chapters.title: Chapter 1945 - 5th level of Law Refinement Realm!
paragraphs: The other nine geniuses turned toward him at once, their expressions shifting again. They’d just gone through the bloodline transfer themselves.

Every one of them had gained a Tier 3 Leader Primordial Bloodline, and they could all feel their bodies, souls, and foundations changing in powerful ways. But none of them had triggered a breakthrough.
Their auras had deepened and their potential had clearly grown, but their cultivation realms hadn’t budged.
Max was different. The energy inside him wasn’t stopping. It was pushing his realm higher.
[Primordial Bloodline Integration Energy Detected.]
[Energy Absorption Beginning.]
[Law Refinement Realm 1st Level Stabilized.]
[Advancement Initiated.]

Max’s eyes sharpened slightly as the system prompts flashed in front of him, but he didn’t show anything outwardly. He just sat cross-legged in silence, letting the leftover Primordial Bloodline energy merge with his cultivation foundation.
Inside him, the laws he’d only recently started refining grew sharper and more condensed.
The Law Refinement Realm was all about taking awakened laws and tempering them into something stable, usable, and deeply tied to yourself.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline energy fit that process perfectly, since every strand of it carried an ancient law quality that naturally refined whatever it touched.
His foundation trembled. Then the first barrier broke.
Boom!
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 2nd Level.]
The pressure around Max increased instantly. A faint wave of Primordial aura spread out from his body, and the nine geniuses felt their newly gained Tier 3 bloodlines react on instinct.
It wasn’t the crude kind of suppression a stronger cultivator throws at a weaker one. It was a deeper hierarchy, born from the gap between bloodline tiers.
Their bloodlines had only just awakened, yet even now they could sense that Max’s bloodline stood above theirs at the source level.

Aurelian’s expression turned extremely ugly. He’d just received a Tier 3 Primordial Bloodline, something that should have been one of the greatest moments of his life. But before he could even enjoy it, Max had gotten a Tier 4 Primarch Bloodline and was now breaking through right in front of everyone.
Orion Starfall stared for a second, then laughed helplessly. "He really doesn’t leave any room for the rest of us to feel proud."
Rakan Thorne grinned, though disbelief still showed in his eyes. "This bastard just finished the bloodline transfer and he’s already breaking through."
Damian Voss stayed quiet, but his gaze turned serious. He could feel that Max’s aura wasn’t just getting stronger. It was getting more refined and more dangerous.
Ervin smiled faintly. "When I saw him back on the reception platform, I figured he’d already gotten stronger after the conference. Turns out that was just the beginning."
Revona watched quietly, her pale eyes reflecting the Primordial light around Max. Her expression stayed calm, but even she couldn’t ignore what was happening in front of her.
’This kid... Is he related to him?’ She thought looking deeply at Max.
Max’s cultivation didn’t stop at the 2nd level.

The remaining Primordial energy kept pouring through him. His newly formed Tier 4 bloodline worked like a supreme vessel, holding, filtering, and directing the energy into his law foundation without letting any of it scatter. His Dimensional Sovereign Body helped spread out the pressure.

His Seven Divine Veins kept the flow steady. His draconic essence and Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline and Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline stopped resisting altogether, and the Dimensional Keeper legacy stayed quiet but steady, deep in his foundation.
The second barrier broke.
Boom!
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 3rd Level.]
Max’s aura rose again. The laws around him condensed into faint threads, each one carrying a trace of Primordial light.
His Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, and Devouring Flames Domain all stirred inside him, growing even more refined under the pressure of his rising cultivation and new bloodline.
They were still Pseudo Cosmic Paths, still incomplete, still nowhere near true Cosmic Paths before the Divine Lord Realm, but their structures grew sharper and deeper.
Another wave of energy burst out. The third barrier broke.
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 4th Level.]
By now, the Bloodline Chamber was glowing almost as bright as it had during the transfer itself.
The ancient runes on the walls seemed to wake up again, not because the formation was still feeding Max more bloodline essence, but because his breakthrough was interacting with the chamber itself.
The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline inside him resonated with the chamber’s origin, and the whole space started humming softly.
Arvantos watched with real interest.
Sarvion, standing off to the side, could no longer fully hide his surprise.
"Primarch," Sarvion said quietly, "his absorption speed is abnormal."
Arvantos smiled. "His foundation is abnormal. The absorption speed is just a result of that."
Max’s body shook once more. The remaining energy gathered into one final surge. It moved through his bloodline, entered his law foundation, and pushed toward the next small realm.
For an ordinary cultivator, jumping several levels at once inside the Law Refinement Realm would have caused instability.

But Max’s foundation was far too strong. He’d accumulated too much depth during the Cosmic Ascension Conference, and the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline had refined his base instead of straining it. Each breakthrough hit hard, but none of them felt hollow.
The final barrier shattered.
Boom!
[Breakthrough Achieved.]
[Law Refinement Realm 5th Level.]
[Remaining Primordial Integration Energy Stabilized.]
[Current Realm: Law Refinement Realm 5th Level.]

Max slowly opened his eyes. For a brief moment, his pupils carried faint primordial rings before they faded. His aura settled around him, no longer erupting wildly, but everyone in the Bloodline Chamber could feel that he’d changed again.

He’d walked into the chamber as a 1st level Law Refinement Realm cultivator. After receiving the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline and absorbing the leftover integration energy, he’d jumped straight to the 5th level of the Law Refinement Realm.
The chamber stayed silent. Even the top ten geniuses didn’t know what to say at first.
Max stood slowly. His aura was calm, but that calm only made him seem more dangerous.

The Primordial Bloodline he’d just gained wasn’t roaring out loud, but it sat inside him like an ancient source waiting for the day it could fully wake up. His cultivation had jumped four small levels, his law foundation had been refined, and his Pseudo Cosmic Paths had grown sharper.
Arvantos looked at the others and seemed to catch what they were thinking.

He spoke calmly. "Don’t misunderstand. Integrating a Primordial Bloodline always leaves behind a large amount of energy, but whether that energy can trigger a breakthrough depends on the cultivator’s current realm and foundation."
The nine geniuses listened closely.

Arvantos continued. "All of you were already at the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm before you entered the Bloodline Chamber. For you, the next step is the Divine Lord Realm. That’s not a small jump you can cross with leftover energy from a bloodline integration. The Divine Lord Realm needs full preparation, a stabilized foundation, deeper law transformation, and the true start of authority."
He paused, then glanced at Max.

"Max Morgan was different. He was still in the Law Refinement Realm. The energy generated from integrating the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline was more than enough to push him through several small levels, especially given his foundation. If he’d also been at the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm like the rest of you, this same energy wouldn’t have been enough to push him into the Divine Lord Realm either."
Only then did some of the others relax a little.
Rakan let out a breath. "So we weren’t cheated out of anything."

Arvantos smiled faintly. "No, you weren’t. Honestly, getting Tier 3 bloodlines at your current realm is already an extraordinary result. Once you properly digest the bloodline and prepare for your Divine Lord breakthrough, the benefits will show a lot more clearly."
Orion nodded thoughtfully. "So our gains run deeper, just not right away."
"Correct," Arvantos said. "The Primordial Bloodline isn’t just some cultivation pill. Its real value isn’t the instant jump in realm. It’s the change to your future ceiling."
Damian Voss looked at his own hand quietly. "So once we break through to the Divine Lord Realm, the difference should start showing."
"It will," Arvantos said. "Your bodies, souls, law affinities, and future paths have all changed."
Ervin glanced at Max and smiled. "Still, watching him climb four levels right in front of us isn’t exactly pleasant."
Max smiled faintly. "You can take it up with the Primordials."
Arvantos looked amused. "I don’t accept complaints."
For a moment, even the tense mood in the Bloodline Chamber loosened up a little.

chapters.title: Chapter 1946: A Major Crisis!
paragraphs: The faint amusement that had settled over the Bloodline Chamber after Max’s breakthrough didn’t last long.

Arvantos’s expression turned serious. The shift was subtle, but everyone in the room felt it right away. The four-colored rings in his eyes slowed down, and the ancient pressure around him grew quieter instead of stronger.

That quiet made the whole chamber feel heavier, since it felt like the Primarch had stopped speaking to them as the man guiding a reward ceremony and started speaking as one of the four leaders of the Primordial Race.
The ten geniuses slowly fell silent.

Rakan, who’d been about to make another comment about Max’s strange breakthrough, closed his mouth. Orion’s faint smile disappeared. Damian’s gaze sharpened. Ervin looked at Arvantos with calm, serious eyes. Revona stayed as expressionless as always, but her Void Origin Eyes opened slightly wider.
Max also turned his full attention toward Arvantos.
Arvantos looked at each of them before speaking.
"There are some things you should know."

The moment he said that, the mood in the room shifted again. Aurelian frowned slightly but didn’t dare interrupt. Rosaline and Morgana traded a quick glance, while Kaiden Voidmere’s silver-gray eyes narrowed in thought.
After everything they’d already been through, none of them believed Arvantos would suddenly change his tone over something small.
Orion finally asked, "What do you mean?"

Arvantos didn’t answer right away. He turned his gaze toward the walls of the Bloodline Chamber. The ancient runes there slowly dimmed, and for a moment the whole chamber seemed to sink into a deeper shade of gold. The silence that followed wasn’t long, but it was enough to make everyone uneasy.
Then Arvantos began.
"A major crisis will soon spread across this universe."
The words came out quiet. But they hit the ten geniuses harder than any shout could have.
The entire universe. Not one clan. Not one region. Not one divine territory. Not even the Divine Realm alone. The entire universe.
The ten geniuses’ expressions all changed at once.
Rakan’s brows pulled tight. "A crisis that big?"
Morgana’s playful look vanished completely. "What kind of crisis?"
Kaiden Voidmere’s eyes turned sharp. "Is it tied to another race? A war? Some kind of collapse in the laws?"
Damian Voss looked at Arvantos too. "How soon?"
Arvantos stayed silent for a few breaths, then said, "I can’t explain the details yet."
That answer only made the room feel heavier.
Rakan frowned. "Can’t, or won’t?"
Arvantos looked at him calmly. "Both."
No one said anything.

Arvantos went on. "Some truths can’t be carried by people who aren’t strong enough yet. Knowing too much too soon won’t help you. It might even become a weight that wrecks your confidence, warps your judgment, or draws attention you’re not ready to handle."
Even Rakan went quiet after that.

Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. He could tell Arvantos wasn’t holding back for the sake of being mysterious. The Primarch’s tone carried the weight of someone who genuinely understood the danger behind his own warning. If one of the four Primarchs chose not to explain the full crisis, then clearly this wasn’t something the current top ten were ready to touch.
Arvantos looked across the group.

"What you need to know is simple. The peace you’ve known won’t last forever. The great forces of the Divine Realm, the Primordial Race, and plenty of ancient powers are already quietly preparing. Most people in the universe have no idea what’s coming, and for now, that’s for the best."
Rosaline’s face paled. "Then why tell us anything at all?"

"Because you’re no longer ordinary geniuses," Arvantos replied. "You’re the top ten of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. You’ve received Primordial Bloodlines. Each of you has stepped onto a path that will make you far more important than you were before. If you keep growing, you might end up part of the power that resists what’s coming."
His gaze lingered on Max for a moment.
"Some of you might even become central to it."
The chamber went quiet again. The words were vague, but the weight behind them wasn’t.

Arvantos raised one hand, and faint Primordial light appeared around the ten geniuses before slowly sinking into their bodies. It wasn’t another bloodline transfer, just a stabilizing force meant to help settle the Primordial Bloodlines they’d just received.
"Don’t waste time," Arvantos said. "That’s the most important warning I can give you."
His voice deepened. "Get stronger as fast as you can."
Every genius listened without blinking.

"If you delay, if you get comfortable because of your current strength, if you assume that getting a Primordial Bloodline means your future is set, you might not get another chance to improve. The crisis heading our way won’t care about your talent, your background, your ranking, your bloodline tier, or your pride. When it arrives, only strength will matter."
The words pressed down on them like a mountain.

Even Aurelian, who’d spent most of this whole process feeling stung by how much more Max had gained, turned solemn. Even he understood Arvantos wasn’t exaggerating. A Primarch had no reason to scare a bunch of juniors just for entertainment.
Ervin lowered his gaze for a second, then smiled faintly. "So the Cosmic Ascension Conference wasn’t just a competition."
"No," Arvantos said. "It was also a selection."
Damian Voss rested his hand lightly near his sword. "And the bloodline transfer was preparation."
"Yes."
Revona finally spoke. "For whatever comes next."
Arvantos looked at her and nodded. "Correct."
The Bloodline Chamber fell into a long silence after that.

The ten geniuses had walked into this place expecting rewards, transformation, and opportunity. They’d gotten all of that. Nine of them had gained Tier 3 Primordial Bloodlines, and Max had gained the Tier 4 Primarch Bloodline. Their bodies, souls, foundations, and futures had all changed in ways that would shock their home forces.
But now the meaning behind those rewards felt heavier. They weren’t just gifts. They were preparation for a disaster no one had named yet.
Max stayed quiet.

A major crisis that would soon spread across the entire universe. Arvantos hadn’t explained what it actually was, and that only made it feel more dangerous. Max already carried enough of his own burdens.

His parents were still imprisoned. Aurelian still held the stolen source of his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. His enemies hadn’t gone anywhere. The secrets behind the Dimensional Keeper legacy were still sitting unanswered in the dark.
And now another shadow had shown up on top of all of that.
