chapters.title: Chapter 1947: A Promise!
paragraphs: Max slowly closed his hand. The Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stirred faintly inside him. His cultivation, now steady at the 5th level of the Law Refinement Realm, felt nowhere near enough. Not for his own goals, and definitely not for whatever crisis could make one of the four Primarchs sound this serious.
Arvantos looked at all of them one last time.
"You’ll stay in the Primordial Ancestral Domain for a short while to stabilize your bloodlines and learn the first stage of Primordial control. After that, you’ll return to your own forces."
His gaze grew heavier.
"Make good use of the time you have."
No one answered right away. There was no need to. Each of them understood.

The Cosmic Ascension Conference had been the stage where they proved themselves. The Primordial Bloodline was the reward that transformed them. But the real trial waiting ahead was something far bigger than any tournament. And if they weren’t strong enough when it arrived, even the title of supreme genius wouldn’t mean anything.
Even though Arvantos’s warning left a heavy shadow over the ten geniuses, none of them kept asking about it.

They were curious, of course. How could they not be? A major crisis that would soon spread across the entire universe wasn’t a small thing to hear. If those words had come from an elder of some ordinary divine clan, a few of them might have suspected exaggeration meant to scare them into obedience.

But the person who’d said it was Arvantos, one of the four Primarchs of the Primordial Race. A being like him had no reason to exaggerate in front of the younger generation, and he certainly had no reason to invent fear without cause.

Still, curiosity alone wasn’t useful. Arvantos had already made it clear that they weren’t qualified to know the full truth yet, so dwelling on it would only waste time. Every one of them had just received a Primordial Bloodline, and that new power hadn’t fully settled into their bodies. If they left it unstable out of carelessness, even a heaven-sent opportunity could turn into a hidden danger.
So, under Sarvion’s guidance, the ten geniuses stayed in the Primordial Ancestral Domain for several more days.

Each of them was assigned a separate cultivation chamber in a quiet area behind the Bloodline Chamber. These chambers sat above streams of ancient primordial energy, and their walls were carved with stabilizing runes meant to ease the friction between each genius’s original foundation and their newly received bloodline.
Once inside, each of them began the long process of circulating their Primordial Bloodline, learning its rhythm, controlling its pressure, and making sure it didn’t clash with their existing powers.
Max sat alone in one of these chambers.

The room around him was circular, silent, and filled with faint golden mist. The floor beneath him held four interlocking runes that resonated faintly with the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline inside his body. Every time his blood circulated, those runes lit up softly, as if responding to a Primarch’s bloodline.

Max sat cross-legged with his eyes closed. Inside him, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stayed calm, but that calm felt more like the stillness of an ocean than the weakness of sleeping power. It hadn’t fully awakened yet. Max could tell that much clearly.

What he’d received was the source and foundation of the bloodline, but bringing out its true abilities would take time, battles, refinement, and deeper cultivation. Even so, in its current state, it had already transformed his body, strengthened his soul, refined his laws, and helped push his cultivation to the 5th level of the Law Refinement Realm.

His Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, and Devouring Flames Domain had also stabilized further thanks to the new bloodline. They were still Pseudo Cosmic Paths, but their edges had grown sharper and their structures more complete.

Max could sense the distant wall between pseudo and true cosmic paths more clearly than ever, and yet that wall also felt impossibly high. No matter how close he seemed to get, he knew he wouldn’t truly cross it until he reached the Divine Lord Realm.

For several days, Max focused only on stabilizing. He didn’t rush. He didn’t try to greedily force the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline to show off abilities before it was ready. He calmly guided it through his body, let it settle into his foundation, and made sure it wouldn’t disturb his other bloodlines.

His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, draconic essence foundation, Seven Divine Veins, Dimensional Sovereign Body, and new Primordial Bloodline were all powerful on their own, but power without balance could destroy the person carrying it. Max had too many extraordinary things inside him, which meant his foundation needed even more control than most.
On the fifth day, while Max quietly circulated the Primordial Bloodline, a communication mark he carried suddenly lit up.
Max opened his eyes. A message appeared before him.
[Max, I need your help.]
[You promised you would help me once in return for me joining Crown.]
[Come to the coordinates I have sent. Come alone.]
[Rose.]
Max looked at the message for a few breaths.

Rose. The young woman who’d agreed to join his force, Crown, in exchange for one favor. She hadn’t asked for that favor right away back then, and Max hadn’t pushed her to explain. He’d simply given his word. Now, it looked like the time had come for her to collect on it.
Max stood up. He didn’t waste any time.
After letting Sarvion know he had a private matter to handle and getting permission to leave the Primordial Ancestral Domain for a while, Max used the coordinates Rose had sent.

A spatial path opened in front of him, and his Dimensional Sovereign Body guided him through the layers of space with far more ease than before. After stepping into the Law Refinement Realm and receiving the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, his control over space had gotten even more natural, almost as if distance itself had softened around him.
A short while later, Max arrived at the location Rose had given him.
The first thing he saw was emptiness. Not the emptiness of void, and not the emptiness of destruction. Just an abandoned planet.

The sky was pale blue, the wind was gentle, and the land stretched endlessly in every direction, covered by vast grass fields rolling like waves under the breeze. There were no cities, no mountains of spiritual energy, no towering sects, no ancient ruins, no divine beasts, no obvious formations, and no visible sign of any powerful clan.
Max stood in the middle of the grass field and looked around silently.
"This is the place?"
For a moment, even he wondered if Rose had sent him to the wrong location by mistake.
Then his eyes narrowed. His Dimensional Sovereign Body reacted. The world looked empty on the surface, but the space here was anything but ordinary.

chapters.title: Chapter 1948: Secrets of the Four Sacred Clans!
paragraphs: [A few scenes got cut here. Max would meet Rose here and then she would reveal she is part of the Evercrest Clan, one of the Four Sacred Clans and then took him to the Evercrest Clan]
Max looked toward the revealed world of the Evercrest Clan.
The abandoned grass planet had disappeared from his view, replaced by a hidden sacred territory folded inside countless layers of space.

Colossal trees rose like pillars between heaven and earth, emerald rivers of energy flowed through the air, and palaces carved from living wood and pale jade stood across floating gardens suspended between branches large enough to hold whole cities.
Everything before him looked ancient, peaceful, and beautiful, yet Max could sense a deep instability hiding beneath the surface, something ordinary eyes would never pick up on.

Rose didn’t take him inside right away. Instead, she stood beside him on the boundary between the abandoned outer world and the hidden clan territory, looking out at the vast Evercrest domain with a complicated expression.
"Before I take you in," she said, "there are some things you should know."
Max glanced at her. "About your clan?"
"About all Four Sacred Clans," Rose replied.
Max’s eyes sharpened slightly.

Rose turned toward him, and the smile she usually wore was gone. "You’ve received the Primordial Bloodline now, and not an ordinary one either. Since you’re already connected to the Primordial Race, there are some secrets about the Divine Realm you’re qualified to know."
Max didn’t interrupt her.

Rose looked back at the hidden domain and began speaking. "Long ago, after humans came into existence, the first human forces to truly rise and establish themselves in the Divine Realm were the Four Sacred Clans. Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest."

Max stayed silent, but his expression shifted slightly. He’d heard of the Four Sacred Clans many times. Their names carried terrifying weight across the Divine Realm. Even forces like the Black Dragon Clan, the Sword God Palace, the War God Palace, the Nine Star Court, and the major world guilds didn’t treat the Four Sacred Clans lightly. They were ancient, mysterious, and powerful enough to sit near the top of human civilization.
But Rose’s next words made things far more complicated.
"The Four Sacred Clans were the earliest great pillars of humanity," Rose continued. "But their origin isn’t the same as ordinary humans."
Max looked at her. "Different how?"

Rose’s eyes grew deeper. "Most humans supposedly descended from Primordials who gave up their bloodline and became mortal. That’s the history you should have been told, and it’s true for the vast majority of humanity."
"The vast majority?" Max repeated.
Rose nodded. "But not all."
The wind moved across the grass behind them, and the hidden entrance to the Evercrest Clan shimmered softly in front of them, like a veil of folded light.
Rose lowered her voice slightly. "The Four Sacred Clans aren’t descendants of those Primordials."
Max’s expression finally changed. He looked straight at her. "Then what are they?"
Rose met his gaze. "The Four Sacred Clans are descended from a forbidden bloodline cursed by the world."
For a moment, even Max didn’t say anything.
A forbidden bloodline cursed by the world. Those words carried a different kind of weight than ordinary ancient secrets.

Max had seen plenty of powerful bloodlines. His own body carried the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, and now a Tier 4 Primarch Bloodline of the Primordial Race. He understood better than most how much a bloodline could shape destiny, power, inheritance, and status.

But a bloodline cursed by the world was something else entirely. For some reason, it reminded him of the Legacy of the Dimensional Keeper where every inheritor of the legacy would end up die in way or another before fully awakening their Dimensional Keeper Legacy.
From what that goddess had told him, Dimensional Keeper Legacy was also cursed by fate.
"Cursed by the world," Max said slowly. "That doesn’t sound like a figure of speech."
"It isn’t," Rose replied.
Max studied her face and asked, "What bloodline?"

Rose didn’t answer right away. Her gaze drifted toward the hidden Evercrest domain, and for a brief moment, something unreadable crossed her eyes. It wasn’t quite fear, but it was close to caution, the kind shown by someone who knew certain names shouldn’t be spoken carelessly.
Rose said, "I can show you inside the clan."
Max’s expression stayed calm, but his thoughts were racing.

The Four Sacred Clans weren’t descended from Primordials like other humans. They carried a forbidden bloodline cursed by the world. They were strong enough to rival Primordials despite lacking the Primordial Race’s own bloodline. And Rose had brought him here because the Evercrest Clan was in trouble.
The pieces were starting to form a dangerous picture.
Max looked at Rose again. "You said the Four Sacred Clans don’t carry the Primordial Race’s bloodline, yet they’re as strong as the Primordials."

Rose nodded. "Yes. That’s why the Four Sacred Clans have always held a special position. They’re human, but not human in the same way most humans are. They don’t carry Primordial Bloodline, yet their inherited power can stand against the Primordial Race. Their ancestors never relied on returning to the Primordial source. They walked a different path, one the world itself rejected."
"Then why are they still called human forces?"

"Because they chose to stand with humanity," Rose said. "Whatever their origin, the Four Sacred Clans protected early humans back when humanity was weak. They built the first great shelters, the first sacred cities, the first human law academies, and the first supreme inheritance grounds. Without them, humanity might have been wiped out before it ever became a major race."

Max listened quietly. This was another hidden layer of history. Arvantos had told the top ten that humans were born from Primordials who gave up their bloodline. Now Rose was telling him that the strongest and oldest human forces didn’t come from that same origin at all.
They came from something forbidden, something cursed, something powerful enough to rival Primordials yet dangerous enough that even its name couldn’t be spoken outside the clan.
Max asked, "Does the Primordial Race know about this?"
Rose smiled faintly. "Of course. The Primordial Race and the Four Sacred Clans have known each other’s secrets for a very long time."
"And they still coexist?"

"They don’t have much choice," Rose replied calmly. "The Divine Realm isn’t peaceful enough for its strongest pillars to destroy each other over old origins. Besides, the Primordial Race and the Four Sacred Clans aren’t enemies. Not usually."
"Not usually?" Max repeated.

chapters.title: Chapter 1949: Unknown Reactions!
paragraphs: Rose’s smile turned a little tired. "Ancient relationships get complicated."
Max looked at her for a moment before asking the question that mattered most.
"What’s the problem you needed my help with?"
Rose didn’t answer right away. The hidden world of the Evercrest Clan shimmered behind her, and the deeper spatial fluctuations grew more intense for a brief instant.

Max felt it clearly this time. Somewhere inside the clan, space was being stretched, folded, torn, and sealed all at once. It wasn’t a natural spatial storm. It felt like something trapped was pressing against the clan’s structure from within.
Rose’s expression turned solemn.
"You’ll know soon."
Max looked at her silently.

Rose turned and walked toward the entrance of the Evercrest Clan. As she stepped forward, the folded space opened for her, revealing a path made of emerald light and silver spatial runes. Each step she took made the hidden domain recognize her bloodline, and the path stretched deeper into the sacred territory.
After a few steps, she looked back at Max.
"Come. I’ll take you inside."
Max didn’t hesitate. He followed her.

The moment he crossed the boundary, the outer abandoned planet vanished completely. The endless grass field, the pale sky, and the ordinary wind disappeared behind him as if they’d never existed. In their place, the Evercrest Clan unfolded in full.

The air grew denser. The laws felt older. The spatial layers turned unbelievably complex. Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body immediately picked up on countless hidden passages, sealed regions, folded courtyards, inverted spaces, and secret domains nested inside one another like an endless maze.
This wasn’t just a clan territory. It was a living spatial fortress built across generations by experts who understood space on a terrifying level.

Rose walked ahead of him. The emerald path carried them across a river of floating energy and toward a massive tree whose trunk was wider than a mountain range. Palaces grew from its branches, glowing softly under the light of hanging spirit moons.
Disciples in green, silver, and white robes moved across the bridges between branches, but when they spotted Rose leading a white-haired young man into the clan, their expressions changed.
Some looked curious. Some looked shocked. Some seemed to recognize Max immediately.
"That’s Max Morgan."
"The champion of the Cosmic Ascension Conference?"
"Why did Lady Rose bring him here?"
"Lady Rose? Haha, more like Abandoned Rose..."
"Is Max really the one who beat Revona?"
"He looks younger than I expected."
Whispers spread quietly. Max ignored them, and Rose paid them no attention either.

She kept leading him deeper into the clan, past the beautiful palaces and floating gardens, past the disciples and elders who turned to watch them, and toward the area where the spatial fluctuations were strongest.
The deeper they went, the more serious Max’s expression became. The Evercrest Clan looked beautiful on the surface, but the closer they got to the core region, the clearer the hidden wound became.

Behind the elegant spatial layers, Max could sense a vast sealed region trembling nonstop. Something inside it was unstable. Something powerful. Something tied to the forbidden bloodline Rose had mentioned.
At last, Rose stopped before a massive gate formed from intertwined roots, silver spatial chains, and emerald crystal. The gate was closed. Beyond it, Max could feel a terrifying distortion.
Rose looked at the gate quietly, then said, "Inside this place, you’ll see the bloodline I couldn’t name outside."
Max stood beside her and looked at the sealed gate. His Dimensional Sovereign Body stirred. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline gave off a faint reaction too.
Rose’s voice softened even more.
"And after that, you’ll understand why I needed your help."
The massive gate of intertwined roots, silver spatial chains, and emerald crystal opened without a sound.

Beyond it wasn’t a palace. It wasn’t a battlefield. It wasn’t even a sealed chamber packed with treasures and inheritance stones. It was a vast circular hall hidden beneath the deepest spatial layer of the Evercrest Clan.

The hall was silent, dim, and ancient, its walls made from dark green stone that seemed to breathe softly with the rhythm of space itself. Countless silver chains stretched from the walls into the center of the chamber, not to bind a living being, but to hold the whole space stable around a single statue.
At the center stood the statue of a man. He was tall and calm, with long hair flowing behind him and one hand resting lightly at his side.

His face wasn’t carved with excessive detail, yet every line seemed to hold an indescribable presence. He didn’t look like a tyrant, a king, or a god, but simply like someone who stood before the world without needing to prove anything. His eyes were closed, but even so, Max felt like those stone eyes could open at any moment and look straight through him.
Rose walked a few steps forward and stopped in front of the statue.
"This is him," she said softly.
Max looked at the statue in silence.

Rose continued, "The ancestor of the Four Sacred Clans. Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest all descend from this man. The forbidden bloodline carried by the Four Sacred Clans came from him."
Max didn’t answer, because the moment he saw the statue, something inside him reacted. Violently. His blood surged without warning. Not just one bloodline. Something deeper.

For an instant, Max felt the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline stir. Then the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline trembled. His newly obtained Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline let out a faint pulse, as if it were recognizing and rejecting something at the same time.
Even the hidden depths of his foundation, places that normally stayed silent unless he actively called on them, suddenly shook, as though an ancient echo had woken up inside him.
Max’s fingers moved slightly. He got the reaction under control right away. His expression stayed the same on the outside.
But inwardly, he was shocked.
’What is this?’
He didn’t know this man. He’d never seen this face before. He had no memory of meeting anyone related to him, yet the reaction inside his body was too strong to ignore.

It wasn’t the simple resonance that happens when two powerful bloodlines sense each other. It ran deeper than that, as if something inside Max recognized the statue on an instinctive level, beyond memory.
His blood kept surging. His Dimensional Sovereign Body also reacted faintly, picking up strange spatial traces around the statue that didn’t belong to ordinary space.
His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stayed calm on the surface, but Max could feel a hidden tremor inside it, like a sleeping ancient monarch had just sensed another authority somewhere in the distance.

Still, Max kept it all hidden. Rose stood beside him, and even though she trusted him enough to bring him here, Max had no plans to reveal every strange reaction happening inside his body. He quietly pushed down the turmoil in his blood and kept his gaze steady.

"Is Max really the one who beat Revona?"
"He looks younger than I expected."
Whispers spread quietly.
Max ignored them, and Rose paid them no attention either.

She kept leading him deeper into the clan, past the beautiful palaces and floating gardens, past the disciples and elders who turned to watch them, and toward the area where the spatial fluctuations were strongest.
The deeper they went, the more serious Max’s expression became.
The Evercrest Clan looked beautiful on the surface, but the closer they got to the core region, the clearer the hidden wound became.
Behind the elegant spatial layers, Max could sense a vast sealed region trembling nonstop.
Something inside it was unstable.
Something powerful.
Something tied to the forbidden bloodline Rose had mentioned.
At last, Rose stopped before a massive gate formed from intertwined roots, silver spatial chains, and emerald crystal.
The gate was closed.
Beyond it, Max could feel a terrifying distortion.
Rose looked at the gate quietly, then said, "Inside this place, you’ll see the bloodline I couldn’t name outside."
Max stood beside her and looked at the sealed gate.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body stirred.
His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline gave off a faint reaction too.
Rose’s voice softened even more.
"And after that, you’ll understand why I needed your help."
The massive gate of intertwined roots, silver spatial chains, and emerald crystal opened without a sound.
Beyond it wasn’t a palace.
It wasn’t a battlefield.
It wasn’t even a sealed chamber packed with treasures and inheritance stones.
It was a vast circular hall hidden beneath the deepest spatial layer of the Evercrest Clan.
The hall was silent, dim, and ancient, its walls made from dark green stone that seemed to breathe softly with the rhythm of space itself.
Countless silver chains stretched from the walls into the center of the chamber, not to bind a living being, but to hold the whole space stable around a single statue.
At the center stood the statue of a man.
He was tall and calm, with long hair flowing behind him and one hand resting lightly at his side.
His face wasn’t carved with excessive detail, yet every line seemed to hold an indescribable presence.
He didn’t look like a tyrant, a king, or a god, but simply like someone who stood before the world without needing to prove anything.
His eyes were closed, but even so, Max felt like those stone eyes could open at any moment and look straight through him.
Rose walked a few steps forward and stopped in front of the statue.
"This is him," she said softly.
Max looked at the statue in silence.
Rose continued, "The ancestor of the Four Sacred Clans.
Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest all descend from this man.
The forbidden bloodline carried by the Four Sacred Clans came from him."
Max didn’t answer, because the moment he saw the statue, something inside him reacted.
Violently.
His blood surged without warning.
Not just one bloodline.
Something deeper.
For an instant, Max felt the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline stir.
Then the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline trembled.
His newly obtained Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline let out a faint pulse, as if it were recognizing and rejecting something at the same time.
Even the hidden depths of his foundation, places that normally stayed silent unless he actively called on them, suddenly shook, as though an ancient echo had woken up inside him.
Max’s fingers moved slightly.
He got the reaction under control right away.
His expression stayed the same on the outside.
But inwardly, he was shocked.
’What is this?’
He didn’t know this man.
He’d never seen this face before.
He had no memory of meeting anyone related to him, yet the reaction inside his body was too strong to ignore.
It wasn’t the simple resonance that happens when two powerful bloodlines sense each other.
It ran deeper than that, as if something inside Max recognized the statue on an instinctive level, beyond memory.
His blood kept surging.
His Dimensional Sovereign Body also reacted faintly, picking up strange spatial traces around the statue that didn’t belong to ordinary space.
His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stayed calm on the surface, but Max could feel a hidden tremor inside it, like a sleeping ancient monarch had just sensed another authority somewhere in the distance.
Still, Max kept it all hidden.
Rose stood beside him, and even though she trusted him enough to bring him here, Max had no plans to reveal every strange reaction happening inside his body.
He quietly pushed down the turmoil in his blood and kept his gaze steady.

chapters.title: Chapter 1950: Bloodline Legacy Battle!
paragraphs: Rose didn’t notice anything unusual. Or maybe she did and simply didn’t show it. She looked at the statue with a complicated expression.

"The Four Sacred Clans worship him as the First Progenitor. His name isn’t spoken casually, and his true bloodline is even more restricted. Most people in the Divine Realm only know the Four Sacred Clans as ancient human pillars, but very few know that our bloodline doesn’t come from Primordials like ordinary humans. It comes from him."
Max asked calmly, "And this bloodline is why the Four Sacred Clans can rival the Primordials?"

Rose nodded. "Yes. Anyone who awakens even a trace of the forbidden bloodline becomes different. Their body, soul, laws, and inheritance all change. Every sacred clan carries the bloodline in a different way, and each branch expresses that power differently. Evercrest specializes in space, life, and sealed domains, but that’s only the outer form. The source is still the same forbidden bloodline."
Max looked at the statue again. His blood gave another faint tremor, and he suppressed it once more.
"Then why did you bring me here?"

Rose went quiet for a moment. The question seemed simple, but her expression shifted in a way that made it clear the answer wasn’t easy for her. She looked away from the statue and turned toward one of the silver chains stretching across the hall. The chain shimmered faintly with spatial light, reflecting her face in broken fragments.
"I’m a direct descendant of the Evercrest Clan," she said quietly.
Max looked at her. "I figured as much."
Rose smiled faintly, though there was no real amusement in it. "Direct descendant in blood, but not in value."
Max didn’t interrupt.
Rose continued, "I was born without the forbidden bloodline."
The hall went quiet. The silver chains hummed softly around them.

Rose’s voice stayed calm, but Max could hear the weight underneath it. "In the Evercrest Clan, bloodline decides everything. Talent matters. Cultivation matters. Intelligence matters. But all of that comes after the forbidden bloodline. Those who awaken it get treated as true heirs. Those who don’t get treated as incomplete descendants."
Max’s gaze deepened slightly.

Rose looked at the statue again. "Children born without the forbidden bloodline aren’t allowed to live on the main premises of the Evercrest Clan. Some get sent to branch territories. Some get placed on distant planets. Some get handed minor resources and told to survive on their own. In name, they still belong to Evercrest. In reality, they’re as good as abandoned."
Max remembered where he’d first met her. Planet Orion. A place far from the heart of the Evercrest Clan.
"So that’s why you were living on Orion," Max said.
Rose nodded. "Yes. Of all places, the direct descendant of one of the Four Sacred Clans was living on Planet Orion like someone with no background at all. Sounds ridiculous, doesn’t it?"
Max said calmly, "It sounds like something old clans would do."
Rose glanced at him. For a moment she smiled, and this time there was a trace of real amusement in it.
"You’re not wrong."
Then her expression turned serious again.

"I wasn’t completely abandoned because I had no talent. Even without the forbidden bloodline, my talent was good enough that some elders thought it was a shame. But pity doesn’t change clan rules. Without the bloodline, I had no right to stay in the sacred territory, no right to compete for true inheritance, and no right to be treated as an heir."
Max looked toward the statue. "And now?"
"Now, an opportunity has come up."
Rose turned fully toward him.
"In a few days, the Four Sacred Clans will hold the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
Max raised an eyebrow slightly. "The Four Sacred Clans?"

Rose nodded. "Yes. This isn’t a ceremony held by the Evercrest Clan alone. Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest will all take part. The Bloodline Legacy Battle is one of the few ancient events shared by all four sacred clans, since the forbidden bloodline carried by all four comes from the same source."
Max’s gaze shifted slightly toward the statue at the center of the hall.
"The First Progenitor."

"Yes," Rose said softly. "All four sacred clans descend from him. Even though each clan developed a different branch of the forbidden bloodline, the root is the same. Because of that, the Bloodline Legacy Battle isn’t run by just one clan. It’s held jointly by all four, and every sacred clan sends descendants, heirs, representatives, and challengers to compete for legacy merit."
Max looked at her. "So this is much bigger than an internal Evercrest matter."
"It is," Rose replied. "That’s why I needed someone like you."
Her expression grew more solemn.

"In the Evercrest Clan, a castaway direct descendant like me would normally never get close to the true inheritance. But during the Bloodline Legacy Battle, there’s an old rule left over from the age of the Four Sacred Ancestors.

Any direct descendant of one of the Four Sacred Clans, even one born without the forbidden bloodline, can request one chance to participate through a chosen representative. If that representative wins enough battles and gathers enough legacy merit, the descendant who chose him gets a chance to inherit or awaken the forbidden bloodline."
Max understood the weight of it right away.
"So I won’t only be fighting Evercrest representatives."
Rose nodded. "You may end up fighting representatives from all four sacred clans."
The hall grew quieter.

Rose continued, "Some will be direct heirs of Valerius. Some will come from Ashbourne. Some will represent Ravenhart. Some will belong to Evercrest. And some will be outsiders hired by sacred clan descendants trying to boost their chances. Everyone there will be dangerous, because no one brings a weak representative to the Bloodline Legacy Battle."
Max smiled faintly. "That sounds better."
Rose looked at him with a complicated expression. "Only you would call that better."
"If the stage belongs to all Four Sacred Clans, then winning there matters more."
Rose’s eyes trembled slightly. For her, this wasn’t just a competition. It was her one chance to return to the bloodline that had rejected her since birth.

If Max won enough battles for her, she wouldn’t just gain some resources or status. She’d gain the chance to enter the Bloodline Inheritance Pool shared by the sacred clans, a place where even someone born without the forbidden bloodline might still awaken it.
She looked toward the statue of the First Progenitor.

"The Bloodline Legacy Battle was created because even the Four Sacred Clans couldn’t fully control the forbidden bloodline. Some direct descendants are born with it. Some aren’t. Some awaken it later. Some die without ever touching it. The ancient ancestors left this ceremony behind so that those rejected by birth could still fight for one chance."
Max looked at her. "And you want that chance."
Rose nodded. "Yes. I want that chance."

She turned back to him and said quietly, "When I joined Crown, I told you I’d need your help one day. This is that help. Represent me in the Bloodline Legacy Battle. Win enough battles to gather legacy merit for me. If you do, I can enter the inheritance trial and try to awaken the forbidden bloodline of the Four Sacred Clans."
Max looked at her for a few breaths.
Then he said, "I’ll represent you."
Rose’s expression softened. "Thank you."
Max glanced once more at the statue of the First Progenitor. The strange reaction inside his blood had finally settled, but the mystery hadn’t.
